contract.settlement_definition: Yes if the named starting pitcher is credited with at least N strikeouts in the one listed game (ladder of 'N+' rungs, one market per N). The pitcher must be the game's starting pitcher and face at least one batter; if he is scratched or is not a starter the market pays the fair market price (a settlement at an undefined 'fair market price', not a No and not necessarily a refund at the entry price; see ks_fair_price_definition); relief appearances never count even if the same man enters later. Strikeouts are the official-scorer count for that pitcher (a strike three that is dropped and lets the batter reach still counts for the pitcher). The sampled text is silent on postponement/suspension and names no explicit data source.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is scratched or is not a starting pitcher, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Non-start or scratch is not a No: it settles at an undefined fair market price, so the tradable distribution is conditional on the pitcher starting.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one batter faced the market will settle based on strikeouts recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement trigger is one batter faced (not one out or one pitch), so an opener or an injured starter after one batter settles on a tiny count, which is a real No for any high rung.

rules_evidence.quote: relief appearances will not count towards this market
rules_evidence.establishes: Only the starting appearance counts; a pitcher who relieves is excluded entirely.

rules_evidence.quote: Drew Rasmussen: 9+ strikeouts?
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike construction is an 'N+' (at-least) ladder per pitcher; each rung is a nested event.

variants_and_edge_cases: Opener or bulk-guy usage: an opener who starts and faces 3-4 batters is still 'a starting pitcher with a batter faced', so the market settles No on 5+/6+ rungs rather than voiding; the 'bulk' reliever who follows is excluded by the relief rule.

Settlement asymmetry: a scratch or a non-start settles at the undefined 'fair market price' (a priced settlement value, not a refund at entry and not a No), but an in-game injury after one batter faced settles on whatever count exists, so injury-exit risk is a priced tail, not a void.

Postponement, suspension, rain-shortened games and extra innings are not addressed in the sampled rules_secondary (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS); a rain-shortened start that reaches few innings still settles on the count recorded.
Counting rule: only strikeouts charged to this pitcher count; dropped-third-strike and strikeout-throw-out plays follow official scoring; Postseason games use the same ladder with shorter hooks.

Zero-batter starter is undefined by the sampled text: the rule covers a starter with at least one batter faced and a scratch or non-starter, but not a starter who throws pitches and leaves (injury, ejection, rain) before a batter is faced (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, see ks_zero_batter_starter).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box score / play-by-play strikeouts for the pitcher (MLB Stats API gamefeed or Retrosheet-equivalent). The sampled rules do not name the source, so this is the presumed source of truth.

mechanism.summary: A starter's strikeout total is a compound count: the number of batters he faces times a per-batter strikeout probability that is re-drawn at every plate appearance. Batters faced is itself the outcome of three competing stopping rules: a pitch budget (rehab or season cap), a performance hook (runs and baserunners allowed trigger a pull), and a managerial inning/trip-through-the-order gate. The per-batter probability comes from the pitcher's pitch-type whiff and called-strike skill applied to the specific nine hitters, their handedness, their whiff by pitch type, and the count dynamics (how often a PA reaches two strikes and how often a two-strike PA ends in K). Umpire zone, catcher and park shift it at the margin. The two pieces are negatively coupled through pitch cost (a strikeout takes more pitches than a ground out) and positively coupled through shared latent 'stuff day' quality, so the output is a joint distribution, with rung probabilities set by the right tail of batters faced multiplied by an overdispersed K-per-batter law. Because Kalshi settles non-starts at an undefined fair market price but settles injury exits and openers on the small count, the start-confirmation stage creates a conditional mixture that must be modelled separately from pure performance.

stages.name: Start status and role gate
stages.description: Before anything else the pitcher must be the listed starter. A scratch settles at the undefined 'fair market price', so it changes holders' P&L and is a priced state rather than a state outside the payoff, but an opener or a short-bulk plan means the pitcher starts, faces three or four batters and settles on a tiny count. The gate therefore has three regimes (conventional starter, planned short outing, non-start) and everything downstream is a mixture over regimes weighted by the probability each regime is true at the time the market is traded, which changes when the lineup card and probable-pitcher updates post.
stages.distribution: Discrete 3-regime categorical; regime probabilities move from near-prior (days before) to near 0/1 at lineup posting. Heavy mass at 'conventional' for most rotation starters, rare but extreme opener regime.

stages.name: Batters-faced budget and hook hazard
stages.description: Given a conventional start, the exit point is a first-passage time: each batter faced carries a hazard of removal that depends on cumulative pitch count, trip through the order, runs and baserunners allowed so far, bullpen freshness and the specific manager's policy. The pitch budget (return from injury, workload cap) is a hard ceiling that truncates the right tail. Because K rungs sit in the right tail (8+, 9+, 10+), what matters is not the mean innings but the probability of surviving to 25-30 batters faced.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, truncated discrete (about 12-30 batters faced) with a point mass at the cap and a left tail of early blow-up exits; start-to-start variance larger than rate uncertainty.

stages.name: Per-batter strikeout probability
stages.description: Within a PA the strikeout is a sequence: reach two strikes, then convert a two-strike count with a swing-and-miss, a called third strike or a foul tip. The pitcher's arsenal (usage by count and batter hand, whiff and chase by pitch) meets each batter's whiff and chase profile by pitch type; the odds-ratio combination of two rates is not additive. The confirmed lineup order matters because the nine hitters are not interchangeable and the top of the order is seen more often when the pitcher goes deep. Times-through-the-order decay lowers the rate on trips two and three. Pitcher-side K talent is a posterior: pitch-quality grades and projection systems form the prior (pitcher_k_talent_prior) that observed K% and pitch-type whiff update, with older history discounted after an arsenal change, an injury return or for a debut.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per batter with probability roughly 0.15 to 0.40 depending on matchup; heterogeneity across the nine batters creates a Poisson-binomial rather than a binomial count.

stages.name: Zone regime (ABS challenges), catcher and environment shifts
stages.description: The home-plate umpire's called zone and the catcher's receiving change the share of borderline pitches called strikes, which converts to strike-three-looking events and to count leverage on every PA; cold air and altitude change spin and movement slightly. These shifts are small relative to the matchup but are known only late (umpire and catcher assignments), so they are timing-sensitive adjustments applied on top of s3. Since 2026 MLB uses the ABS challenge system in all regular-season and postseason games (two challenges per team, borderline pitches reviewed by the automated zone), so human-umpire zone and catcher framing history (UmpScorecards, framing runs) comes from a different regime; framing and umpire effects are shrunk harder toward neutral for 2026+ and the challenge-usage and success pattern becomes an input.
stages.distribution: Small multiplicative shift on per-batter K probability (a few percent of rate); effect heterogeneous by pitcher's looking-strikeout share.

stages.name: Count distribution and start-level latent state
stages.description: Realised strikeouts vary more than a binomial with the right mean because pitchers have good and bad days that move whiff rate for all batters at once (grip, command, release), and because K and batters faced are coupled by pitch cost. The settled probability of each rung is the upper tail of this overdispersed, coupled distribution, and neighbouring rungs are nested so a single latent explains the whole ladder.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (Beta-binomial-like) with positive within-start correlation and negative K-vs-BF coupling via pitch cost; fat right tail relative to binomial.

opponent_matchup.note: Confirmed-lineup whiff by pitch and by count.

availability_news.note: Scratches, IL returns and velocity-based fatigue flags.

environment.note: Park and temperature effects on movement.

game_context_script.note: Score-state-triggered pulls and postseason shortening. The hazard curve needs the run state a hook reacts to; the opposing lineup team_wrc_vs_hand and own-bullpen quality supply a non-market run-environment prior.

distribution_variance.note: Overdispersed K count with start-level latent.

settlement_contract.note: One-batter-faced trigger, settlement at the undefined fair market price on a scratch or non-start (see ks_fair_price_definition), relief appearances excluded.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest days and workload enter through the pitch budget and velocity trend already, and no rest-of-season motivation changes a single start's strikeout rate except clinched-team rotation resets, which show up as pitch_count_limit and opener flags rather than as a separate factor.

mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.label: Two-strike putaway decomposition: P(reach 2 strikes) x P(K | 2 strikes) by batter hand
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.mechanism: A strikeout needs two sub-events: the PA reaches a two-strike count, then the pitcher converts. The two pieces are driven by different pitches (first-pitch and early-count strikes versus chase/whiff pitches).
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.rationale: Aggregate K% and CSW hide that a pitcher can have a high K% from elite putaway on few two-strike PAs (fragile to lineup contact skill) or from reaching two strikes constantly (stable). Opposing hitters differ separately on 'gets to two strikes' (takes, fouls) and 'strikes out once there' (whiff on the chase pitch), so the matchup must be applied to each sub-event, not to the end rate.
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.measurement: For each pitcher, 3 seasons of pitch-level data with half-life 120 batters faced: r2 = share of PAs that reach 2 strikes (by batter hand); c2 = K / PAs reaching 2 strikes. For each batter: his own r2_b and c2_b, shrunk to league-by-hand with k = 150 PAs for r2 and k = 120 two-strike PAs for c2. Combine with odds-ratio (log5) per sub-event: logit(r2_match) = logit(r2_p) + logit(r2_b) - logit(r2_league), same for c2; matchup P(K) = r2_match * c2_match. Sum over the confirmed order weighted by expected PA per slot. Units: probability per PA; as-of the lineup-post timestamp using only games dated before the game.
free_sources: Baseball Savant / pybaseball Statcast pitch-level (balls, strikes, events)
raw_data: statcast pitches: pitcher, batter, stand, p_throws, balls, strikes, description, events, game_date, at_bat_number
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.why: Strikeout rungs at 8+ to 10+ are sensitive to which sub-event drives a pitcher's K%, and a lineup of patient fouling hitters is a different test than a lineup of free swingers; this keeps the matchup count-state-aware.

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: The single shared starter exit-hazard model for every pitcher prop and window (strikeouts, outs, earned runs/hits/walks, F5, inherited runners, win credit). Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), third-trip indicator I(b >= 19), inning-boundary indicator I(batter b made the third out of an inning), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket (leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3), days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts; reset when the manager changes), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days); an announced pitch cap from mlb.pitch_count_limit enters as a hard truncation (h = 1 once the cap is reached). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36, E[BF] = sum S(b), and, run inside the PA simulation with outs per batter, the distribution of outs at exit. mlb.sp_workload, mlb.exit_boundary_mass and mlb.leash are readouts or components of this model and are not fitted separately. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.
raw_data: start-level: pitcher, manager, BF, pitches, exit inning/out, runs allowed, runners at exit, score at exit, bullpen usage prior 2 days
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.why: The Kalshi ladder pays on the right tail of strikeouts, and the right tail is exit-time driven; a hazard curve makes the hook policy of this manager and this bullpen state an explicit, testable factor.

mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.label: Start-level dispersion of strikeouts beyond Poisson-binomial (rho parameter)
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.mechanism: Strikeouts across the nine batters share a pitcher-day latent state, so counts are more dispersed than independent Bernoulli draws.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.rationale: The ladder prices neighbouring rungs from one distribution; if the variance is too small the 10+ and 11+ rungs are systematically underpriced and the 4+ rungs overpriced for high-K arms. A per-pitcher (or per-archetype) intra-start correlation parameter is the cheapest way to calibrate the width.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.measurement: From 4 seasons of starts: for each start compute standardized residual of K given modelled expected K per batter faced (Pearson z = (K - sum p_i)/sqrt(sum p_i(1-p_i))). Estimate rho by moment matching: Var(K) = sum p_i(1-p_i) + rho*sum_{i!=j} sqrt(p_i(1-p_i)p_j(1-p_j)); pool pitchers by arsenal cluster (fastball-heavy, breaking-ball-heavy, finesse) and shrink to the pooled value with k = 25 starts. Report rho by cluster and by temperature bucket. As-of: estimated through the prior season, refreshed weekly in-season.
raw_data: start-level K, batters faced, per-batter expected K from the matchup model
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.why: Rungs are nested thresholds on one count; without the dispersion parameter the model cannot price both tails of the ladder consistently.

mlb.battery_assignment.label: Pitcher-catcher battery effect (actual catcher assigned) on K%-over-expected
mlb.battery_assignment.mechanism: The catcher selected for the start changes framing, pitch-calling and blocking; some pitchers have personal catchers.
mlb.battery_assignment.rationale: Existing catcher_framing is a team-season catcher metric; what moves a single start is which catcher is in the lineup card and whether the pitcher is paired with him. Backup catchers have a materially different framing level and often start day games after night games, so it is partly predictable from the schedule.
mlb.battery_assignment.measurement: Output expected framing runs per 1000 called pitches for the game = sum over catchers c of P(c) * framing_c, framing_c = the catcher's Statcast framing runs per 1000 called pitches over the last 2 seasons shrunk to league mean with k = 2000 called pitches. P(c) before lineup post = logistic on the team's catcher start shares over the last 30 team games, consecutive-start count and day-game-after-night-game flag; after lineup post P(c) = 1 for the listed catcher. Convert the difference from the team's season-average catcher into K% points per BF with the league slope of K% on framing runs per 1000 estimated 2021-2025. No separate pitcher-catcher pair term unless shrunk with k = 800 BF to 0. Units: K probability points per BF. As-of: lineup post or earlier projection.
raw_data: catcher framing runs per called pitch (Statcast)
lineup card catcher and team start shares
mlb.battery_assignment.why: A backup catcher can shift the called-strike share enough to move a 7+/8+ rung, and the information arrives with the lineup.

mlb.abs_challenge_regime.label: ABS challenge-system zone regime (2026+): effective zone, challenge availability and success, catcher/batter challenge skill
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.mechanism: With automated ball-strike challenges, a borderline pitch can be overturned to the true zone, so called-strike probability on edge pitches, framing value and umpire zone effects shrink toward the robotic zone and challenge skill matters.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.rationale: Every 2026 regular-season and postseason game (including the sampled Oct 28 2026 game) uses challenges (two per team, successful ones retained, extra challenges in extras), so strikeout-looking events, count leverage and framing value differ from the human-umpire seasons that supply most history; umpire and framing effects estimated on 2021-2025 do not transfer unchanged.
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.measurement: Using 2026+ pitch-level data with challenge events, per battery (pitcher-catcher) and batter: (a) edge_cs = share of pitches within 1.5 inches of the rulebook zone edge that end as called strikes after any overturn; (b) challenge_rate = challenges per 100 edge pitches taken and overturn_rate = overturned/challenges, each shrunk to the league rate with k = 30 challenges; (c) league_shift = league edge_cs 2026-to-date minus 2025 edge_cs at matched counts. Pre-2026 umpire and framing effects are rescaled by r = SD across umpires of edge_cs in 2026 divided by the same SD in 2025, with r = 1 until 100 edge pitches per umpire exist and r regressed to 1 with k = 500 edge pitches. Output: change in edge-pitch called-strike probability and in K% and BB% per PA (probability points, using the league K/BB elasticity to edge_cs fitted 2021-2025). As-of: games completed before the target first pitch.
free_sources: Baseball Savant pitch-level data with ABS challenge fields (assumed present in 2026 exports, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
MLB Stats API gamefeed review events
raw_data: pitch-level plate_x/plate_z, zone edge geometry, call, game_date
challenge events: challenger, outcome, challenges remaining
mlb.abs_challenge_regime.why: Adds the missing 2026+ zone mechanism for strikeout ladders, where called third strikes and count leverage are central.

mlb.pitcher_k_talent_prior.label: Pitcher strikeout-rate prior from pitch-quality grades and projection systems, blended with observed K% by sample size and arsenal-change status
mlb.pitcher_k_talent_prior.mechanism: A pitcher's strikeout ability is fixed by the physical quality of his pitches (velocity, movement, extension, release) long before his observed K% stabilises, so a pitch-quality grade and a projection prior carry the information when observed samples are short or obsolete.
mlb.pitcher_k_talent_prior.rationale: Observed K% needs several hundred batters faced to stabilise, and the 120-BF half-life used for k_rates throws away the history that would help; after an arsenal change (new pitch, velocity jump), an injury return or a debut, the observed rate measures a pitcher who no longer exists. Pitch-shape grades react within one or two starts and projections encode minor-league and aging information, so the prior matters most exactly on the rungs where markets misprice rookies and retooled starters.
mlb.pitcher_k_talent_prior.measurement: prior_K = w * projK + (1 - w) * stuffK, where projK = mean of the latest Steamer and ZiPS K% (rest-of-season if published, else preseason) at the as-of date, and stuffK = league K% + beta * (usage-weighted pitch-model whiff grade - league mean), with the per-pitch whiff grade a logistic model on release speed, induced vertical and horizontal break, spin rate, extension, release height and arm angle, and speed/movement differences to the primary fastball, fitted on 2021-2025 Statcast pitches; beta fitted by regressing pitcher-season K% on the grade (min 150 BF). w = 0.5 by default, 0.3 when the pitcher's last-3-start arsenal differs from his prior season (new pitch type with >= 10% usage or fastball velocity change >= 1.5 mph). Posterior K% = (BF_eff * obsK + 150 * prior_K) / (BF_eff + 150), with BF_eff = BF since the arsenal change at full weight plus earlier BF at weight 0.25; rookies with < 100 MLB BF use projK from MiLB-translated projections. As-of: projections and pitches dated before the game; units K per batter faced.
free_sources: FanGraphs projections (Steamer, ZiPS) and pitch-model leaderboards (Stuff+, Pitching+)
Baseball Savant / pybaseball Statcast pitch-level (release_speed, pfx_x, pfx_z, release_extension, release_pos_z, spin_rate, arm_angle)
raw_data: projection snapshots: pitcher_id, system, K%, BF, publish_date
statcast pitches: pitcher_id, pitch_type, release_speed, pfx_x, pfx_z, release_extension, release_pos_z, release_spin_rate, arm_angle, description, game_date
mlb.pitcher_k_talent_prior.why: Strikeout rungs on rookies, injury returns and pitchers with a new pitch are where k_rates and pitch_type_whiff have the least valid data; this prior supplies talent there and sets the shrinkage target for everyone else.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Core rate input, but the label fuses two objects (pitcher K%/whiff and lineup K%) and the lineup half duplicates lineup_k_platoon; use as pitcher-side talent only.

mlb.pitch_type_whiff.reason: Pitch-by-pitch whiff by batter hand is the actual K generator; needs shrinkage by pitch-type sample (small for sweepers and splitters).

mlb.lineup_whiff_by_pitch.reason: Confirmed-lineup whiff by pitch type converts arsenal into expected Ks; sparse per hitter so must be shrunk to hitter-hand-level whiff.

mlb.lineup_k_platoon.reason: Lineup K% by hand is the low-variance anchor that lineup_whiff_by_pitch is shrunk toward; partially redundant once that exists.

mlb.pitch_mix.reason: Supplies the usage weights multiplied against pitch whiff; by itself says nothing about outcomes, and arsenal changes mid-season matter.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Expected batters faced is the multiplier; but a mean is not enough, the survival distribution is needed (see sp_hook_hazard_curve). Computed as a readout of the shared exit hazard (E[BF] = sum of survival S(b)), never fitted separately.

mlb.leash.reason: Manager hook tendency has no estimand of its own; its content (manager random effect, bullpen freshness, pitch-count and run-state triggers) is a component of the one shared starter exit-hazard model sp_hook_hazard_curve, and the catalog definition of leash is patched to say so.

mlb.pitch_count_limit.reason: Matters only for rehab/return starts or hard innings caps, but there it truncates the right tail sharply; needs an announced-cap field.

mlb.sp_efficiency.reason: Pitches per PA converts the pitch budget to batters faced; high-K profiles are pitch-expensive so it is correlated with k_rates.

mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.reason: Opponent patience raises pitch cost per batter and shortens outings; weak when lineup is unknown.

mlb.tto.reason: Per-trip K decay and hook gate are both visible in the third trip; pitcher-specific decay is more informative than league average.

mlb.umpire.reason: Identity of the umpire and his tendency is the same information that umpire_k_bb_effect already quantifies with adjustment. Pre-2026 umpire-zone history is a different regime from the ABS challenge system (see abs_challenge_regime).

mlb.umpire_k_bb_effect.reason: Adjusted umpire K/BB effect is small but systematic; vintage matters since assignments post late.

mlb.catcher_framing.reason: Framing is a catcher-season measure; the actual-assigned catcher (battery_assignment) is what moves a given start.

mlb.velo_trend.reason: Velocity loss relative to the pitcher's own baseline predicts both lower whiff and earlier exit and flags injury; measured in last 3 starts.

mlb.opener_bulk_flag.reason: Under this contract an opener who faces one batter still settles (no void), so the flag decides whether high rungs are near-certain No; it is a gate, not a secondary factor.

mlb.bullpen.reason: Works only through the hook hazard; keep as an input to sp_hook_hazard_curve rather than a standalone driver.

mlb.park.reason: Park effect on K is modest; mostly altitude and sightlines, and indirectly through run environment and exit risk.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Claimed cold-weather velocity effect is small and untested; only extreme temperature or roof status plausibly matters.

mlb.platoon.reason: Handedness composition of the lineup is the same information as lineup K% by hand once the confirmed order is used.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: A scratch settles at the undefined fair market price rather than on the count, so the value is in pre-lock scratch probability (a priced state), lineup absences and the in-game injury risk of a pitcher returning from the IL.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Rung construction (floor_strike, 'N+' / 'greater' N-0.5, nesting, monotonicity) is contract metadata captured by rules text; only rung prices and cross-rung price consistency are market-derived, and those are benchmarks, not inputs.

m.rules_text.reason: The one-batter-faced settlement trigger and relief exclusion define the conditional population; wording must be versioned.

m.quote_history.reason: Price path after lineup confirmation is a market reaction, not information about the pitcher.

interactions.mechanism: A high-strikeout style raises the number of two-strike pitches and fouls, so the same pitcher who gains Ks per batter also spends more pitches per batter and survives fewer batters. Strikeouts and batters faced are therefore negatively coupled through the pitch budget, and the coupling is strongest against patient lineups that foul off two-strike pitches.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit K and BF jointly (copula or simulation) versus independent product; compare tail calibration of 8+/9+ rungs for high-whiff pitchers against patient lineups.

interactions.mechanism: The contract settles an opener on the small count but settles a scratch at the undefined fair market price, so the distribution is a mixture over three regimes whose weights move with news. The hazard curve differs by regime (about 3-4 batters for an opener versus a normal starter curve), and the mixture weight, not the performance model, dominates high-rung probability whenever opener risk is above a few percent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model log loss on starts flagged opener-risk versus not; test whether adding a regime indicator removes miscalibration at 7+ rungs.

interactions.mechanism: Called strikes contribute only to the looking-strikeout share of a pitcher's Ks, so a wider zone and a better framer help most the pitchers who live on the edges and hurt least those who get strikeouts swinging. Adjustments must be scaled by the pitcher's looking-K share rather than added flat. Under the 2026 ABS challenge regime the zone effect is partially overridden on challenged edge pitches, so the interaction must be estimated with a regime flag and shrunk umpire/framing coefficients.
interactions.how_to_test: Add terms umpire_effect x looking_K_share and framing x edge_pitch_share; check coefficient sign and out-of-sample gain.

interactions.mechanism: On the second and third trips pitchers lean away from their best pitch and hitters have seen it, so the effective whiff rate steps down at batter 19 and 28 while lineup whiff by pitch type changes sign of importance (the offspeed whiff matters more later). The decay is a step at trip boundaries, not smooth in batters faced.
interactions.how_to_test: Include trip-indexed pitch-mix usage and trip dummies; test slope discontinuity at BF 18/27 in per-batter K logistic.

interactions.mechanism: Start-level latent quality widens the K distribution as batters faced grows (variance of a correlated sum scales with BF squared), so on long outings a good day produces 11+ Ks far more often than independence implies. Early velocity relative to baseline is the only pregame-adjacent signal of the latent state.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho by BF bucket and by first-inning velocity deviation (post-hoc check); compare rung calibration with and without the rho term.

interactions.mechanism: The weight on observed whiff and K% versus the pitch-quality prior is a step function of effective sample: it drops when the arsenal changes (old pitches no longer thrown) and rises as new-arsenal batters faced accumulate, so the same observed K% means different things for a stable veteran and a pitcher who added a sweeper three starts ago.
interactions.how_to_test: Backtest K-rung calibration on pitcher-starts within 5 starts of a flagged arsenal change, rookie debuts and IL returns, comparing k_rates alone versus the blended posterior.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped threshold in batters faced: P(K>=k) rises steeply across the BF range where k/K% falls (about 27-33 BF for a 9+ rung at 30% K), nearly zero below 20 BF and saturating above 33
nonlinearities.why: Strikeouts are bounded by batters faced, so rung probabilities are a steep logistic in BF near the rung's requirement and flat elsewhere; linear workload terms mis-price the middle rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Approximate step or steep gradient around the second and third trips (batters 18-19 and 27-28); exact form is uncertain (see ks_shape_constants)
nonlinearities.why: Times-through-the-order penalties and the managerial gate act at trip boundaries; a smooth innings term spreads a discrete change and hides the hook cliff.

nonlinearities.shape: Assumed threshold: little effect for small velocity drops and a sharp negative effect for sustained larger drops; the 1 mph cutoff is an unsourced guess to be estimated
nonlinearities.why: Velocity noise start to start is large; only a sustained multi-start decline separates a sick arm, so a linear velocity term is dominated by noise.

nonlinearities.shape: Odds-ratio (log5-type) combination rather than additive; saturating at extreme pitcher K% against high-whiff lineups
nonlinearities.why: Per-batter K probability combines pitcher and batter propensities multiplicatively on the odds scale, so adding K% differences over-predicts at the extremes.

contract.settlement_definition: KXMLBOUTS (the only live series, now filed in this archetype) pays Yes if the named starting pitcher records at least N outs in the listed game ('15+' rung, floor_strike 14.5 sampled). Gate: 'If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one pitch the market will settle based on outs recorded', i.e. one pitch thrown, not one batter faced as in the strikeout, earned-run and walk ladders. A scratch or non-starter settles at the undefined 'fair market price' (not a refund at entry), and a later relief appearance does not count. Outs are presumed to be the official-scorer outs credited while he is on the mound (thirds of an inning). Postponement, suspension and shortened-game handling are not stated and no data source is named.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one pitch the market will settle based on outs recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The settlement gate is one pitch thrown by a starter, so a first-pitch injury or ejection settles on the outs recorded (usually zero) instead of the fair-price branch.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is scratched or is not a starting pitcher, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Scratch and non-start states settle at an undefined fair market price, a priced settlement state rather than a No.

rules_evidence.quote: relief appearances will not count towards this market
rules_evidence.establishes: Outs recorded in a later relief appearance by the same pitcher are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen has 15+ outs recorded
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike construction is an 'N+' outs rung; the sampled rung is 15+ (five complete innings).

variants_and_edge_cases: Gate difference versus the strikeout ladder: KXMLBOUTS triggers on one pitch thrown (not one batter faced), so a starter injured on his first pitch settles on zero outs (a No for every rung) rather than at the fair market price.

Outs are not innings: partial innings count and outs recorded by double plays, caught-stealing and pickoffs are presumed (box-score convention, not rules text) to count for the pitcher on the mound; only the 15+ rung (floor_strike 14.5) was sampled, so the existence of other rungs is not established.
Rain delay or suspension during the start: the starter may be removed after a long delay and the count freezes; postponement treatment is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS in the sampled text.

Rung construction is an 'N+' ladder (the sampled rung 15+ equals five full innings); if rungs at multiples of three or at 16 and 17 exist (not sampled), boundaries sit where managerial exits cluster, which would make adjacent rungs differ by more than a smooth model implies.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score outs / innings pitched for the starter (MLB Stats API or Retrosheet); presumed, because the KXMLBOUTS text names no source.

mechanism.summary: Outs recorded by a starter is a first-passage quantity: the game removes the pitcher at a stopping time and the count at that time is outs. Each plate appearance produces one out with a probability that is not simply one minus on-base percentage, because ground-ball double plays add a second out on the same batter, and caught stealings and pickoffs add outs without a plate appearance. The stopping time is set by a pitch budget (cap or workload ramp), by pitch cost per out (strikeouts and walks are expensive, early-count ground balls are cheap), by a performance trigger (runs and traffic cause a pull), and by managerial exit conventions that concentrate removals at inning ends and at the start of the third trip through the order. The right tail is bounded by the pitch ceiling divided by pitches per out and the left tail by blow-ups, giving a left-skewed, lumpy distribution on a lattice of thirds of innings. Rung probabilities near multiples of three depend on exit-boundary behaviour as much as on pitcher quality, and rain delays and openers act as regime switches.

stages.name: Starter identity and one-pitch gate
stages.description: The pitcher must be the starter; openers and bulk-guy plans collapse outs to roughly three to six, while a conventional starter is on a 15-21 out scale. Under the KXMLBOUTS wording the gate is one pitch, so an early injury also settles low rather than at the fair market price. The stage therefore yields a regime probability (conventional, opener, bulk-after-opener, non-start) that must be combined with the performance model, and the regime posterior changes at the lineup card and at warm-up reports.
stages.distribution: Categorical with a rare, extreme opener regime; regime posterior is a step function in time around lineup posting.

stages.name: Pitch budget and cost per out
stages.description: The ceiling on outs is the pitch cap divided by pitches per out. Pitches per out equals pitches per plate appearance divided by outs per plate appearance, so a pitcher with good pitches-per-PA but a high on-base rate against may still be pitch-inefficient, and a patient lineup lifts pitches per PA and shortens the outing before performance does. Return-from-injury caps, season innings limits and days of rest set the cap itself, which is often announced rather than inferred.
stages.distribution: Truncated right tail with a point mass at the cap (about 85-110 pitches); pitches per out roughly 5-7, right-skewed by long at-bats.

stages.name: Outs generated per batter and on the bases
stages.description: Outs per batter faced is one minus the rate of reaching base (hits, walks, hit by pitch, reach on error) plus extra outs from double plays and baserunning outs. Strikeouts and ground balls convert at different pitch costs: strikeouts generate an out with certainty only when the batter does not reach on a dropped third strike, ground balls add double-play upside when a runner is on first. The lineup's on-base and double-play proneness and the defense behind the pitcher decide how many outs arrive per hundred pitches.
stages.distribution: Per-batter near-Bernoulli (out probability about 0.68-0.78) with an upside tail from double plays; baserunning outs are rare, independent Poisson-like.

stages.name: Performance trigger and exit-boundary policy
stages.description: A starter is removed when a hook rule fires: a bad inning with runs and runners, the third time through the order, a pitch count threshold, or simply an inning end. Managers differ in whether they let a starter finish an inning, and removals concentrate on inning boundaries and at the first batter of the third trip, so the exit-out distribution has mass spikes at multiples of three. Bullpen freshness and series position (postseason leash) shift the probabilities. The exit lattice is not a second model: exit_boundary_mass is read off the shared sp_hook_hazard_curve (which carries inning-boundary, third-trip, pitch-count and run-state terms with a manager effect), so strikeout, outs and earned-run ladders of the same start stay consistent.
stages.distribution: Lattice-valued exit time with spikes at outs divisible by 3, left tail of blow-up exits, ceiling exits; mixture over managers.

stages.name: Weather and delay interruptions
stages.description: A rain delay of an hour or more ends most starters' nights, so outs freeze at the delay point; heat and humidity affect pitch count tolerance at the margin. The probability of an in-game delay depends on the forecast and roof status, and the removal-after-delay behaviour is a separate manager policy.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete truncation event (delay probability a few percent, higher in rain-prone parks) with near-certain removal conditional on a long delay.

opponent_matchup.note: Patience and contact of the lineup.

pace_volume.note: Pitch budget and cost per out.

officiating_rules.note: 2026 ABS challenges change walks and pitch cost per out; modelled through abs_zone_pitch_cost.

settlement_contract.note: The one-pitch gate, fair-market-price settlement of scratches and the relief exclusion are quoted verbatim from KXMLBOUTS in rules_evidence.

mlb.exit_boundary_mass.label: Exit-outs lattice readout of the shared starter exit hazard: P(removal at outs = j | reached), including the spikes at inning boundaries
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.mechanism: Starter removals cluster at inning boundaries and at the start of the third time through; this lattice is read off the one shared exit-hazard model rather than estimated as a separate model, so outs, strikeout and earned-run ladders of the same start stay consistent.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.rationale: Outs ladders sit on multiples of three; if removals are smooth, P(outs>=15) and P(outs>=16) are priced alike, but if the manager lets starters finish innings then 16-17 outs are rare while 15 and 18 carry mass. Existing leash does not carry this discreteness.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.measurement: Not fitted separately. Simulate the start with mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve (which carries the inning-boundary, third-trip, pitch-count and run-state terms and the manager effect) inside the plate-appearance simulation, mapping batters faced to outs with mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning; record exit_outs in each of 20,000 simulated starts. Output f(j) = share of simulations ending with exactly j outs for j = 0..27, g_j = f(j) / P(outs >= j), and P(outs >= m). Diagnostic only: compare g_j with the manager's empirical exit lattice over the last 4 seasons (cells of pitch-count bucket <85, 85-100, >100 x run-state bucket, shrunk to league with k = 30 starts); persistent gaps are fixed by adding terms to the shared hazard, never by a second model. As-of: games through the previous day.
free_sources: Retrosheet game logs and event files
raw_data: start-level: manager, pitcher, exit_outs, pitches at exit, score at exit, inning, outs, runners
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.why: The ladder is lattice-valued; managers' inning-completion habits decide whether neighbouring rungs are priced near-equal or far apart.

mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.label: Outs per batter faced including double plays and baserunning outs
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.mechanism: Outs are not one per batter: GIDP adds a second out, and caught stealing and pickoffs add outs without a PA.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.rationale: Using one minus OBP per batter understates outs for ground-ball pitchers with a double-play-prone lineup and a runner on first; it also ignores that reach-on-error and fielder's choice change who is out. This is the pitcher-level conversion that links batters faced to outs.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.measurement: Outs per batter faced = sum over PA outcomes o of P(o) x E[outs_on_play | o, base-out state], where outcomes are K, BB, HBP, ground-out, fly/line-out, GIDP (2 outs), fielder's choice (1 out), reach-on-error (0), hit (0). P(o) per matchup via log5 between pitcher rates (2 seasons, half-life 300 BF, shrink k = 250 BF to league by batter hand) and each confirmed batter's rates (shrink k = 200 PA), weighted by expected PA per slot; GIDP uses P(GB) x P(runner on 1B, <2 outs from lineup Markov chain). Add baserunning outs (CS + pickoffs) per BF from the pitcher/catcher/runner model. Units: outs per batter faced. As-of: lineup post, data dated before the game.
raw_data: event-level: batter, pitcher, events, outs_on_play, runners before, game state
catcher pop time, runner sprint speed
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.why: Directly converts the batters-faced distribution into outs; a pitcher with 24 BF and 4 DP outs gets 3 more outs than 'one out per out-batter' implies.

mlb.delay_starter_removal.label: Rain-delay interruption hazard and starter-removal-after-delay rule
mlb.delay_starter_removal.mechanism: A long weather delay usually ends the starter's night; outs are frozen at the delay.
mlb.delay_starter_removal.rationale: Weather appears in the existing catalog only as heat and generic delay; the outs outcome has an explicit truncation that depends on delay length and on whether the manager returns the starter. In rain-prone parks with open roofs the interruption probability is not trivial and shifts the middle rungs.
mlb.delay_starter_removal.measurement: Condition on a delay occurring; P(delay) comes from mlb.delay_risk and is not recomputed. P(starter does not return | delay of L minutes) = logistic(a + b1*I(30<=L<60) + b2*I(L>=60) + b3*starter_pitches_at_delay + b4*innings_completed) with a manager random effect shrunk with k = 15 delays, fitted on 2015-2025 in-game delays (delay timing from game-feed notes, return flag from play-by-play). Output P(starter not returning | delay) and the implied expected starter outs truncation by inning; set to zero for closed-roof games. As-of: lineup post, using upstream delay probability available then.
free_sources: MLB Stats API game status and delay durations
raw_data: in-game delay start/end from game feed notes
starter pitches and innings at delay, return flag
mlb.delay_starter_removal.why: Rain is the one interruption that changes outs without any pitching information.

mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.label: Confirmed opposing batting order out-rate profile: OBP, strikeout, ground-ball double-play and speed by slot against the starter's hand
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.mechanism: Outs per batter faced depend on the nine specific hitters: on-base skill lowers outs per PA, strikeouts and grounders into double plays raise them.
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.rationale: The outs ladder converts batters faced into outs; a lineup of high-OBP, low-GIDP hitters can cost two or three outs over a start relative to a free-swinging lineup, and the order of the hitters changes who bats with runners on. The lineup posts a few hours before first pitch, so the input has a vintage problem.
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.measurement: For each of the nine confirmed slots take projected out probability per PA = 1 - OBP_proj(vs starter hand) + GIDP_rate x P(runner on first with <2 outs) (ZiPS/Steamer shrunk to 2-season stats with k = 300 PA), weighted by expected PA through the starter's modelled batters faced (slot PA weights 4.65 down to 3.85 per game, truncated to the starter's expected BF). Output: expected outs per batter faced for the lineup (about 0.68-0.72 league) and its deviation from league; units outs per BF. As-of: lineup post; before it, a mixture over the team's usual orders.
raw_data: PA events with outs_on_play and base state
mlb.opposing_lineup_out_rate_profile.why: Supplies the opposing-offence driver of outs per batter faced, which the pitcher-only inputs lacked.

mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.label: ABS-regime effect on pitches per plate appearance and walk rate (2026+)
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.mechanism: Under automated ball-strike challenges the called zone on borderline pitches is more consistent, shifting walks, called strikes and therefore pitch cost per out relative to the human-umpire seasons that supply history.
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.rationale: Pitches per PA is a history-based average and cannot contain the day's zone regime; all 2026 games use ABS challenges, which changes walks and called strikes. The pitch budget that caps outs depends on pitches per out, so an unmodelled regime shift mis-states the ceiling.
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.measurement: From 2026 pitch-level data compute league and pitcher-level changes versus 2025 in (a) pitches per PA, (b) BB rate, (c) called-strike share of borderline pitches, with shrinkage of the pitcher-level shift toward the league shift using k = 150 PA; apply the shift to pre-2026 pitches-per-PA priors. Units: pitches per PA and walk probability. As-of: through prior games; 2026 sample builds over the season.
raw_data: pitch-level location, call, count and PA outcome by season
mlb.abs_zone_pitch_cost.why: Replaces the circular claim that the zone effect is already inside pitches per PA by modelling the 2026 regime shift explicitly.

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: The single shared starter exit-hazard model for every pitcher prop and window (strikeouts, outs, earned runs/hits/walks, F5, inherited runners, win credit). Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), third-trip indicator I(b >= 19), inning-boundary indicator I(batter b made the third out of an inning), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket (leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3), days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts; reset when the manager changes), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days); an announced pitch cap from mlb.pitch_count_limit enters as a hard truncation (h = 1 once the cap is reached). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36, E[BF] = sum S(b), and, run inside the PA simulation with outs per batter, the distribution of outs at exit. mlb.sp_workload, mlb.exit_boundary_mass and mlb.leash are readouts or components of this model and are not fitted separately. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.
raw_data: start-level: pitcher, manager, BF, pitches, exit inning/out, runs allowed, runners at exit, score at exit, bullpen usage prior 2 days
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.why: Outs recorded are a first-passage time of the starter's removal; the shared hazard model (same object as for strikeouts and earned runs) carries the inning-boundary and run-state terms whose outs lattice is exit_boundary_mass.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Mean batters faced is the base; needs the whole survival distribution, not just the mean, because rungs are thresholds. Computed as a readout of the shared exit hazard (E[BF] = sum of survival S(b)), never fitted separately.

mlb.leash.reason: Manager hook tendency has no estimand of its own; its content (manager random effect, bullpen freshness, pitch-count and run-state triggers) is a component of the one shared starter exit-hazard model sp_hook_hazard_curve, and the catalog definition of leash is patched to say so.

mlb.pitch_count_limit.reason: A regime gate that binds only on limited-return or capped starts and is irrelevant for uncapped starters, so it is secondary with an announced-cap data field rather than a primary continuous input.

mlb.sp_efficiency.reason: Pitches per PA and first-pitch strike set cost; must be converted to pitches per out, not left as per-PA.

mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.reason: Opponent patience raises pitch cost; effect size is second-order versus pitcher efficiency and lineup is unknown until the card posts.

mlb.sp_quality.reason: Run-prevention quality predicts blow-up exits but is a weak driver of the lattice; its use should be conditional on the hook model.

mlb.contact_defense.reason: Contact quality and defense determine hit-driven baserunners, which both reduce outs per BF and trigger pulls.

mlb.plate_discipline.reason: Walks are pitch-expensive non-outs; command matters for both outs per BF and pitches per out.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Strikeouts are certain outs but pitch-expensive; high K% cuts both ways, so the net effect is conditional on pitch cap.

mlb.tto.reason: The third-trip penalty and pull gate matter, but the effect is best captured as a boundary in exit_boundary_mass.

mlb.velo_trend.reason: Velocity loss is an early-exit and injury flag; sample is short and noisy, use as a threshold.

mlb.sp_rest_days.reason: Rest and prior-start pitch count set stamina and the cap; weak on its own for standard five-day starters.

mlb.bullpen.reason: Freshness lengthens or shortens the leash; effect is through the hook hazard and is second-order.

mlb.opener_bulk_flag.reason: Opener/bulk plan gates the whole distribution; one pitch is enough to settle low, so the flag is the first term.

mlb.postseason_leverage_usage.reason: Postseason leash is demonstrably shorter and ladders in October need that regime; no regular-season data for it.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Heat effect on stamina is asserted, not measured; the actionable weather piece is rain-delay truncation (delay_starter_removal).

mlb.park.reason: Run environment affects blow-up risk modestly; large only at extreme parks.

m.rules_text.reason: Gate (pitch thrown vs batter faced), partial-inning handling and postponement text decide which population is priced; must be versioned and compared with the strikeout ladder.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Nested-rung consistency is a market-derived diagnostic and not information about the pitcher.

interactions.mechanism: The outs ceiling equals the pitch cap divided by pitches per out, so for capped starters (rehab, innings limit) the cap is binding and the opponent's patience determines which rung the ceiling falls on; for uncapped starters the cap never binds and patience only matters through the performance hook. The effect is a regime switch on whether cap/(pitches per out) falls below the rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute cap-implied outs ceiling per start and compare tail calibration for capped versus uncapped starts.

interactions.mechanism: Managers who pull at the start of the third trip remove starters at outs 18 and nearly never at 19-20, while fresh bullpens raise the probability a hook is pulled at the boundary. The rung P(outs>=19) therefore depends on the boundary decision rather than on running performance, and the dependence is on the bullpen state in discrete steps.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate exit mass at j=18 by bullpen-freshness tercile and by manager; check discontinuity of P(outs>=18) vs P(outs>=19).

interactions.mechanism: Early runs convert contact allowed into a pull: a starter with weak contact suppression who allows a first-inning crooked number is removed early, so the same quality gap shows up as a left-tail mass rather than a shift of the mean. The hook response is conditional on runs allowed to date, not on pregame quality alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit hazard with runs-allowed interaction by pitcher contact-quality tercile on historical starts; compare predicted P(outs<=9) to observed.

interactions.mechanism: Ground-ball pitchers earn extra outs by double plays when a runner is on first, but only in lineups that put runners on and hit grounders; strikeout pitchers earn no DP outs. Outs per BF is therefore a product of GB share, traffic on first and lineup DP rate rather than an additive pitcher quality term.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare outs-per-BF prediction with and without the GB x traffic x DP-rate term on held-out starts.

interactions.mechanism: A weather delay matters only when the roof is open and rain overlaps the middle innings; given a delay over an hour the starter usually does not return, so the effect on outs is conditional on both timing and length, truncating the right tail only in wet parks.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition outs distribution on delayed-game flag in historical data by park roof type; estimate fraction of delayed games where the starter returns.

interactions.mechanism: Outs recorded are pitch budget divided by pitches per out, and pitches per out is pitches per PA divided by outs per PA: a lineup with low out rate raises pitches per out and pulls the pitch ceiling down, so lineup out-rate and pitch efficiency multiply through the cap rather than adding.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress outs recorded on pitch budget / (pitches per PA / lineup outs per PA) and compare with additive terms across starts with announced caps.

nonlinearities.shape: Hard ceiling: probability mass piled at cap/pitches-per-out, none above
nonlinearities.why: A cap truncates outs sharply; a linear effect of the cap smears out a point mass and mis-prices the rung that sits exactly at the ceiling.

nonlinearities.shape: Lumpy lattice: spikes at multiples of three outs (inning ends) and at third-trip start
nonlinearities.why: Removals cluster at inning boundaries, so the survival function falls in steps; a smooth hazard in outs gives the wrong rung spacing.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex cost: pitches per PA above about 4.2 compounds through full counts and long at-bats, shortening outings disproportionately
nonlinearities.why: A few high-leverage two-strike battles make pitch spending right-skewed, so average pitches per PA understates the probability of a high-pitch-count outing.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at sustained multi-start decline; flat inside normal start-to-start noise
nonlinearities.why: Only a decline outside noise predicts injury or fatigue exits; before that velocity is uninformative about outs.
