contract.settlement_definition: Three starter ladders now filed here, all with sampled rules: KXMLBERA (earned runs), KXMLBWA (walks allowed) and KXMLBHA (hits allowed) pay Yes if the named starter 'records N+' of the stat in the listed game. All three use the same gate: a starter with 'at least one batter faced' settles on the recorded count; a scratch or non-starter settles at the undefined 'fair market price'; relief appearances are excluded. Only one rung per ladder was sampled (4+ ER, 3+ BB, 6+ H). Official-scoring conventions (earned versus unearned runs, inherited runners charged to the starter, intentional walks counted, hit versus error) are presumed scoring convention, not Kalshi text. Postponement, scorer changes and the data source are not stated.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one batter faced the market will settle based on earned runs recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The ER ladder settles on official earned runs once the starter has faced one batter.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one batter faced the market will settle based on walks allowed recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The walks ladder uses the same one-batter-faced gate.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one batter faced the market will settle based on hits allowed recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: The hits-allowed ladder (previously thought title-only) has the same one-batter-faced gate.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is scratched or is not a starting pitcher, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Scratches and non-starts settle at an undefined fair market price across the three ladders.

variants_and_edge_cases: Earned vs unearned: a run scored after an error or passed ball that would have ended the inning is unearned and does not count; the scorer reconstructs the inning without the error, so a team's error and passed-ball rate is a direct driver of how many runs count for ER rungs.
Inherited runners: runs charged to the starter after he is removed (runners he left on base) count for him, making bullpen quality a driver of his earned runs after exit.
Hits and errors boundary is an official scorer decision and can be changed after the game; walks count intentional walks, not hit-by-pitch.

Starter gate is one batter faced in the sampled KXMLBERA, KXMLBWA and KXMLBHA text. A starter who throws pitches but leaves before facing a batter is undefined by the text (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, see erhw_zero_batter_starter), so claims that an opener or immediate injury 'settles on tiny counts' are presumptions.
Earned-run, inherited-runner, intentional-walk and hit/error conventions are the official scorer's rules and are assumed here, not stated in the Kalshi text.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score statistics (earned runs, hits, walks allowed) for the starter from MLB Stats API or Retrosheet; presumed, since none of the three sampled texts names a source or a post-game scoring-change policy.

mechanism.summary: Hits, walks and earned runs allowed by a starter are three linked counts generated by the same sequence of batters faced but with different branching structure. Batters faced is truncated by the hook. Each batter ends in a strikeout, a walk or hit-by-pitch, a ball in play, or a home run. Walks come from command against plate discipline and the called zone; hits come from balls in play multiplied by hit probability set by contact quality, defense, park and luck; earned runs are a downstream function of how baserunners are sequenced by extra-base hits and home runs, how many are stranded, how many runs are charged as unearned, and how many inherited runners the bullpen lets score after exit. The three counts share latent command and contact quality, so they are positively correlated, and they are negatively correlated with outs and strikeouts. Because earned runs truncate the outing (a blow-up ends it), the ER distribution is a mixture of normal outings and early-exit blow-ups with a heavy right tail only partly capped. Hits and walks are close to compound-binomial in batters faced, while earned runs need base-out state.

stages.name: Gate and exposure
stages.description: The starter must have faced a batter. Exposure is batters faced from the hook process, the same stopping-time logic that governs outs but here with an asymmetry: runs allowed accelerate the pull, so the number of batters faced is endogenous to the counts being predicted, which truncates the ER tail and the hits tail in blow-up games. Exposure comes from the shared starter exit hazard (sp_hook_hazard_curve) evaluated inside the PA simulation, so runs allowed shorten the outing endogenously instead of using a fixed batters-faced mean.
stages.distribution: Truncated discrete exposure correlated with the outcomes themselves.

stages.name: Plate-appearance outcome split
stages.description: For each batter the outcome is a multinomial among strikeout, walk or HBP, ball in play, and home run. Strikeout and walk rates come from the pitcher's strike-throwing and the lineup's chase and patience; the batted-ball mix (ground, line, fly) is set by pitcher profile and hitters' swing. Each branch uses an odds-ratio combination of pitcher and batter skill, then is adjusted for platoon, park, umpire and catcher receiving.
stages.distribution: Multinomial per batter; heterogeneity across the lineup makes counts Poisson-binomial; HBP is rare.

stages.name: Balls in play to hits
stages.description: Hits equal balls in play times the probability a ball in play is a hit, which depends on exit velocity and angle mix (expected batting average on contact), defense and positioning, park dimensions and surface, and luck that regresses. High-strikeout pitchers face fewer balls in play, so hits are mechanically coupled to strikeouts and walks through the balls-in-play count. The official scorer's hit-versus-error call is the final filter.
stages.distribution: Binomial in balls in play with overdispersion from batted-ball quality clustering; scorer discretion adds a small noise term.

stages.name: Baserunner sequencing to earned runs
stages.description: Runs depend on the base-out states hits and walks create, on extra-base hits and home runs that advance runners, and on stranding. Home runs score the batter plus every runner, so traffic multiplies HR cost; errors and passed balls produce unearned runs that are not charged. Inherited runners left by the starter add charged runs after exit. A base-out run-expectancy conversion of baserunners is a better predictor than LOB% regression.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed count with zero mass (about 35-40% of starts allow 0-1 ER) and a heavy right tail from HR plus traffic; truncated by the hook.

stages.name: Joint distribution across the three ladders
stages.description: The three counts share start-level latent command (pitch location, release) and contact quality, so they are correlated within a start, while rungs within each ladder are nested events of one count. Pricing consistency across H, BB and ER ladders requires the joint distribution, not three independent marginals, and plate-appearance simulation generates it naturally.
stages.distribution: Positively correlated overdispersed counts (H, BB, ER) with negative correlation to K and outs; copula-like dependence.

talent_strength.note: Pitcher talent on K, BB and batted ball mix.

opponent_matchup.note: Lineup quality and patience by hand.

efficiency_conversion.note: BIP to hits, hits to runs.

distribution_variance.note: Joint distribution engine (a method) for the three ladders; contact_dist is the wrong object for pitcher counts and is not claimed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: A single regular-season start's walk/hit/earned-run counts are not changed by standings or rest incentives beyond pitch limits already in workload; postseason and clinched-team lineups enter through lineup_pit and workload rather than as a separate motivation factor.

mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.label: Run-expectancy conversion of baserunners (RE24-allowed by base-out state, pitcher profile)
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.mechanism: Earned runs equal the sum of run-value increments across base-out states; HR and extra-base hits convert traffic to runs.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.rationale: LOB% regression treats strand rate as luck, but strand rate partly reflects pitcher skill (K and GB with runners on) and HR timing. A direct PA-level run-expectancy accounting separates how many baserunners a pitcher allows from how many each is worth.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.measurement: For each pitcher, estimate PA outcome probabilities (K, BB/HBP, GB-DP, HR, other) separately in 8 groups (bases empty, then runners on with 0, 1, 2 outs for runner on 1B only vs scoring position) over the last 2 seasons with 400-BF half-life weights, shrunk to the league group rate with k = 250 BF in that group. Expected earned runs for the target game = Markov-chain simulation (10,000 games) over the confirmed batting order using these state-dependent pitcher outcomes combined by log5 with batter rates and the park, minus the unearned share from mlb.er_ur_scoring_split; also report RE24 allowed per PA by group (RE24 after minus before plus runs on play, season league matrices). Units: expected runs charged to the starter over his expected batters faced. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Statcast events with runners on base and outs
raw_data: event-level: base-out state before, event, runs on play, batter, pitcher, park
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.why: Provides the conversion from hits and walks ladders to the earned-runs ladder without relying on a regressed LOB% alone.

mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.label: Expected unearned-run share (team errors, passed balls, catcher and infield error rates)
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.mechanism: Runs after an error or passed ball that extends an inning can be unearned and are not counted.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.rationale: Earned runs are what the contract pays on; runs can differ. Teams with poor infield defense or a passed-ball-prone catcher have a larger gap, and an error that extends an inning raises the number of batters faced and baserunners without adding earned runs.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.measurement: Team factor f_team = u_team/u_league, where u_team = unearned runs per game over the last 2 seasons with half-life 60 games shrunk to league with k = 40 games. Pitcher factor f_p = (pitcher unearned share over 3 seasons shrunk to league with k = 300 BF)/league share. Fielder factor f_def = sum over confirmed fielders of error rate per chance (shrunk to league with k = 400 chances) relative to league, weighted by position error-opportunity shares; catcher factor f_c = (passed balls + wild pitches per 100 innings, shrunk with k = 600 innings)/league. unearned_share = league_share * (f_team * f_p * f_def * f_c)^(1/2) clipped to [0.5, 2] x league_share. Expected ER = expected runs * (1 - unearned_share). Units: fraction of runs. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Retrosheet / Baseball-Reference fielding and error data
raw_data: team-game: runs, earned runs, errors, passed balls
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.why: Earned runs ladder differs from the runs distribution by this share; rungs at 3+ and 4+ move materially on a bad defense. Category reflects a fielding/defence quantity (errors and passed balls) rather than an official judgement, though the earned/unearned split is an official-scorer rule.

mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.label: Inherited-runner charge risk after starter exit (expected extra earned runs)
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.mechanism: A starter is charged for runners left on base when relieved, so the bullpen strand rate determines part of his earned runs.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.rationale: The starter's earned-run count is not finished when he leaves: if he leaves with traffic and the reliever allows them to score, those runs are his. Exit-with-traffic probability is high in blow-up outings, the same outings that populate the right tail of the ER ladder.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.measurement: P(exit with k runners) from the shared exit hazard mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve evaluated inside the PA simulation x P(each inherited runner scores | reliever profile) with reliever strand rate shrunk to league (k = 60 BF with inherited runners). Expected extra ER = sum_k P(k) x k x p_score x (1-unearned share). Use the likely first reliever from bullpen availability (setup man or long man). Units: expected earned runs added. As-of: lineup post + bullpen usage from prior 2 days.
raw_data: relief-appearance level: inherited runners, inherited scored, reliever, team, game state
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.why: Needed for the ER tail rungs where blow-ups leave a crowded base path.

mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.label: Scorer hit/error tendency by park (borderline play calls)
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.mechanism: Hits depend on official scorer rulings at the hit/error margin.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.rationale: In some parks the scorer rules more plays errors than average, converting would-be hits into unearned reached-base events; changes made after the game may alter settlement values.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.measurement: Per home park over the last 3 seasons: for balls in play with expected hit probability (Statcast xBA bucket, deciles) between 0.2 and 0.8, compute error rate = field_error / (hits + field_error) in each bucket, pooled across buckets with weights equal to league bucket frequency; shrink the park rate toward the league rate with k = 200 qualifying plays; shift = park error rate minus league error rate (probability points). Exclude plays whose ruling was later changed from the first-published value only if the first-published value is the settlement source. Scorer identity is not used. Units: probability shift in hit per contact bucket. As-of: through the prior game.
raw_data: Statcast batted balls with events (hit vs field_error), xBA or exit velocity/launch/sprint bucket, park
MLB Stats API scoring change records
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.why: Hits allowed is a scorer-decided count; tendencies shift rungs slightly and can flip close settlements.

mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.label: ABS-regime effect on walk and run-scoring probability (2026+): borderline-pitch call share and challenge outcomes
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.mechanism: Walks come from called balls and strikes; automated challenges on borderline pitches change the called-strike share and the value of framing and umpire zones relative to human-umpire history.
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.rationale: Every 2026 game uses ABS challenges, so the walks ladder and the baserunner volume feeding earned runs depend on a zone regime for which UmpScorecards and catcher-framing history are only a prior; the convex walk response to the called-strike share makes small regime shifts matter at the 3+ walks rung.
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.measurement: From 2026 pitch-level data estimate the league and pitcher-battery change versus 2025 in BB rate on borderline-pitch counts: delta_BB = BB%_2026 - BB%_2025 at matched count and zone-edge mix, shrunk toward the league delta with k = 150 PA per pitcher. Rescale pre-2026 umpire and framing coefficients by the ratio of 2026 to 2025 edge-pitch called-strike spread. Units: walk probability per PA. As-of: through prior games.
free_sources: MLB Stats API gamefeed review events
mlb.abs_zone_walk_effect.why: Adds the missing 2026 zone-regime driver to the walks ladder and to baserunner volume for ER.

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: The single shared starter exit-hazard model for every pitcher prop and window (strikeouts, outs, earned runs/hits/walks, F5, inherited runners, win credit). Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), third-trip indicator I(b >= 19), inning-boundary indicator I(batter b made the third out of an inning), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket (leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3), days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts; reset when the manager changes), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days); an announced pitch cap from mlb.pitch_count_limit enters as a hard truncation (h = 1 once the cap is reached). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36, E[BF] = sum S(b), and, run inside the PA simulation with outs per batter, the distribution of outs at exit. mlb.sp_workload, mlb.exit_boundary_mass and mlb.leash are readouts or components of this model and are not fitted separately. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.
raw_data: start-level: pitcher, manager, BF, pitches, exit inning/out, runs allowed, runners at exit, score at exit, bullpen usage prior 2 days
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.why: Batters faced multiplies all three ladders and runs allowed accelerate removal; the shared hazard model with its runs-allowed term gives the BF distribution and the exit states used for inherited-runner charges.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Batters faced multiplies all three ladders; needs the hook-conditional distribution since runs allowed accelerate exits. Computed as a readout of the shared exit hazard (E[BF] = sum of survival S(b)), never fitted separately.

mlb.leash.reason: Manager hook tendency has no estimand of its own; its content (manager random effect, bullpen freshness, pitch-count and run-state triggers) is a component of the one shared starter exit-hazard model sp_hook_hazard_curve, and the catalog definition of leash is patched to say so.

mlb.contact_defense.reason: Hits depend on contact quality and defense; primary for the hits ladder, secondary for walks (none). Primary for the hits ladder only; not a walks driver.

mlb.plate_discipline.reason: Walk driver on both sides (command vs chase/patience); only real input to the walks ladder besides zone. Primary for the walks ladder only.

mlb.team_wrc_vs_hand.reason: Team-level wRC+ is a coarse summary of the confirmed nine and a lineup-specific PA-level matchup replaces it, so it is not a staged input once the card is posted.

mlb.lineup_pit.reason: The confirmed order defines the hitters actually faced; vintage and platoon-driven scratches matter.

mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.reason: HR/FB and barrels allowed drive the heavy tail of earned runs because HR scores traffic. Primary for the ER ladder only.

mlb.babip_luck.reason: Regress BABIP to expected for hits, but regression target must be contact quality and defense, not league average.

mlb.lob_strand_luck.reason: Strand regression is useful but crude; run-expectancy conversion by base-out state is a better estimator of the same thing.

mlb.umpire.reason: Zone size shifts walks; small effect and only known late.

mlb.catcher_framing.reason: Framing affects walks and strikeouts by called strikes; catcher assignment known only at lineup post.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Strikeouts remove balls in play and baserunner chances; correlation with hits and ER is mechanical.

mlb.pitcher_gb_rate.reason: Ground-ball share lowers extra-base hits and HR; matters for ER tail and double plays.

mlb.defense.reason: Label bundles team OAA and catcher framing; the OAA part is defense behind the pitcher and belongs in contact_defense, and the catcher part duplicates catcher_framing.

mlb.park.reason: Hit and HR factors by hand; matter in extreme parks.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Wind out and heat raise HR; effect is already partly in park norms.

mlb.bullpen.reason: Matters via inherited runners and the exit point; use as input to inherited_runner_charge_risk.

m.rules_text.reason: Earned-run definition, relief exclusion and starter gate are settlement-critical and must be read per ladder.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Price monotonicity across rungs is market-derived and only a consistency check.

mlb.pa_sim.reason: A simulation engine, not an input; kept as the method for the joint distribution across ladders.

mlb.contact_dist.reason: Defined as hitter hit/TB/RBI count distributions given PA, which is the wrong object for pitcher counts; the pitcher analogue (BIP-conditional hits) is not defined.

interactions.mechanism: Hits equal balls in play times hit probability, and balls in play are batters faced minus strikeouts, walks and home runs. A high-strikeout pitcher therefore has lower exposure to BABIP luck and a pitcher with a high BABIP-against can still be low on hits if he strikes batters out, so the effect of contact quality is scaled by the share of PAs that reach play.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress hits on BIP count and BABIP-expected separately versus on batters faced; check which has lower residual overdispersion.

interactions.mechanism: Walk probability per PA rises convexly with the number of borderline balls called, because full counts compound: a smaller called zone and a poor framer push more counts to 3-ball, and each added ball increases the chance of a walk non-linearly. Command-poor pitchers against patient lineups are most exposed. In 2026 the zone is partly overridden by ABS challenges, so umpire and framing coefficients are estimated with a regime flag.
interactions.how_to_test: Add zone-size x pitcher edge rate x lineup chase interaction in a count-level walk model; test convexity in the zone-size term.

interactions.mechanism: A home run costs one run plus the number of runners aboard, so expected earned runs from HR vulnerability grows convexly with traffic; HR-friendly parks and wind raise the probability that traffic is cleared. The ER ladder at 4+ is dominated by this joint of traffic and HR, not by average HR rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute expected ER from base-out Markov with HR probability by state versus flat HR/9; compare calibration of 4+ ER rung.

interactions.mechanism: If the starter is pulled with runners on base, part of his final earned runs depends on which reliever enters and how fresh the bullpen is. The hook and the bullpen jointly create a conditional addition to ER that is largest in exactly the outings that already ended badly.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition ER residual on exit-with-traffic flag and reliever quality tercile; estimate added runs per inherited runner.

interactions.mechanism: When an error or passed ball extends an inning, the scorer reconstructs the inning and later runs become unearned, so ER switches regime from tracking runs to lagging them. Teams with weak infield defense or a passed-ball catcher spend more time in the second regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model fit predicting ER vs predicting runs and applying team-level unearned share; test whether team error rate improves ER calibration.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in batters faced for ER and hits rungs (4+ ER nearly impossible under about 15 BF, hits 7+ needs about 24+ BF)
nonlinearities.why: Counts of hits and runs are bounded by exposure; rung probabilities are steep logistic functions of batters faced near the rung requirement.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex: HR rate effect on ER grows with traffic (ER gain per extra HR is not constant)
nonlinearities.why: A home run is worth more with runners aboard, so HR tendency interacts with baserunner volume and the ER ladder's right tail steepens.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in zone rate (cutoff near 42 percent is an unsourced author guess to be estimated); ABS regime shifts the curve
nonlinearities.why: Count leverage compounds through three-ball counts, so a small drop in strike rate produces an accelerating increase in walks.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating regression: extreme LOB% deviations (>80% or <65%) revert more than linear
nonlinearities.why: Strand luck is bounded by baserunner volume and pitcher skill; extremes carry less persistent information than a linear coefficient implies.

fields: post_bat_score (runs on play derived from the difference; no direct runs_scored_on_play column)

required_data.fields: team, errors, unearned runs, passed balls, catcher, relief inherited runners and runs, fielding OAA
required_data.timestamp_requirement: As-of prior game; bullpen availability from prior 2 days.

required_data.dataset: Starter start log and lineup card
required_data.fields: game_pk, pitcher_id, batters_faced, exit state, lineup order with handedness
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Announcement timestamps for lineup card.

contract.settlement_definition: Yes if the named batter, who must be in the official starting lineup and record at least one plate appearance, finishes the listed game with at least N hits (KXMLBHIT), N total bases (KXMLBTB, singles=1 to home runs=4) or N hits plus runs plus RBIs (KXMLBHRR). A scratch, a bench start, or a starter with no plate appearance pays the fair market price; a player who enters later as a pinch hitter or substitute also settles at the fair market price, and pinch-hit at-bats do not count. So the priced population is 'starts and bats at least once'. Postponement, suspension and rain-shortened handling are not stated in the sampled text; the source of truth is presumably the official box score.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick starts the game but does not record a plate appearance, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: A starter with zero PA settles at the fair market price, not a No, so the settled population requires at least one PA.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick is in the starting lineup and records at least one plate appearance the market will settle based on total bases recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Total bases ladder settles on official total bases once the starter has batted.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick records 5+ total hits + runs + rbis in the Milwaukee vs Tampa Bay professional baseball game originally scheduled for Oct 28, 2026 at 8:00 PM EDT
rules_evidence.establishes: Combo threshold counts the sum of hits, runs scored and RBIs (overlapping events) for the listed game.

rules_evidence.quote: pinch hit at bats will not count towards the market
rules_evidence.establishes: Substitutes entering after the lineup card settle at the fair market price and their at-bats are excluded.

variants_and_edge_cases: Hits, total bases and hits+runs+RBIs are three ladders on one set of plate-appearance outcomes; a home run adds 1 hit, 4 total bases and at least 3 H+R+RBI points (hit, run, RBI) so the ladders are overlapping, not independent.

Extra innings add plate appearances and, with the automatic runner, runs and RBI chances; a hitter whose PA count differs from the slot expectation because the game goes long is a settlement-relevant tail.

Population is conditional on start and at least one PA; because a late scratch settles at the undefined fair market price rather than on the count, the model can condition on the confirmed lineup but price risk is the in-game removal that reduces PA without voiding.
The hits-allowed, All-Star Game hits and Derby longest-HR series once filed here were moved by the reconciliation; all three remaining series use the batter start-plus-one-PA gate.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box score (hits, total bases, runs, RBIs) for the player; presumed MLB Stats API; sampled rules do not name the source.

mechanism.summary: A hitter's hits, total bases or hits-plus-runs-plus-RBI are sums over his plate appearances of an outcome that has a multinomial structure: out, walk, single, double, triple, home run. The mean is therefore the number of plate appearances times the per-PA outcome probabilities and the variance is compound. Plate appearances come from lineup slot, the game's total run environment, extra innings and the chance the hitter is removed early (pinch hitter, defensive replacement, blowout rest). Per-PA outcome probabilities come from contact quality and handedness-specific skill met by the starter's arsenal for the first two or three PAs and by relievers (often of the opposite hand, chosen by the manager) for later ones, adjusted for park, weather, defense and BABIP luck. Total bases require the outcome split between singles and extra-base hits; H+R+RBI adds team-driven components of runners on base and hitters behind, making the outcome depend on the whole inning-level scoring process. The contract settles non-starters and zero-PA starters at an undefined fair market price, so the priced distribution is conditional on batting at least once.

stages.name: Lineup gate and slot
stages.description: The market settles anyone not starting or with no PA at the fair market price, so what matters is the confirmed batting order and slot after the card posts: a rest day, platoon sit or late scratch removes the market's population, while the actual slot (leadoff versus eighth) determines the PA budget. Handedness of the opposing starter drives platoon sits for part-time players and the lineup is typically posted a few hours before first pitch.
stages.distribution: Binary start/no-start with timestamped resolution; slot is categorical 1-9 with known PA means (about 4.6 for leadoff down to about 3.7 for ninth).

stages.name: Plate-appearance budget
stages.description: Expected PA equals the batting-order position times the number of times the order turns over, which depends on team run scoring (more runs, more PAs), game length (extra innings, home team not batting in a won ninth) and the chance the starter is removed early. Blowouts and late-game replacements truncate the fifth PA, and PA count is a small discrete variable (3, 4, 5, rarely 6) so thresholds like 3+ hits interact with the PA mass.
stages.distribution: Discrete 3-6 with mass at 4 and 5; correlated with team total; early-removal tail.

stages.name: Per-PA outcome distribution
stages.description: Given a PA, the probabilities of out, walk, single, double, triple and home run come from the hitter's contact quality and plate skill, shifted by pitcher quality and arsenal (platoon, pitch-type), park dimensions and surface, weather and defense (alignment and range). Total bases weights outcomes 1-4, so the extra-base split (power) matters for TB rungs beyond hit probability. BABIP luck regresses toward an expectation set by contact quality and speed.
stages.distribution: Multinomial per PA; hit probability about 0.22-0.30 per PA; TB per PA right-skewed with HR tail.

stages.name: Starter-to-bullpen handoff
stages.description: The first two to three PAs are against the starter; later ones are against relievers whose handedness and quality differ and who are used to create platoon advantages, so a lefty hitter who gets a right-hander starter will often face a lefty reliever late. Which relievers appear depends on the starter's exit time and bullpen availability, and managers pinch-hit for starters in leverage spots which cuts PA.
stages.distribution: Mixture over exit times; reliever handedness is a categorical draw with manager-driven probability.

stages.name: Overlap and count distribution
stages.description: The H+R+RBI ladder is a weighted sum of events that overlap (a home run scores the hitter, counts as a hit and drives in at least one run), and the hits and TB ladders are the same PA sequence aggregated differently. A PA simulation with base-out states gives the joint distribution; per-rung nestedness holds within each ladder. For the runs and RBI legs the same lineup Markov chain used by the RBI archetype (pa_base_out_state_chain) supplies, PA by PA, the runners on base ahead of him and the chance the hitters behind him drive him in, so H+R+RBI is built from one shared chain rather than slot averages.
stages.distribution: Compound multinomial; overdispersed relative to binomial because of shared game environment; H+R+RBI has heavier tail from inning-level clustering.

environment.note: Park and weather by hit type.

distribution_variance.note: Count distribution is derived from the PA-count survival vector and per-PA outcome probabilities, plus the H+R+RBI joint overlap; contact_dist is a target and is not claimed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and clinched-seed effects act through the lineup card (who sits) and playing_time_role rather than altering per-PA hit probability, so no separate schedule driver is needed beyond the lineup stage; no motivation effect on a given batter's hit rate is documented.

officiating_rules.note: The settled count is the official scorer's: a borderline hit-versus-error call adds or removes a hit and its total bases, so the park scorer's hit/error tendency is a direct settlement input; the umpire zone effect on hits per PA is small and is not modelled separately.

mlb.late_replacement_risk.label: Early-removal and pinch-hit-for risk for a starting hitter (PA truncation)
mlb.late_replacement_risk.mechanism: A starter may be lifted for a pinch hitter or defensive replacement, so PA count is truncated and the late PAs against the bullpen go to someone else.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.rationale: Slot-based PA expectations assume a full game; platoon players, catchers and aging regulars are routinely removed in high-leverage late innings or in blowouts, and the settlement counts only the starter's own PAs.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.measurement: For each hitter-season and k in {3, 4, 5}: a game is eligible if the team's PA count reached 9*(k-1) + slot (the hitter's slot would have its k-th PA). Event 'removed before PA k' = hitter has fewer than k PAs in an eligible game. Estimate P(removed before PA k) by the score state at his previous PA (lead >= 4, within 3, trail >= 4) and the opposing reliever hand, with hitter rates shrunk to role-class means (everyday, platoon, catcher, veteran DH) with k = 60 games. Output survival probabilities to PA3, PA4, PA5. As-of: confirmed lineup plus the model score-state distribution.
raw_data: game-level: batter, slot, PA count, replaced_by, replaced_inning, score at replacement
mlb.late_replacement_risk.why: A 3+ hit rung needs a third and often fourth PA, so the truncation survival to PA4 is a first-order determinant.

mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.label: Expected PA split against the starter versus relievers with reliever handedness
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.mechanism: Later PAs are against relievers, often of the batter's weaker platoon side, so the hitter's per-PA rate differs for PA 1-3 versus 4-5.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.rationale: Team-level bullpen talent hides which relievers the batter faces; the batter faces a distribution over reliever identities determined by starter exit time and managerial matchup use, which changes both handedness and quality.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.measurement: Expected PA vs starter for each slot = sum over PA index of S(b) from mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve evaluated at the batters faced before that PA. Remaining PA allocated to relievers: probability the next reliever is LHP/RHP by team and manager from the last 2 seasons of relief sequences conditional on batter handedness and inning, restricted to relievers available (not used >=25 pitches yesterday or 3 straight days), closer excluded before the 9th unless lead <=3. Batter per-PA rates vs hand = overall rate shrunk toward same-hand/opposite-hand split with k = 200 PA (same hand) and 400 PA (opposite hand). Output: expected PA vs starter, vs LHP relief, vs RHP relief per slot. Units: PA. As-of: lineup post plus bullpen availability.
raw_data: PA-level: batter, pitcher, pitcher hand, inning, role, score state
team reliever usage by hand last 2 seasons
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.why: Total bases and hits for left-handed hitters against righty starters depend materially on the likelihood of facing a left-handed reliever later.

mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.label: Batted-ball outcome model P(1B, 2B, 3B, HR | exit velocity, launch angle, spray, park, defense)
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.mechanism: Total bases weights outcomes 1-4, so per-hit and per-PA probabilities of each outcome type, not just hit probability, drive TB rungs.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.rationale: xBA and xSLG are season-aggregate and park-neutral; a single game needs the outcome mix given the actual park, handedness and the opposing defense. Doubles and triples depend on spray and park geometry (gap depth, wall height) and on runner speed, and HR depends on the carry.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.measurement: Fit a multinomial logit on 4 seasons of Statcast batted balls in play: outcome in {out, 1B, 2B, 3B, HR} ~ spline(launch_speed, launch_angle) x spray-angle bin + park random effect (shrunk with k = 400 BIP per park) + batter stand + infield alignment flag (2023+). A hitter's batted-ball distribution (EV, LA, spray) uses the last 2 seasons with 200-BIP half-life, shrunk to the hand-class mean with k = 150 BIP. Per game: P(outcome | BIP) integrates the model over the hitter's distribution at the game park. Expected TB per PA = P(BIP | PA) * [P(1B) + 2*P(2B) + 3*P(3B) + 4*P(HR)] with P(BIP | PA) = 1 - K% - BB% - HBP% (HR counted inside BIP); strikeouts and walks contribute 0. Units: bases per PA. As-of: lineup post, data through prior day.
free_sources: FanGraphs park factors by hit type
raw_data: Statcast batted-ball events: launch_speed, launch_angle, hc_x, hc_y, events, stand, park, year, if_fielding_alignment
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.why: Distinguishes a singles hitter from a power hitter with the same xBA, which matters for the 2+/3+/4+ total-bases rungs.

mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.label: Per-PA base-out state distribution from the confirmed lineup (Markov chain)
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.mechanism: RBI opportunity is the probability distribution of runners and outs when the hitter bats, derived from the hitters ahead.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.rationale: Average RBI opportunity per slot hides lineup-specific variation: the same cleanup hitter has materially more RBI chances behind two .380-OBP hitters than behind two .300-OBP hitters, and opposing starter baserunner allowance scales it.
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.measurement: Markov chain over 24 transient base-out states (8 base occupancy sets x 0/1/2 outs) plus the inning-end absorbing state, with per-batter outcome probabilities (1B, 2B, 3B, HR, BB/HBP, K, GIDP, other out, reach on error) from batter rates shrunk to league with k = 200 PA, log5-adjusted to the starter (first 2.5 times through) then bullpen, with park multiplier. Runner advancement probabilities from league event data by outcome and base-out state. Solve analytically across the 9-slot order for 9 innings; for each batter's n-th PA output the distribution of (runners on base, outs) and the expected runners on base per PA. Units: expected runners per PA. As-of: lineup post.
raw_data: confirmed lineup and batter hand splits
mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain.why: KXMLBHRR adds runs and RBIs to hits; both depend on the base-out states created by the hitters batting around him in the confirmed order, which this shared chain (also used by hitter_rbis_runs_sb) supplies per PA.

mlb.expected_pa.reason: PA count scales every ladder; needs a distribution (3/4/5/6) rather than a single mean and a link to extra innings. The catalog measurement conditions PA on the team total (implied runs); here that conditioning must use the model's own projected team runs, since a market-implied total is BENCHMARK_ONLY.

mlb.lineup_pit.reason: Settlement is conditional on the confirmed lineup; vintage matters because a scratch settles at the fair market price instead of on the count.

mlb.hitter_quality.reason: Per-PA true talent baseline; projections preferred to small-sample splits.

mlb.hitter_contact_profile.reason: Barrels, hard-hit and launch angle predict hit and TB outcomes beyond results; needs conversion into outcome mix.

mlb.platoon.reason: Hand split is large and known with the card, but reliever hand changes it later (see pa_split_sp_vs_pen).

mlb.batter_vs_pitch.reason: Batter-by-pitch-type samples against a given starter are tiny; usable only as a heavily shrunk adjustment on top of platoon.

mlb.sp_quality.reason: Starter quality only touches PAs 1-3; secondary to hitter and role terms.

mlb.contact_defense.reason: Contact allowed and defense behind the starter affect hit probability modestly; weak for TB.

mlb.bullpen_talent.reason: Team-level bullpen quality is too coarse; reliever hand and identity (pa_split_sp_vs_pen) is the actionable form.

mlb.park.reason: Hit-type and handedness park factors shift doubles, triples and HR, relevant for TB more than hits.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Weather effects on extra-base hits are small; mostly through wind on fly balls, already in park norms.

mlb.hitter_speed.reason: Infield hits and extra bases taken raise hit and TB rates for fast hitters; lower predictive weight than contact quality.

mlb.babip_luck.reason: BABIP gap regression is useful but must regress toward contact quality plus speed, not league average.

mlb.hitter_recent_form.reason: Rolling hot/cold windows contain little signal beyond projections; justified only as tiny shrunk role-change detector.

mlb.contact_dist.reason: Describes the outcome count distribution, i.e. a modelling target rather than information; the count distribution is derived from the PA-count distribution and per-PA outcome probabilities, so it is removed from stage inputs and interactions.

mlb.rbi_opportunity.reason: Needed for the RBI component of H+R+RBI only; irrelevant for hits and TB ladders. Superseded for KXMLBHRR by mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain once the card posts; kept only as the slot-average prior before lineup confirmation.

mlb.run_scoring_opportunity.reason: Needed for the runs component of H+R+RBI only; irrelevant for hits and TB ladders. Superseded for KXMLBHRR by mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain once the card posts; kept only as the slot-average prior before lineup confirmation.

m.rules_text.reason: Start and one-PA gate and pinch-hit exclusion define the population.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung price consistency is market-derived and not a driver of hitting outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: A 3+ hit rung needs at least three PAs and realistically four, so its probability is a step-like function of the PA distribution: replacing the fifth PA with a pinch hitter moves P(3+ hits) little while losing the fourth moves it a lot. The PA distribution, not the mean, interacts with per-PA hit probability. Stated on the PA-count survival vector crossed with the per-PA hit/total-base probability from the batted-ball outcome model.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rung calibration using the PA survival vector versus a mean-PA binomial across lineup slots.

interactions.mechanism: Platoon advantage flips between the starter and later relievers, so the batter's per-PA probability is conditional on pitcher hand by PA index; a lefty hitter vs a righty starter may face two lefty relievers late, offsetting the early advantage. Pitch-type specifics add little on top of hand.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit per-PA hit logit with interaction hand-match x PA index; check sign reversal at PA4-5.

interactions.mechanism: Total bases depend on the product of contact quality, park gap/wall geometry and runner speed on doubles and triples; a hard-hit line drive in a deep-gap park by a fast runner is worth more than the same ball elsewhere. Park factors for doubles/triples must be applied to the hitter's spray profile, not league-average park multipliers.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare TB prediction with spray-specific park factors versus park-level multipliers.

interactions.mechanism: In blowouts regulars on the leading team are removed early (PA lost) while on the trailing team they bat to the end; the game-script regime therefore changes both team strength and the hitter's PA, in opposite directions across the two teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact team score-state regime with PA survival; test PA4 survival for favorites versus underdogs controlling for slot.

interactions.mechanism: H+R+RBI counts the same events multiple times, so the components are positively correlated through team scoring and inning clustering; the sum's variance is greater than the sum of component variances. A hitter's own hit adds to all three when he scores and drives himself in.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the combo through base-out states and compare variance and tail with an independent-sum model.

interactions.mechanism: On an HRR rung the hitter's own extra-base hit both counts as a hit and changes the base state for himself and for the next hitters, so his hits, runs and RBIs are jointly generated by one chain: a double with two on adds one hit and two RBIs and puts him in scoring position; treating the legs as independent understates the upper-rung tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate HRR with the chain versus summing marginal hit, run and RBI distributions; compare calibration of 4+ and 5+ rungs on past games of the same hitters.

nonlinearities.shape: Step-like: probability of 3+ hits changes steeply between 3 and 4 PA and little above 5
nonlinearities.why: Hit counts are bounded by PA and rungs at 2+/3+ sit at the boundary of the PA support, so mean-PA linear terms are misleading.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in barrel rate for total bases: each point of barrel% adds more TB than a point of hard-hit or xBA
nonlinearities.why: Total bases weight home runs (4) and extra-base hits (2-3) heavily, so power metrics enter convexly relative to hits.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating regression to expectation; extreme deviations regress further in one-start horizons
nonlinearities.why: BABIP luck is bounded and reverts at a rate depending on balls in play, so one extra hot week should have little weight.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by hit type: doubles and triples respond to gap geometry nonlinearly, HR to carry
nonlinearities.why: Park effects are not uniform across hit types, so a single multiplier distorts TB more than hits.

contract.settlement_definition: One live series, KXMLBHR (single game; only the 1+ rung was sampled, higher rungs presumed), with sampled rules: Yes if the named batter, who must be in the official starting lineup and record at least one plate appearance, records at least N home runs in the game 'originally scheduled for' the listed date; a scratch or a bench start, a starter with no plate appearance, and a player who enters later all settle at the undefined fair market price, and pinch-hit at-bats do not count. The text is silent on whether extra-inning home runs count (presumed yes, as the official box score includes them), on postponement or suspension of the originally scheduled game, and on a rain-shortened game; no source of truth is named. The playoff-series home-run ladder (KXMLBSERIESHR) moved to the counting-specials archetype.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick is not in the starting lineup but later enters the game, the market will resolve to the fair market price, pinch hit at bats will not count towards the market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Single-game HR ladder excludes substitutes and settles them at the fair market price; population is starters with a PA.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick starts the game but does not record a plate appearance, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: A starter removed before batting (injury in the top of the first, early ejection) does not settle No; the priced event is conditional on at least one PA.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick records 1+ home runs in Milwaukee vs Tampa Bay professional baseball game originally scheduled for Oct 28, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The ladder counts home runs in one game tied to its original schedule date, with 'N+' rungs (floor_strike 0.5 for 1+).

variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: 1+ and 2+ rungs on one game are nested events of the same count, so P(2+) <= P(1+) and both come from one per-game HR distribution.

Extra innings, inside-the-park home runs and postponement are not addressed in the KXMLBHR text; the official scorer's count presumably includes extra-inning and inside-the-park home runs (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, hr_extras_postponement).

Population is conditional on start and at least one PA (rule text), so the priced distribution excludes zero-PA games; the fair-market-price branch replaces what would otherwise be a No for late scratches.

Series totals, playoff league totals, walk-off counts and window markets (KXMLBSERIESHR, KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS, KXMLBWALKOFFS, KXMLBNEXTHR) are filed in the counting-specials archetype and are not modelled here.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box-score home runs for the player (presumed MLB Stats API); the sampled text names no source.

mechanism.summary: A home run in a game is the union over the hitter's plate appearances of a low-probability event (about 3 to 6 percent per PA), so P(1+) is approximately 1 minus the product of (1 minus p) over his PAs and P(2+) comes from the tail of a Poisson-binomial. The per-PA probability is a product of hitter power (barrel, pull-air and bat-speed profile), pitcher vulnerability by handedness and pitch type, and a park-weather carry factor that depends on wall geometry in the hitter's spray direction, wind component along that direction, temperature, humidity, altitude and the ball. The number of PAs depends on slot and removal risk, and later PAs face relievers. The event is dominated by Bernoulli luck, so the edge is in the multiplicative environment and matchup terms and in knowing the starter, because HR/FB regresses. Series, window and playoff-count home-run markets are filed in the counting-specials archetype and are not generated here.

stages.name: Participation and PA count
stages.description: The market settles non-starters and zero-PA starters at the fair market price, so the priced population is starters with at least one PA, and the lineup slot plus game length fix the number of HR opportunities. Because per-PA probability is small, expected HRs are almost linear in PA, so lineup posting and early replacement matter proportionally.
stages.distribution: Binary participation resolved at card time; PA count discrete 3-6.

stages.name: Hitter power profile
stages.description: Per-PA HR probability starts with the batter's batted-ball quality (barrels, exit velocity, launch angle), his pull-air rate (home runs are disproportionately pulled fly balls), bat speed and squared-up rate as early signals, and his HR/FB which regresses toward barrel-implied rate. The profile is hand-specific against pitcher handedness.
stages.distribution: Heavy-tailed hitter heterogeneity: per-PA rates from under 1.5% to over 8% across regular hitters.

stages.name: Pitcher and pitch-type vulnerability
stages.description: The starter's HR/FB, barrels allowed, fly-ball rate and the pitch types he throws in hittable locations determine how much of the hitter's power profile is realised; relievers have different HR vulnerability and handedness. The hitter's pitch-type strengths meet the pitcher's usage in damage zones. The contract voids nothing when the opposing starter changes: the HR text settles at fair price only for the named hitter, so before first pitch the pitcher side is a mixture over the announced starter and his replacement distribution (next rotation arm, opener-plus-bulk or bullpen game) weighted by the change probability.
stages.distribution: Pitcher HR vulnerability ranges about 0.6 to 1.8 HR/9; relief HR rates differ and are lower sample.

stages.name: Park, wind and carry
stages.description: The same batted ball is a home run in some parks and a fly out in others: wall distance and height by sector, roof state, wind component along the ball's flight path, air density (temperature, humidity, altitude) and ball characteristics determine carry. Because park factors are averages, deviations by hitter spray profile and day-specific wind matter, and the effect is multiplicative on per-PA probability.
stages.distribution: Multiplicative shift from about 0.6 to 1.6 of the neutral per-PA probability; wind adds game-specific variance.

stages.name: Single-game aggregation and within-game dependence
stages.description: Single-game P(1+) and P(2+) come from the Poisson-binomial over the hitter's plate appearances against the starter and then relievers, with the game-shared environment (wind, ball carry, the opposing pitcher's day) adding positive correlation across his PAs. The 2+ rung is far more sensitive to that shared component than the 1+ rung because it needs two events on the same day, and to the chance of a fifth PA in a high-scoring or extra-inning game.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial over 3-6 PAs with overdispersion from a game-level random effect; P(2+) roughly proportional to the square of the per-PA rate times a dispersion inflation.

opponent_matchup.note: Pitcher HR vulnerability by hand and pitch.

availability_news.note: A scratch settles at the fair market price, so lineup confirmation is the main news driver.

game_context_script.note: Game length and score state set the number of PAs (a fifth PA in high-scoring or extra-inning games) and the shared game environment.

distribution_variance.note: Within-game HR dependence (dispersion) that inflates the 2+ rung relative to an independent Poisson-binomial.

settlement_contract.note: Start and one-PA gate, fair-market-price branch, pinch-hit exclusion and nested N+ rungs.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers do not influence a hitter's HR probability beyond lineup slot and pinch-hitting, both captured in lineup and expected PA; there is no strategic switch (like bunting or intentional walks) that materially changes per-PA HR rate in the sampled contracts.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and clinched status operate only through whether the hitter starts (lineup card), and per-PA HR probability itself is not documented to change with stakes; the series market's rest effect is within lineup exposure.

officiating_rules.note: The umpire zone and rules shape walk and strikeout rates but not the HR probability per ball in play at the level this contract can price; no rule difference changes whether a ball counts as a home run except inside-the-park, which is rare and counted.

mlb.park_specific_xhr.label: Park-and-weather-specific expected home runs per fly ball (xHR by batted-ball sector)
mlb.park_specific_xhr.mechanism: Whether a hit fly ball clears the wall depends on distance, wall height in that sector, wind component, air density and roof.
mlb.park_specific_xhr.rationale: A park HR factor averages over all sprays; a pull-heavy hitter in a park with a short porch on his pull side gets a very different factor from a spray hitter. Deviation from the average on a specific day (wind out to right) matters most for hitters who hit to that sector.
mlb.park_specific_xhr.measurement: From 4 seasons of batted balls with exit velocity, launch angle and spray angle, fit P(HR | EV, LA, spray) per park by logistic spline with park random effect; add wind component along the spray direction and air density as covariates. For each hitter compute expected HR per fly ball by integrating his empirical (EV, LA, spray) distribution (half-life 200 BIP, shrink to hand-class k = 150 BIP) over the game park with the day's wind and density. Units: probability per batted ball and per PA. As-of: forecast at lineup post.
free_sources: park wall geometry (Ballparks of Baseball / team sites)
raw_data: batted ball EV, LA, spray, park, HR flag
mlb.park_specific_xhr.why: Connects hitter spray profile to day-specific carry, a more exact form of the park-by-wind interaction than separate factors.

mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.label: Expected reliever HR vulnerability by hand for the PAs after the starter exits
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.mechanism: Later PAs face relievers whose HR rate and handedness differ from the starter's.
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.rationale: HR rates of relievers are not the starter's; relief pitchers are often fastball-heavy but with lower HR/FB, and managers match hands. For a batter with 4 PAs, one or two come against relievers so ignoring them mis-sets the late-PA HR probability.
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.measurement: Using the starter-exit survival, allocate PA index to likely relievers (top 3-4 by team usage in last 20 games, by hand). Reliever HR rate per PA vs same-hand and opposite-hand batters over 2 seasons half-life 250 BF, shrink to league relief by hand with k = 200 BF. Per-hitter HR probability for PA >= k = hitter power x reliever vulnerability. Units: HR per PA. As-of: bullpen availability at lineup post.
raw_data: PA-level: pitcher id, role, hand, HR flag, batter hand, inning
mlb.relief_hr_vulnerability_by_hand.why: Team bullpen_talent (xFIP) conflates K/BB with HR; the HR-specific relief exposure is what matters here.

mlb.series_hr_exposure.label: Series home-run exposure: games played distribution x start probability x per-game HR rate
mlb.series_hr_exposure.mechanism: A series HR total is an aggregation over a random number of games in which the hitter may or may not start.
mlb.series_hr_exposure.rationale: The 2+ HR series rung is dominated by how many games the series goes (4-7) and whether the hitter plays each; the per-game HR probability then compounds. Team playoffs and rest days change both exposure and opposing starters (aces vs fifth starter).
mlb.series_hr_exposure.measurement: N_games ~ distribution from series win-prob model (probability each game, length distribution 4-7 for best-of-7); P(start) per game from role (everyday = 0.95, platoon = 0.55 conditional on opposing starter hand); per-game p_HR from the single-game model with each game's probable starter. Series count distribution = compound sum. Units: expected HR in series. As-of: before each game with updated series state.
raw_data: series state, probable starters, games remaining
mlb.series_hr_exposure.why: Defined here while KXMLBSERIESHR was filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation the series ladder is in the counting-specials archetype, which stages this input; it is not staged here.

mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.label: Within-game shared HR environment dispersion (wind/ball/pitcher day latent)
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.mechanism: Home runs by different hitters in the same game share environment and pitcher states, so counts are overdispersed relative to independent Bernoullis.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.rationale: Single-hitter markets need only his marginal, but any multi-hitter or team inference (and the 2+ HR rung) depends on positive dependence; wind blowing out raises everyone's probability together and HR events cluster when a pitcher is lacking command.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.measurement: From 4 seasons of games compute the variance ratio of team-plus-opponent HR counts to the Poisson-binomial expectation given the matchup model, by park roof type and wind-out strength decile; estimate dispersion phi (negative binomial) shrunk to league with k = 100 games. Units: variance inflation. As-of: through prior games. FALLBACK (pre-registered, no matchup model needed): estimate phi first from league-average HR per PA by park, roof type and wind-out decile using plate-appearance counts, then replace expectation with the project's matchup model once it exists; the two-step version avoids circularity.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.why: Calibrates the 2+ HR rung and joint HR outcomes consistently.

mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.label: Playoff walk-off count: remaining-games exposure and per-game walk-off probability
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.mechanism: A walk-off is a home-team win in the bottom of the 9th or an extra inning; the playoff count is the sum over remaining playoff games of a Bernoulli event whose probability depends on late-inning state, closer quality and who is home.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.rationale: KXMLBWALKOFFS pays on at least N walk-offs across the playoffs (the run that gives the home team the lead ends the game), so it is a count over a random number of games, with the count so far fixed. The per-game probability is not constant: it needs the home team to be tied or trailing by a small margin entering its last at-bat and to score the go-ahead run, and it varies with bullpen quality, extras probability and home-team identity.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.measurement: Count so far W0 from official game results. Remaining games G are random: enumerate bracket paths and series lengths (best-of-5 or 7) from own per-game win probabilities. For each future game compute p_walkoff = P(home team trails by <=3 or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th and takes the lead before three outs, or wins in an extra inning) from the game run model plus half-inning chain with the visiting closer and due-up slots (walk-off stopping rule), shrunk to the league postseason rate over 2015-2025 with k = 100 games. P(count >= N) = P(W0 + sum Bernoulli(p_g) >= N) integrated over the distribution of G (Poisson-binomial mixture). Units: count and probability. As-of: daily during the playoffs.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason schedule and linescores
raw_data: postseason game log with inning-by-inning score and walk-off flag
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.why: Defined here when KXMLBWALKOFFS was filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation the series is in unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials, which stages this input. Not a hitter-HR input.

mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.label: Probability the listed starter does not start (scratch, opener, bulk swap) and replacement distribution
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.mechanism: Contracts that do not gate on the pitcher (F5 lines, opposing-hitter props) stay live when the listed starter is scratched or swapped, so the change probability and the replacement's identity shift the whole outcome distribution.
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.rationale: Pre-lineup prices sit on the announced pitcher; a late scratch or opener plan is a large run-expectation change (a quality starter replaced by a bullpen day), and in the postseason pitching plans change.
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.measurement: P(change) = logistic(a + b1*days_to_first_pitch + b2*IL_return_flag + b3*injury_report_flag + b4*team opener or bulk start rate in last 10 starts + b5*postseason + b6*doubleheader), fitted only on own-captured announced-versus-actual starters; until at least one full season of captured vintages exists, use the league base rate stratified by status flags with a Beta prior (k = 100 games) and label the output uncalibrated. Replacement distribution = mixture of next-in-rotation, bulk reliever and opener with their F5 run rates over 2 seasons shrunk to team average with k = 8 starts. Output P(change), the replacement distribution (identity, throwing hand and role of each candidate with probabilities), E[F5 runs | change] minus E[F5 runs | no change] for F5 markets, and the replacement mixture used by opposing-hitter props through mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability. As-of: each timestamp before first pitch, using only announcements available then.
free_sources: MLB Stats API probable pitchers history (vintage unverified)
mlb.f5_starter_change_risk.why: The single-game HR ladder gates only on the named hitter (fair price if he does not start), so a scratched or swapped opposing starter leaves the market live; pitcher HR vulnerability must be a mixture over the announced and replacement starters weighted by this risk.

mlb.hitter_hr_profile.reason: Barrel, pull-air and max EV are the best stable power signals; HR totals themselves are too noisy.

mlb.bat_tracking.reason: Bat speed and squared-up rate stabilise earlier than barrels but history only exists from 2023-24; useful as early-season prior.

mlb.hitter_contact_profile.reason: Barrel and hard-hit rates are the same measurements already in hitter_hr_profile; the xBA/xSLG part is hit-oriented and adds nothing for HR.

mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.reason: HR/FB and barrels allowed by batter hand set the pitcher side; should be regressed to barrel-implied HR rate.

mlb.hr_environment.reason: Park HR factor by handedness; label conflates wind and carry that other inputs already carry.

mlb.wind_vector_park.reason: Day-specific wind component along the park axis is a first-order game-level factor; needs spray-direction specificity.

mlb.air_density.reason: Density changes carry but varies slowly within season and is already partly in park norms; use as deviation from park mean.

mlb.platoon.reason: Hand split in power is real but modest relative to barrel rate and park, and it is superseded by hand-specific hitter and pitcher HR profiles, so it is not a separate staged input.

mlb.batter_vs_pitch.reason: Pitch-type interaction is sample-starved for HR; effect is not separable from pitcher HR vulnerability at game level.

mlb.expected_pa.reason: Per-PA probability is small so expected HR scales almost linearly in PA; needs survival to PA 4/5. Its catalog measurement conditions on implied team runs from the market total; for this ladder use model-projected team runs instead (market totals are BENCHMARK_ONLY).

mlb.lineup_pit.reason: Start gate: only confirmed starters with a PA settle on the count; also yields slot.

mlb.bullpen_talent.reason: Team bullpen quality is a poor HR proxy; reliever HR vulnerability by hand (new input) is the usable measurement.

mlb.hrfb_regression.reason: HR/FB regression is needed to avoid chasing hot streaks; works as a shrinkage procedure on top of the profile rather than a new signal.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of 1+ and 2+ prices is market-derived; useful as a check only.

m.rules_text.reason: The start/PA gate of the single-game ladder and the series scope (no start gate, other rounds excluded) both come from rules text and must be versioned per series.

mlb.pa_sim.reason: A simulation method, not an input; kept only as the aggregation engine for the 2+ rung and series totals and no longer listed as a staged input.

mlb.contact_dist.reason: Hit/TB/RBI count distributions given PA are defined for hits; HR needs a Poisson-binomial with shared environment, which this definition does not provide.

interactions.mechanism: A pull-power hitter's HR probability is the product of his pull-air barrel rate, the park's wall geometry on that side and the wind component along that line; each alone is mild but together they move per-PA probability by factors of two. The spray direction links the hitter profile to the specific wind and wall, so they must be modelled jointly.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(HR) per batted ball with a spray x wind x park term and compare with a model using separate park and wind factors.

interactions.mechanism: Per-PA HR probability changes mid-game as the starter is replaced: PAs 1-3 use the starter's vulnerability, PAs 4-5 the reliever's. A homer-prone starter who is pulled early shifts exposure to a different arm, so total HR expectation is a PA-weighted mix conditioned on exit time.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute expected HR with PA-index-specific pitcher vulnerability versus a single starter rate; compare calibration.

interactions.mechanism: Carry gains from thin air and tailwind add to the park norm but saturate near the wall: a ball that clears by feet gains nothing from more carry while a ball at the warning track gains most. The joint effect is therefore concave in the sum of wind and density and strongest for borderline fly balls.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit P(HR) as logistic in distance-over-wall with wind/density shifting the distance; check concavity in wind and density deviations.

interactions.mechanism: HRs of hitters in the same game share weather and pitcher-day factors, so P(2+) and any multi-hitter outcome has positive dependence; the 2+ rung for one hitter is sensitive to the shared factor and to his PA count in the extra-inning tail.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed rate of 2+ HR games by hitter strength decile against Poisson-binomial and negative-binomial predictions.

interactions.mechanism: The 2+ rung needs two home runs, so it is convex in the number of plate appearances: a leadoff hitter in a game with high projected team runs who stays in for a fifth PA has a disproportionately higher P(2+) than a bottom-order hitter at risk of being pinch-hit for late, while P(1+) moves almost linearly. Power hitters are rarely pinch-hit for, so the truncation risk concentrates in platoon and defensive players.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised 2+ rates against a linear-in-PA model across lineup slots and game totals, split by pinch-hit-for frequency.

interactions.mechanism: If the announced starter is scratched, the hitter's per-PA HR rate is evaluated against the replacement: a bulk or bullpen day raises the share of PAs against relievers of known hand, so the effect of a change depends on how far the replacement's HR allowed by hand differs from the starter's; for a fly-ball replacement facing a pull hitter the change raises P(1+).
interactions.how_to_test: On games with a late starter change, compare realised hitter HR against predictions using the announced starter versus the mixture; the mixture should reduce log loss only in changed games.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in barrel rate: HR probability per PA rises faster than linearly with barrel% and pull-air%
nonlinearities.why: HRs concentrate in the top tail of exit velocity and launch angle, so power metrics enter convexly; linear barrel terms underprice elite hitters.

nonlinearities.shape: Asymmetric saturating in wind component: gains from tailwind exceed losses from headwind and both saturate at high speed
nonlinearities.why: Carry depends nonlinearly on speed and wall distance; the same wind has different value for borderline versus deep fly balls.

nonlinearities.shape: Near-linear in PA at small p but with a discrete floor/ceiling at 3 and 6 PA
nonlinearities.why: Per-PA probability is small so 1 - (1-p)^PA is almost linear, but discrete support of PA and extra-inning cases create tails.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating shrinkage with fly-ball count: regression weight falls as ln(FB) rises
nonlinearities.why: HR/FB signal stabilises slowly (hundreds of FBs), so early-season HR/FB should be heavily shrunk and later weights grow slowly.

required_data.dataset: Batted-ball events with spray and park
required_data.timestamp_requirement: All events before game date; bat tracking only from 2023 in public Savant data. Note: squared_up is a Savant leaderboard metric, not a per-event Statcast CSV column, so it must be derived from bat speed and exit velocity or taken from leaderboards at season grain.

required_data.grain: one row per game; one per park
required_data.fields: wind speed/direction, temperature, humidity, pressure, roof, park wall distance and height by sector
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Forecast vintages at lineup post.

required_data.grain: one row per game-batter and per series
required_data.fields: lineup slot, starter flag, PA, probable starters
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Time-stamped lineup; bracket updates.

required_data.fields: ticker, strike, rules text
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Version rules.

unresolved.what_would_resolve: Sample KXMLBHR rules for a regular-season game and compare the participation clauses.

unresolved.description: Ball carry changes (ball manufacturing, humidors) shift league HR rate year to year; there is no public per-game measurement of ball properties, so carry regime must be inferred from league HR/FB residuals.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Track league-wide HR/FB residual by month and check against a regime-switching term.

unresolved.description: Stadium-level wind speed and direction at ball height are not exposed by free forecast APIs, which give airport or grid values; whether the resolution is good enough to capture park-specific wind swirl is unverified.
unresolved.what_would_resolve: Compare free forecast winds against paid stadium sensors or Statcast ball-flight residuals.

unresolved.description: The single-game HR ladder is conditional only on the hitter, so a scratch of the opposing starter does not trigger the fair-price branch, yet the only availability input is lineup_pit; the probable-pitcher change risk input defined in first5_markets is not available here and pitcher_hr_vulnerability is evaluated for the announced starter only.
