contract.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation the only live series is KXMLBFODTEAMS (rules sampled): one market per club, Yes 'If Washington is confirmed to be in the Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game'; the market 'resolves immediately on team selection for the game', and 'If no Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game is announced to have participants or occurs, all markets resolve to No'. Two clubs are selected, so Yes probabilities across clubs sum to about two when a game is staged. The text gives no deadline for the announcement, does not say what happens if announced teams are later replaced or the game is cancelled after selection, and names no source beyond confirmation. The franchise-sale market formerly filed here (KXMLBTEAMSALE) was classified out of scope (franchise business); awards, delay and hiring series moved earlier.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is confirmed to be in the Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Each club market settles on confirmation that the club is a participant in the 2027 Field of Dreams game, not on the game being played.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves immediately on team selection for the game.
rules_evidence.establishes: Resolution is triggered by the selection announcement (typically with the schedule release), so later cancellation of the game appears not to reverse a Yes.

rules_evidence.quote: If no Pro Baseball 2027 Field of Dreams Game is announced to have participants or occurs, all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: If the event is not staged in 2027 every club resolves No, so P(game staged) multiplies every club probability.

variants_and_edge_cases: Two participants per game: club markets are a structured set whose Yes probabilities sum to two times P(game staged), so club probabilities must be modelled jointly as a pair choice rather than independently.

Selection precedes play: 'resolves immediately on team selection' means a club announced and later replaced (in 2020 the game was announced, re-planned and then cancelled before being played in 2021) would already have resolved Yes; the text does not address re-selection (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, off_reselection).

No deadline is stated for 'announced to have participants or occurs'; with the CBA expiring Dec 1 2026, a delayed 2027 schedule release postpones selection, and the market's close date governs whether a late announcement counts (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, off_no_deadline).
The event has been intermittent (played 2021 and 2022, not staged 2023-2025), so whether a 2027 game exists at all is the largest single factor, ahead of which clubs play.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB schedule release and club announcements of the Field of Dreams participants (presumed); the text says only 'confirmed'.

mechanism.summary: The Field of Dreams team market is a scheduling decision, not a sporting outcome. First the league must decide to stage a game at the Dyersville, Iowa site in 2027, which depends on venue readiness and its owners' development plans, the broadcast partner's appetite, the schedule-making calendar and, this cycle, a collective bargaining agreement that expires on Dec 1 2026 and could delay the 2027 schedule. Given a game, two clubs are chosen: the league and broadcaster favour Midwestern clubs within driving distance of Iowa, high-profile or nationally marketable matchups, clubs not used recently (2021 White Sox-Yankees, 2022 Cubs-Reds), and a designated home club willing to give up a home date at a stadium of roughly 8,000 seats; the pairing must fit the schedule matrix, usually as part of an existing series. The announcement normally arrives with the schedule release or in a dedicated press event, preceded by leaks of uneven credibility. Team quality and player performance play no role.

stages.name: Contract scope and resolution trigger
stages.description: The family must be identified from the rules text rather than the prefix, which has carried award, delay, esports, hiring and sale markets. For KXMLBFODTEAMS the text fixes a resolution trigger at team selection, an all-No branch if no 2027 game is announced with participants or played, and no explicit announcement deadline; the market close time relative to the expected schedule release decides how much labour-delay risk the contract carries.
stages.distribution: Deterministic routing; a small discrete probability that re-selection or a late announcement is treated differently from the plain reading.

stages.name: Whether a 2027 game is staged
stages.description: The league staged the game in 2021 and 2022 and skipped it from 2023 through 2025 while the Dyersville site was redeveloped, so staging is an annual decision driven by venue status, broadcast and sponsorship commitments, the league's portfolio of special-event games (Little League Classic, Rickwood, international series) and the schedule calendar. A lockout after the CBA expiry would delay the 2027 schedule and could remove the event entirely, which sends every club market to No.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli with a probability that moves in jumps on venue, broadcaster and labour news; heavy dependence on a single league decision, so no averaging across clubs.

stages.name: Choice of the two participating clubs
stages.description: Given a game, the pair is chosen to maximise attendance draw, television value and regional fit: clubs within a few hundred miles of eastern Iowa (Cubs, White Sox, Cardinals, Twins, Royals, Brewers, Reds) carry most of the mass, a national draw can be paired with a regional club, recently used clubs are less likely, and the designated home club gives up a home date and gate revenue. The pairing must also exist in the 2027 schedule matrix (a division, rivalry or interleague series in mid-season).
stages.distribution: Categorical over about 435 unordered club pairs, concentrated on a few dozen Midwestern pairings; club-level marginals sum to two given staging, with strong negative dependence between clubs in the same slot.

stages.name: Schedule release and report flow
stages.description: Participants are usually confirmed with the schedule release or a dedicated announcement, and local reports, permit filings and broadcaster leaks precede it. Before the release the state is a posterior over staging and pairings given these reports weighted by source reliability; a CBA negotiation that delays the schedule shifts the announcement date and can push it past the market's close.
stages.distribution: Discrete jumps at report times; an announcement-date distribution that is right-skewed under labour uncertainty.

talent_strength.note: Club quality does not decide Field of Dreams participation; selection rests on geography, marketability and scheduling, so no team-strength input changes the club probabilities.

opponent_matchup.note: Which pairings are attractive (regional rivalry, national draw paired with a Midwestern club) and fit the schedule matrix.

role_personnel.note: The designated home club's willingness to give up a home date is the only club-role element; no player role matters.

availability_news.note: Timestamped leaks and announcements about staging and participants, scored by source reliability.

coaching_scheme.note: Managers and tactics have no influence on whether a club is chosen for a special-event game; the decision sits with the league office, the broadcaster and the clubs' business side.

environment.note: Venue readiness and status of the Dyersville site enter through the staging probability.

game_context_script.note: The contract resolves on selection, before any game is played, so no in-game state, score or leverage can affect it.

pace_volume.note: There are no opportunity counts; the only count is two participants per staged game, which is a structural constraint inside the pair-choice input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion exists; the event is a single league scheduling decision followed by a pair choice, with no repeated trials to convert.

distribution_variance.note: All club outcomes share one staging Bernoulli and a pair constraint, so outcomes are strongly dependent; few historical events make the base rate wide.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Event calendar, CBA expiry and schedule-matrix fit.

officiating_rules.note: The labour agreement governs whether and when the 2027 schedule is made; no on-field officiating applies.

settlement_contract.note: Selection trigger, all-No branch, missing deadline and market close relative to the schedule release.

mlb.special_event_game_staging.label: Special-event game staging probability (Field of Dreams and similar one-off venue games) for a season
mlb.special_event_game_staging.mechanism: A one-off venue game exists only if the league schedules it, which depends on venue readiness, broadcaster commitment and the schedule calendar.
mlb.special_event_game_staging.rationale: Every club market resolves No if no 2027 game is staged, so this single probability scales all club probabilities; it is driven by site redevelopment status in Dyersville, the national broadcaster's special-event slate, the league's other special events that compete for the same mid-season window, and labour risk around the Dec 1 2026 CBA expiry.
mlb.special_event_game_staging.measurement: P(staged in season Y) = logistic(b0 + b1*venue_ready_flag + b2*broadcaster_slot_confirmed + b3*prior_season_staged + b4*announced_by_date_flag) times (1 - P(labour stoppage cancels or delays the event past the market close)); fit b on special-event venue games 2016-2026 (Fort Bragg, Williamsport Little League Classic, Field of Dreams, Rickwood, international series) with a weakly informative prior (sd 1 on each coefficient) because N is under 30; labour factor from mlb.labor_stoppage_regime. As-of: latest dated venue, broadcaster or league report; units: probability.
free_sources: MLB press releases and schedule announcements (free_scrape)
Local Iowa press on the Dyersville site (free_scrape)
raw_data: special-event games by season with announcement date, venue, participants
mlb.special_event_game_staging.why: KXMLBFODTEAMS resolves all clubs No if no 2027 game is announced with participants or played, so staging is the first multiplier.

mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.label: Special-event participant selection affinity by club pair (distance, marketability, recency, home-date cost, schedule fit)
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.mechanism: The league and broadcaster pick the pair that maximises regional attendance and national audience subject to the schedule matrix and a home club willing to move a home date.
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.rationale: Club probabilities are a pair choice, not independent events: Midwestern clubs dominate, national draws are paired with regional clubs, recent participants are less likely, and the designated home club loses gate revenue at a small temporary stadium; the pairing must already exist as a mid-season series in the 2027 matrix.
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.measurement: Conditional logit over unordered club pairs: utility = a1*log(min road distance of the two clubs to Dyersville, miles) + a2*(TV market size rank sum) + a3*(either club used in the last 3 stagings) + a4*(pair is a division or traditional rival) + a5*(pair has a mid-season series in the released or projected matrix); fit on special-event venue selections 2016-2026 with coefficients shrunk to a distance-only model (shrinkage weight k = 10 events). Club marginal = sum of pair probabilities containing the club (sums to 2). As-of: matrix and report date; units: probability.
free_sources: Club market-size and stadium distance data (public geography)
raw_data: club coordinates and distance to Dyersville
mlb.special_event_team_selection_affinit.why: Gives each KXMLBFODTEAMS club market a probability that respects the two-participant constraint and regional selection pattern.

mlb.offfield_base_rate.reason: A single off-field reference class is too coarse; for KXMLBFODTEAMS only the special-event staging and selection history is a relevant base rate, and it is better carried by the two special-event inputs. Context only.

mlb.news.reason: Leaks from local Iowa press, broadcasters and clubs precede the official participant announcement; reports must be timestamped and weighted by news_source_reliability_score.

mlb.roster_moves.reason: Player transactions have no bearing on which clubs are chosen for the Field of Dreams game, the only live series after the reconciliation.

interactions.mechanism: A club's Yes probability is P(game staged) times its marginal in the pair choice; news that strengthens one club's selection does nothing if the event itself is doubtful, and a staging confirmation lifts every plausible club at once while leaving their ratios unchanged.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose historical special-event club probabilities into staging and selection parts and check that staging news moves club prices proportionally.

interactions.mechanism: Under a lockout after Dec 1 2026 the 2027 schedule is not finalised, so selection cannot be announced and the event may be dropped; if the market closes before a delayed release the all-No branch applies, so labour risk matters more the earlier the close date.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare schedule-release dates in labour-dispute years (1994-95, 2021-22) with normal years and map them against the market close time.

interactions.mechanism: A report naming a pairing moves club probabilities in proportion to the outlet's reliability for schedule leaks; local reports about hotel blocks or permits for specific dates are informative only if the clubs scheduled that week match the leaked pairing.
interactions.how_to_test: Score past schedule-leak reports by outlet against released schedules and fit outlet-level likelihood ratios.

interactions.mechanism: Clubs beyond a few hundred miles of eastern Iowa have near-zero selection probability unless they are a national draw, so the distance effect is a threshold rather than a smooth decline, and the generic off-field base rate overstates distant clubs.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot selection frequency against distance for regional special events and test a threshold against a log-linear distance term.

nonlinearities.shape: step function in time at announcement dates
nonlinearities.why: Staging probability jumps to near one at the participant announcement and to near zero if the schedule is released without the event; between announcements it drifts only with venue and labour news.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold in distance with a national-draw exception
nonlinearities.why: Selection mass falls sharply beyond driving distance of the site, except for a few national-draw clubs paired with a regional club, so a linear distance effect misprices both groups.

contract.settlement_definition: Five live series after the reconciliation. KXMLBSTART (rules sampled) pays Yes if the named player is in the official starting batting order (including as designated hitter) when the game begins; announcement in an earlier lineup then replacement before the game begins resolves No, and entering later as a pinch hitter or substitute does not qualify. KXMLBPITCH (rules sampled) pays Yes if the named player records at least one pitch in a regular-season game inside a date window (example after Jul 28 and before Sep 28, 2026). KXMLBRETURN (rules sampled) pays Yes if the named player 'must enter a game for the Tigers' (his named club) after one date and before another; it does not restrict the window to the regular season and is silent on a trade to another club. KXMLBSTARTER (starting pitcher) and KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP are title-only. CAUTION: the sampled KXMLBSTART rules_secondary is truncated at 'An actual plate appearance is ', so a clause that may require a plate appearance is unseen (pp_start_rules_truncated). Late insertion: a bench player placed into the posted card before the game begins because a teammate is scratched is in the official starting order when the game begins and resolves Yes; the No path applies only to the replaced player. Next-team and debut markets moved to transactions.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution is based on the official starting batting order recorded by the governing league.
rules_evidence.establishes: Start market settles on the official starting batting order at game start (including DH), not on a probable or announced lineup.

rules_evidence.quote: Entering the game later as a pinch hitter or other substitute does not qualify.
rules_evidence.establishes: Substitutes do not count, so the market is a pure starting-lineup event.

rules_evidence.quote: must record at least 1 pitch in a Pro Baseball regular season game after Jul 28, 2026 and before Sep 28, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: Pitch-in-window market is a multi-game availability event (regular season only) with a date window, not a single-game start.

rules_evidence.quote: If Shohei Ohtani is announced in an earlier lineup but is replaced before the game begins, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: An announced starter who is scratched before first pitch resolves No, so the late-scratch hazard after the card posts is priced.

rules_evidence.quote: In order for the market to resolve to Yes, Tarik Skubal must enter a game for the Tigers after May 8, 2026 and before June 8, 2026.
rules_evidence.establishes: The return market counts any game entry for the named club inside the window (a relief or pinch appearance counts), so it is a return-from-injury hazard tied to one club.

variants_and_edge_cases: Population differs: single-game starting-lineup markets (KXMLBSTART, KXMLBSTARTINGLINEUP), a starting-pitcher market (KXMLBSTARTER), a window-long 'will he pitch' market (KXMLBPITCH) and a window-long return market for an injured player with his named club (KXMLBRETURN) have different hazards (manager's lineup decision, rotation slot, injury/rehab progression).

Start market: an announced lineup that changes before first pitch resolves No (late scratch), so lineup posting time and warm-up scratch hazard matter; a player who starts as pitcher qualifies only if he is in the batting order.

Pitch window: regular season only (postseason pitches do not count in the sampled text), 'after' and 'before' dates are exclusive, and rehab appearances in the minors presumably do not count; exact handling of injury list is not stated.

KXMLBSTARTER is title-only: whether it settles on the announced probable or on the pitcher who throws the first pitch, and how an opener day is treated, is unseen; the hitter-card rule (announced then replaced resolves No) may not carry over.

Late card insertion: the player who replaces a scratched starter before first pitch settles Yes under 'official starting batting order ... when the game begins', so late_scratch_hazard for the replaced player and a late-insertion probability for bench players are two different quantities.

Return window (KXMLBRETURN): any entry into a game for the named club counts, including a pinch-running or relief appearance; the text names the club, so a trade before the return presumably resolves No, and unlike KXMLBPITCH it does not say 'regular season' (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, pp_return_scope).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official starting batting order recorded by the league (MLB Stats API game feed) for start markets; league game logs for pitch and game-entry records (KXMLBPITCH, KXMLBRETURN); injured-list transactions for return timing.

mechanism.summary: Participation contracts depend on a manager's decision conditional on a player's availability. For a single game the chain is: roster status (active, injured list, minors), the manager's rest and platoon policy for that day (day game after night game, catcher rest, opposing starter handedness, DH rotation), posting of the lineup card a few hours before first pitch, and the residual chance of a late scratch between posting and the first pitch. Before the card posts the probability is a mixture over the manager's patterns, after it is near one unless the player is hurt in warm-up. For windows (will he pitch between two dates) availability is a hazard process: a returning player must progress through a rehab sequence, the team must have a role and a reason (race, rest of rotation), and injury risk can end it. For return windows (will an injured player appear for his club between two dates) the same rehab hazard applies, with the minor-league rehab assignment as the last observable stage and activation from the injured list as the trigger. The edge lies in knowing the timing of information (lineup posting relative to price) and in the specific manager and player, not in team strength.

stages.name: Roster status and health gate
stages.description: A player must be on the active roster and healthy; IL placement, minor-league assignment, rehab status and day-to-day injuries set the upper bound on the probability of any participation. Injury information arrives through official transactions and beat reports and is timestamped, so the information vintage determines the model state.
stages.distribution: Mostly 0/1 with an uncertain middle for day-to-day and returning players.

stages.name: Manager's decision for the specific game
stages.description: Given health, the manager decides to start the player based on role (everyday, platoon, bench), the opposing starter's handedness, rest patterns after travel or a night game, catcher and veteran rest conventions, DH rotation and lineup construction style, and in September or when clinched, rest and prospect-call-up policy. Players on a platoon sit against same-handed starters unless exceptions apply. The opposing starter is an explicit input: his identity and hand as announced at the as-of time (with the chance he is replaced) decide platoon starts, so the start probability is a mixture over the opposing hand rather than a fixed platoon flag.
stages.distribution: Binary, with probabilities of start by role: everyday about 0.9, platoon 0.3-0.7 by opposing hand, bench near 0.1.

stages.name: Lineup posting and late-scratch hazard
stages.description: The lineup card is posted several hours before first pitch; the start market is effectively resolved then, except for the late-scratch hazard between posting and the first pitch (pregame injury, illness, warm-up). The market contract resolves No if the announced lineup changes before the game, so the late-scratch probability conditional on posting is a small but non-zero residual that depends on the player's injury status.
stages.distribution: Time-to-event: near-certain at card posting; residual probability of a scratch about 1-3% for listed starters, higher with day-to-day injuries.

stages.name: Window availability and exposure
stages.description: The pitch-in-window market integrates over games: the probability that a player records at least one pitch in a window is one minus the product of per-game non-appearance probabilities, but failures are strongly correlated through an absorbing injury state and through the team's plan, so a hazard model with injury absorption is appropriate. A rehabbing or two-way player needs a plan for pitching.
stages.distribution: Compound survival with absorption; per-game probabilities correlated; right-censored by season end.

stages.name: Return-from-injury window
stages.description: KXMLBRETURN asks whether an injured player enters any game for his named club inside a window. The chain is injury type and date, minimum injured-list duration, the rehab sequence (throwing or hitting progression, minor-league rehab assignment with its day limits), the club's activation decision given roster need and the race, and then the first game entry, which for a position player is almost immediate after activation and for a starting pitcher waits for a rotation turn. Setbacks reset the sequence, and a trade to another club would end exposure for the named club.
stages.distribution: Time-to-return with a long right tail by injury class (lognormal-like), discrete steps at rehab milestones, and a setback probability that creates a second mode well after the window.

stages.name: Starting-pitcher rotation slot
stages.description: The starting-pitcher market follows the rotation slot after off days, skipped starts, six-man or opener plans and staff injuries, with the announced probable replaced only occasionally (illness, short-notice injury, a bullpen game). It does not follow from the hitter lineup-card chain in stages s1-s3: the decision is made days earlier and announced as a probable, so the information vintage is the probable-pitcher announcement rather than the card.
stages.distribution: Near-deterministic once the slot is announced (P about 0.9 or higher) with a small change tail; before announcement a mixture over slot orderings driven by off days and rest.

stages.name: Postseason and labour-stoppage branches
stages.description: Two regimes change the manager-decision stage. In October only the round's postseason roster (26 players, reset between rounds, injured players replaceable but then ineligible for the next round) can start; there are scheduled off days, no clinch rest and almost no rest days for regulars, so start probability for everyday players approaches one and the open question is the platoon or bench slot. For 2027 windows, a lockout after the CBA expiry at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec 1 2026 would remove games from the window or the whole window; exposure is then a mixture over stoppage scenarios, and how a cancelled game settles is not stated in the sampled text.
stages.distribution: Postseason: start probability concentrated near 1 for regulars and bimodal for platoon players by opposing hand; labour branch: a point mass at zero exposure with the stoppage probability, otherwise the regular-season window.

role_personnel.note: Hitter role and platoon; pitcher rotation slot.

game_context_script.note: Standings state affects rest in September.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, congestion and clinched status in the regular season; postseason roster eligibility and the 2027 labour-stoppage regime as separate branches (stage s7).

settlement_contract.note: Official starting order, pinch hitter exclusion, window rules.

talent_strength.note: Player or team quality does not change whether a player starts except through role (starter versus bench), which is captured in the playing_time_role input; no talent estimate is needed beyond that for the participation event.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing probable starter identity, hand and announcement vintage drive platoon start decisions.

efficiency_conversion.note: Participation has no conversion rate per opportunity; the closest object is the probability that a posted lineup holds, treated as a hazard in late_scratch_hazard.

distribution_variance.note: The outcome is binary (or at least one in a window); the relevant shape is the correlation of per-game failures through injury, captured in the window exposure and rehab inputs rather than a separate distribution variable.

officiating_rules.note: No officiating factor affects whether a player starts; only roster rules (active roster size, option and IL rules) matter, which are captured in settlement and roster-move inputs.

mlb.late_scratch_hazard.label: Late-scratch hazard between lineup posting and first pitch (conditional on listed starter)
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.mechanism: A posted lineup can still change before the game for illness, injury or warm-up discomfort.
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.rationale: KXMLBSTART resolves No if the player is announced in a lineup and replaced before the game begins; the probability is low on average but elevated for players with day-to-day injuries and for catchers and pitchers.
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.measurement: Reconstruct posted-lineup vintages from MLB Stats API live-feed timecodes where available (2022-2025) and from own capture going forward; for each player in a posted lineup, event = not in the final starting order at first pitch (excluding games not played). Estimate P(event) by logistic on injury flag at post time (none, day-to-day, back from IL within 7 days), position (C, P/DH, other) and minutes between post and first pitch, with team random effect shrunk with k = 100 games. Late insertion (bench player added after posting) estimated identically. All rates are fitted values; where vintages are incomplete report covered sample size and use the league base rate with a Beta(2, 198) prior. As-of: lineup posting timestamp.
free_sources: MLB Stats API lineup changes (historical vintage unverified)
mlb.late_scratch_hazard.why: The contract's No-on-replacement rule makes this hazard a term in the price after the card posts.

mlb.rehab_progression_stage.label: Rehab progression stage and return-to-pitch/play timeline for injured players
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.mechanism: A returning player must progress through defined rehab steps before appearing, so timing depends on the stage reached.
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.rationale: Window markets such as 'will he pitch before a date' are hazard problems; the information is the rehab stage (throwing program, bullpen sessions, simulated games, minor-league rehab assignment) and the team's stated timetable.
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.measurement: Weibull survival on time from IL placement to activation by injury class (shoulder, elbow, hamstring, other) from MLB transactions 2015-2025, with covariates age, prior IL stays, and a flag for rehab assignment started (time-varying). Stages 0-3 are recorded forward by own capture and enter as covariates only after >=30 observations per class; before that, only rehab-assignment status is used. Class parameters shrunk to the overall Weibull with k = 10 players. P(appear in window) = P(activation before window end | survived to as-of) x P(used within window | active), the latter from the team's last 30 days of relief or start usage for the same role. Units: probability. As-of: latest dated report.
raw_data: IL transactions with dates and injury type
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.why: KXMLBPITCH and similar windows depend on rehab timing rather than games played.

mlb.window_exposure_schedule.label: Window exposure: games, off days, doubleheaders and role-probability per game within the window
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.mechanism: A multi-game window aggregates per-game participation probabilities with schedule structure.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.rationale: P(at least one) in a window depends on the number of team games remaining (off days, doubleheaders, postponement) and on the team's usage pattern; a two-way player's pitching is limited by rotation turns.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.measurement: N = number of team games in the window from the official schedule (adjust for postponement probability from mlb.forecast_precip_timing). Per-game participation p_g: hitters from mlb.playing_time_role start probability, pitchers from mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest P(start on date) plus relief-appearance rate for relievers. P(healthy through g) = (1 - h)^g with per-game injury hazard h from mlb.injuries_pit shrunk to league by age/role (k = 100 player-seasons). P(at least one) = 1 - prod_g (1 - p_g x P(healthy through g)); multiply by (1 - clinched rest factor) from mlb.clinched_rest_policy after the clinch date. Units: probability. As-of: daily.
raw_data: schedule with dates, rotation order, off days
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.why: Converts single-game probabilities to window-level probability with correct correlation structure.

mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.label: Starting-pitcher rotation slot, days of rest, off-day skipping and announced-probable status
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.mechanism: A pitcher starts when his rotation turn arrives after the club's off days, injuries and bullpen days, and when the announced probable is not replaced.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.rationale: KXMLBSTARTER-type markets depend on the rotation: position in the five-man (or six-man) order, days since the last start, whether the club will skip him around an off day, opener or bullpen-game usage, staff injuries and the probable-pitcher announcement vintage. Hitter lineup-card inputs (platoon, catcher rest, DH rotation) do not describe it.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.measurement: For each pitcher compute (a) days_rest = game date - last start date, (b) expected next-start date = last start + 5 days adjusted for scheduled off days using the team's last 3 seasons of skip rate on off days (shrunk k = 20 team-off-days), (c) probable-pitcher announcement flag with timestamp and the historical change rate by days-to-game (own capture), (d) opener/bullpen-game rate of the team over the last 30 days. Output P(start on date d) = P(slot lands on d) x P(no change | announced). As-of: announcement time; before announcement the slot-based prior.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule hydrate probablePitcher and game logs
raw_data: start log with dates and rest
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.why: Gives the starting-pitcher participation market a rotation-based mechanism instead of the hitter lineup chain.

mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.label: Call-up pipeline: 40-man status, option years, service-time and roster-need signals for a first MLB appearance
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.mechanism: A debut requires 40-man roster addition, a roster vacancy or injury need, and a club decision informed by prospect readiness and service-time incentives.
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.rationale: KXMLBDEBUT cannot be modelled by lineup inputs: it depends on whether the player is on the 40-man, whether a need exists at his position, the club's service-time and Rule 5/waiver considerations, minor-league performance and September roster rules. The date of the market window determines which of these dominates.
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.measurement: For each prospect-day 2015-2025 compute: on_40man flag, option years remaining, MiLB OPS (hitters) or FIP (pitchers) relative to the level mean over the last 120 PA or 40 IP, age relative to level median, position_need = clip(1 - team projected MLB WAR at the position / league-average WAR at that position, 0, 1) from FanGraphs depth charts, active IL count at the position, days left in the roster window, an extra-service-year flag (days still needed to avoid a year of service before the Super Two cutoff), and a September-roster indicator. Fit a discrete-time logistic hazard of first MLB appearance per day with team random effect shrunk with k = 5 team-years. Output P(debut before date t) = 1 - prod over days of (1 - h_d). All covariates as of the snapshot day only.
free_sources: MLB Stats API transactions and rosters
raw_data: depth charts and IL status by date
mlb.callup_eligibility_pipeline.why: Defined here when KXMLBDEBUT was filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation the debut market is in transactions, which stages this input.

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.label: Labour-stoppage regime: CBA expiry (Dec 1 2026), lockout flag and expected end, and transaction freeze rules
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.mechanism: A lockout freezes 40-man roster transactions and free-agent signings, turning a window into a pre-expiry rush, a frozen interval of unknown length and a post-deal rush.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.rationale: The 2022 CBA expires at 11:59 pm ET on Dec 1 2026 and a lockout is widely reported as likely; in 2021-22 the lockout froze 40-man transactions from Dec 2 until Mar 10 2022. A next-team market closing Mar 25 2027 and any call-up or opening-day contract in 2027 are therefore mixtures over stoppage length, and 15 years of calendar hazard history include only one such stoppage.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.measurement: State variables: days to CBA expiry, lockout flag, days since lockout start, reported negotiation status (own capture of timestamped reports coded into ordinal stage 0-4). Model the stoppage length L with a survival model whose prior is built from the 1994-95, 2021-22 and 1990 stoppages (3 events, heavy shrinkage) and updated by negotiation stage; apply the freeze: hazard of any 40-man transaction = 0 during lockout, with a post-agreement rush multiple estimated from March 2022 (units: multiple of baseline hazard). Output P(freeze covers date d) and the adjusted calendar hazard. As-of: daily.
raw_data: CBA expiry date and labour news timeline
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.why: Any 2027 KXMLBSTART, KXMLBSTARTER or KXMLBPITCH window depends on whether games are played: the CBA expires 11:59 p.m. ET Dec 1 2026 and a lockout that cancels games removes exposure from the window (the contract treatment of cancelled games is unseen).

mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.label: Postseason roster eligibility between rounds: injured-player replacement, roster resets and who can be on the series roster
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.mechanism: Each series has its own submitted roster, so an injured player may return or be replaced between rounds, which changes team strength round by round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.rationale: A team's strength entering the league championship series is not the same roster as in the division series; hitters and pitchers can be swapped between rounds under league rules. This matters for hosting-count markets that span several rounds and for any series where injuries occur in the previous round.
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.measurement: For each team and round: Delta = sum over players added of projected rest-of-season WAR per 150 games (ZiPS/Steamer average) times expected playing-time share, minus the same for players removed from the prior-round roster; unconfirmed injured players enter with probability p = P(activated by deadline) from mlb.rehab_progression_stage rather than as a flag. Convert Delta to runs per game (wins/10). Log submitted rosters by round 2012-2025 from MLB transactions to estimate the base rate of injured-list replacements per round. Units: runs per game. As-of: roster submission deadline and public injury reports available at the snapshot.
free_sources: MLB transactions page and postseason roster announcements (free_scrape)
mlb.postseason_roster_reset_eligibility.why: The sampled single-game start markets are October playoff games; only players on that round's postseason roster can start, and rosters are reset between rounds with injury replacements, so eligibility gates the start decision in the postseason branch.

mlb.opposing_probable_starter_vintage.label: Opposing probable starter identity, throwing hand and announcement timestamp, with the probability the listed starter changes
mlb.opposing_probable_starter_vintage.mechanism: Managers bench platoon hitters against same-handed starters, so whether a part-time player starts is decided by the opposing probable starter's throwing hand as it is known at the time, and changes if that starter is replaced.
mlb.opposing_probable_starter_vintage.rationale: Platoon status alone says a player sits against left-handers; it does not say who is pitching or when that became known. Probables are announced days ahead and occasionally change (scratch, opener, bullpen day), and a change of hand flips platoon starts for several hitters at once, so the start probability before the card posts must be a mixture over the opposing starter's hand with its announcement vintage.
mlb.opposing_probable_starter_vintage.measurement: Snapshot the MLB Stats API schedule (hydrate=probablePitcher) every 30 minutes from 3 days before first pitch; per game and team store probable pitcher id, pitchHand code (L/R), first-seen timestamp and each change. At as-of time t: P(opp hand = L) = (1 - P(change)) * I(listed hand = L) + P(change) * share of left-handers in the replacement distribution, with P(change) and the replacement distribution taken from mlb.f5_starter_change_risk at the same t; before any probable is listed use the rotation order from mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest. For each hitter, P(start | hand) comes from his manager-specific start rates against LHP and RHP over the last 2 seasons (shrunk to his role class with k = 30 games per hand); P(start) = sum over hands of P(hand) * P(start | hand). Units: probability; as-of the snapshot time, using only announcements visible then.
free_sources: MLB Stats API statsapi.mlb.com /api/v1/schedule?hydrate=probablePitcher (probable pitcher and pitchHand)

mlb.opposing_probable_starter_vintage.why: For platoon and part-time hitters the opposing starter's hand is the single biggest driver of a KXMLBSTART outcome before the card posts, and its vintage determines what was knowable when the market traded.

mlb.lineup_pit.reason: The lineup card is the resolving event for start markets; vintage and posting time matter and replacement after posting resolves No.

mlb.playing_time_role.reason: Starter versus platoon versus bench role is the strongest prior for start probability before the card posts.

mlb.rest_day_patterns.reason: Day-after-night, catcher and veteran rest patterns are manager-specific and highly predictive.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: IL and day-to-day status gate participation and set the scratch hazard; timestamps must be as-of.

mlb.team_style.reason: Manager substitution and platoon style; partially redundant with rest_day_patterns and platoon.

mlb.rest_travel.reason: Schedule density and doubleheaders; overlaps rest_day_patterns.

mlb.platoon.reason: Opposing starter hand drives platoon sits for part-time players; no effect for everyday players.

mlb.news.reason: Beat reports precede transactions and injury changes; credibility varies by source.

m.rules_text.reason: Distinguishes the starting-order and pitch-window wording; the 'announced then replaced resolves No' clause is decisive and the truncated KXMLBSTART text must be re-read in full.

m.lifecycle.reason: Lineup posting time versus market close determines the information state but is not an input to the event.

mlb.clinched_rest_policy.reason: Clinched or eliminated teams rest regulars and call up prospects; large late-season effect on participation.

interactions.mechanism: A platoon player sits against same-handed starters and rests after night games, so start probability is a conditional product of role, opposing hand and rest pattern; for everyday players only the rest pattern matters, so the effect of handedness is gated by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit start logistic with role x hand x rest-day terms and compare calibration by role.

interactions.mechanism: Before the card posts the probability is a mixture of manager patterns, after posting it collapses to the scratch hazard; the transition is a step in time at posting, so the value of information is concentrated at posting relative to market close.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model error before and after the observed posting timestamp for historical games.

interactions.mechanism: Window availability is a survival process: rehab stage determines time to activation, injury hazard after activation determines early failure, and the number of games available determines how many opportunities there are; failures across games are correlated through the absorbing state.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate window-level probability with and without correlated absorption; compare to naive product of per-game probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: After a team clinches a seed or is eliminated, rest probability switches regime: regulars sit and prospects play, with the size of the switch depending on the manager's style and on whether seeding still matters; before clinching the baseline pattern applies.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate start probability by standings state (clinched/eliminated) and manager; test the discontinuity at clinching date.

interactions.mechanism: Role changes (call-up, trade, injury replacement) announced by news shift start probability at a discrete date, so the window model must restart its per-game probabilities at the change; the number of games after the change drives the window probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Segment games by role-change date and compare window predictions with piecewise versus constant role probabilities.

interactions.mechanism: For a returning starting pitcher the window market is Yes only if activation comes early enough for a rotation turn inside the window: activation two days before the window ends may produce no appearance if his slot falls after it, whereas a position player activated the same day usually enters at once, so the same rehab stage implies different window probabilities by role.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare days from activation to first appearance for starters versus position players and relievers in injured-list returns since 2015.

interactions.mechanism: The opposing hand moves start probability only for hitters whose role is platoon or part-time: an everyday regular starts against either hand, a strong-side platoon bat sits against same-handed starters, so a late switch from a right-hander to a left-hander flips several start markets on one team at once and leaves the regulars unchanged.
interactions.how_to_test: On games where the probable changed hand after announcement, compare realised starts of platoon versus everyday hitters against predictions using the original versus the updated hand.

interactions.mechanism: Rest-day and clinch-rest patterns fitted on the regular season switch off in the postseason: rosters are round-specific, off days replace rest days and managers start regulars every game, so applying regular-season rest rates to October games understates start probability for regulars and overstates it for bench players left off the round roster.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit start probability on postseason games separately and compare coefficients on rest-day features with the regular-season fit; check calibration of the regular-season model on 2021-2025 postseason starts.

nonlinearities.shape: Small base rate with threshold increase for day-to-day injuries
nonlinearities.why: Probability is near zero for healthy players and rises sharply with a recorded day-to-day designation, so a linear effect misses the regime.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function by stage with right-skewed durations
nonlinearities.why: Progress through rehab stages is discrete and the time to the next stage is skewed by setbacks, so timing is not smooth in elapsed days.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in number of games: 1 - prod(1 - p) saturates with exposure
nonlinearities.why: With many games available, additional games add little to P(at least one); with few games, each adds a lot.

nonlinearities.shape: Regime step at clinching or elimination date
nonlinearities.why: Rest policy changes discontinuously at the point stakes disappear.

contract.settlement_definition: Four live series after the reconciliation. KXMLBTRADE (rules sampled): Yes if the named player is traded before the date; 'The trade must be officially processed and approved by MLB' before the date, and a trade later rescinded or voided by a failed physical after official processing still resolves Yes. KXMLBNEXTTEAM (rules sampled): one market per team plus 'Retires / No Team'; a player who remains on his issuance team on the date resolves for that team, a free agent who 'signs a contract with any team, including their previous team' resolves for that team, an extension or re-signing while under contract does not trigger early resolution, and retirement or no team on the date resolves Retires/No Team (text truncated after that). KXMLBDEBUT (rules sampled): Yes if the named prospect 'plays for any MLB team in a regular season or playoff game' before the date (Nov 1, 2028 in the sample); what counts as playing (pinch-running, defensive replacement) is not defined. KXMLBCOACH (next manager) is title-only. The draft-pick market moved to the amateur-draft archetype. Whether NEXTTEAM waits for an official announcement, and how a failed physical affects a signing, is not stated (see tr_settlement_assumed).

rules_evidence.quote: signs a contract with any team, including their previous team, the market for that team will resolve Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: A free agent re-signing with his old team resolves for that team; any signing during free agency counts.

rules_evidence.quote: If Ronald Acuna remains on the team they were on upon issuance on Mar 25, 2027, then the market for that team will resolve Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Status quo at the date resolves for the current team, so the no-move probability sits on one strike.

rules_evidence.quote: plays for any MLB team in a regular season or playoff game before Nov 1, 2028
rules_evidence.establishes: Debut counts regular-season and playoff appearances for any club, over a multi-season window.

rules_evidence.quote: The trade must be officially processed and approved by MLB before Aug 5, 2026 for market to resolve to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Trade markets settle on official league processing before the deadline, so a reported agreement that is processed after the date resolves No.

rules_evidence.quote: If Paul Skenes later fails their physical and/or the trade is rescinded for any reason after being officially processed, the market nonetheless resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Post-processing failures do not reverse a Yes, so the failure-mode stage applies before official processing only.

variants_and_edge_cases: Next-team: a player who stays with his team resolves Yes for that team at the date, a free agent who signs elsewhere resolves for the new team; extensions while under contract do not resolve early.

Announcement and physicals: for trades the text requires official MLB processing before the date and keeps a Yes even if the trade is later rescinded or a physical is failed; for NEXTTEAM the text says only 'signs a contract with any team' and is silent on announcement, physicals or voiding, so the trade rule cannot be assumed to carry over (see tr_settlement_assumed).
Manager markets: the next manager of a team requires a hire announcement, and interim managers are an edge case not covered in the sample.
Deadline structure: trade-deadline, non-tender, qualifying offer and Rule 5 dates create calendar clusters where the market window includes or excludes them.
Debut: the window spans more than two seasons and any club counts, so a trade does not reset the clock; whether a pinch-running or defensive-only appearance counts as 'plays' is undefined.

Trade window (KXMLBTRADE): the sampled date (Aug 5, 2026) presumably falls just after the 2026 trade deadline (deadline date not verified here), so nearly all mass would sit in deadline week; no-trade clauses, 10-and-5 rights and club control years shape feasibility, and processing lag on deadline day decides borderline cases.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official team or league transaction announcements (MLB transactions log); not named in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: Transactions follow institutional calendars and incentives, so the event is a time-to-event process with hazards that change by date and context. For trades, a seller with a short-contract player is likely to deal near the deadline and the buyer-seller status of the team is driven by playoff probability and payroll; for free-agent signings, contract expiry, qualifying-offer decisions, positional market and team payroll space drive timing, with most signings clustered in the first weeks of free agency and again at the winter meetings; for manager changes, tenure, team underperformance relative to expectations, owner statements and contract status matter. Beat-writer reports precede most official moves, with source credibility varying; the contract resolves on the official announcement, so lead times and process failures (physicals, vetoes) matter. There is little statistical structure in team performance beyond its effect on incentives, so the best-supported approach is reference-class hazard modelling updated by timestamped reports. The trade market (KXMLBTRADE) settles on official MLB processing before the date and ignores later rescissions, so the relevant process ends at league approval, not at a physical. After the reconciliation the archetype also holds the prospect-debut market, a hazard over the call-up pipeline, and a next-manager market; the draft-pick market moved to its own archetype.

stages.name: Eligibility and constraints
stages.description: A transaction requires that the player or manager is eligible: contract expiry or opt-out for free agency, service time and 40-man status for call-ups and trades, no-trade protections and 10-and-5 rights, club options, and the qualifying offer system. The constraint set determines which events are possible at all and when.
stages.distribution: Binary feasibility gating with time-varying eligibility dates.

stages.name: Team incentives and finances
stages.description: Buyer or seller status depends on playoff probability and distance to contention; payroll and luxury-tax thresholds constrain the ability to add salary; managers are fired when expectations are missed and the organization is willing to pay a replacement. Incentives are partly observable from standings and projections.
stages.distribution: Continuous incentive index with threshold behaviour at playoff-odds boundaries.

stages.name: Calendar and process timing
stages.description: Transaction hazards are not constant: trade deadline day, the end-of-season window, the non-tender and qualifying-offer deadlines, the winter meetings, the Rule 5 draft and the start of spring training concentrate events on known dates. Process steps (negotiation, medical review, league processing) add lags between agreement and official processing; for the trade market only processing before the date counts, so deadline-day agreements processed late are the boundary cases.
stages.distribution: Piecewise-constant hazard with spikes at calendar anchors; lag distribution from agreement to official.

stages.name: Information flow and report credibility
stages.description: Credible reporters often announce agreements hours or days before official announcements; the probability of eventual official completion given a report depends on the report's wording ('close to', 'agreed', 'pending physical') and on the reporter's track record. Prices respond to reports, so the quantity of interest is the posterior given report text and source.
stages.distribution: Bayesian update with source-specific likelihood ratios; most information arrives in discrete jumps.

stages.name: Resolution wording and failure modes
stages.description: Contracts resolve on events meeting specified conditions, and the wording differs by series: a trade counts once officially processed and approved by MLB before the date and stays Yes even if later rescinded or voided by a failed physical, whereas the next-team text is silent on announcement, physicals and voiding. Remaining failure modes before official processing include a collapsed negotiation, a player using no-trade rights, a sign-and-trade, or processing that lands after the market date.
stages.distribution: Absorbing event with a small pre-processing failure mass after a report; zero post-processing failure mass for trades by rule; wording determines edge cases.

stages.name: Destination or candidate selection and labour regime
stages.description: After eligibility and timing, a free agent chooses among teams and a club chooses among manager candidates, so the market object is a categorical choice shaped by positional need, competing bids, market size and preferences; independently, a CBA lockout beginning after Dec 1 2026 would freeze transactions for an unknown time, making any window that spans the expiry a mixture over stoppage length.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice with a few credible destinations and a long tail; stoppage length is a heavy-tailed mixture with zero-length (no lockout) mass.

stages.name: Debut and next-manager events
stages.description: A debut before a multi-year deadline is a hazard over the call-up pipeline (40-man status, options, minor-league performance, positional need and service-time incentives), not a lineup decision; any club counts, so a trade does not reset it. The next-manager market first needs a vacancy, which depends on the incumbent's firing hazard (tenure, underperformance versus expectation, contract status), and then is a selection among named candidates driven by interview reports and front-office ties.
stages.distribution: Debut: right-skewed time-to-event with spikes at September and injury call-ups and near-certain mass for top prospects; manager: vacancy hazard followed by a categorical choice with a front-runner.

role_personnel.note: Contract and eligibility, call-up pipeline and manager candidate selection.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed stage durations and a lockout mixture; the weak all-family base rate is no longer claimed.

settlement_contract.note: Official processing before the date for trades (rescission after processing still Yes), status-quo and re-signing clauses for next team, any-club debut definition.

opponent_matchup.note: Competing bidders and positional need decide which team signs the player.

environment.note: Venue, weather and altitude do not affect transaction timing; location of a team may affect free agent preferences only weakly and is not measurable in a way a market can price.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume of opportunities in a transaction event; the quantity analogous to pace is the calendar hazard rate, included under calendar timing.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate per opportunity applies; the nearest object is the stage conversion from report to official announcement, included as report credibility.

officiating_rules.note: CBA windows, lockout freezes and service-time rules are the rule regime of transactions.

mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.label: Contract status and service clock (expiry, options, opt-outs, no-trade, qualifying-offer eligibility)
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.mechanism: Transactions are possible only when contractual and CBA conditions allow them.
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.rationale: A player's free-agency status, club or player option, no-trade protection, arbitration status and service time determine the set and timing of feasible events; 'next team' markets differ sharply for players under contract versus free agents.
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.measurement: Per player build a record: contract_end_year, AAV, option type (club/player/mutual) with decision date, opt-out dates, no-trade clause (full/partial), 10-and-5 status (10 MLB years and 5 with current club), arbitration year (pre-arb, arb 1-3, Super Two) and service days at date (172 days = 1 year). qualifying_offer_eligible = final contract year AND never previously received a QO AND on the same club for the full season prior to free agency. When providers disagree, use the provider with the latest timestamp before the snapshot and set a source_conflict flag. Output boolean flags and dates. As-of: contract data timestamp before the snapshot.
raw_data: player contract table: years, AAV, options, opt-outs, no-trade clauses, service days
mlb.contract_status_and_service_clock.why: Defines feasibility and timing, which are first-order for next-team markets.

mlb.news_source_reliability_score.label: Source-level reliability: P(official | report type) from historical reports
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.mechanism: Not all reports are equal; some reporters' 'agreement reached' items are nearly always followed by official moves.
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.rationale: Market reaction to reports is only warranted if the posterior given the source and wording exceeds the market's pricing; track record and wording ('close', 'agreed', 'pending physical') strongly change completion probability.
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.measurement: For each reporter-source and wording class compute historical fraction of reports that led to the official event within 14 days (Beta posterior with prior from class average, k = 10 reports) and distribution of lead time. Output P(official by date) and expected lead. As-of: report timestamp. Units: probability and days.
free_sources: social media archives (unavailable_public via API limits)
raw_data: report-level: reporter/source, text, timestamp, wording class
official transaction date from MLB transactions feed
mlb.news_source_reliability_score.why: Provides the likelihood ratio for the most important information type.

mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.label: Calendar hazard function by transaction type (trade, free-agent signing, extension, manager hire)
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.mechanism: Hazard of each event type is concentrated on known dates.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.rationale: Using a flat per-day rate misprices markets that straddle deadlines and meeting dates; for example, a large share of free-agent signings occur in specific off-season windows and trade completions spike near the deadline.
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.measurement: From 2010-2025 MLB transactions, for each type define the eligible stock on day d: trades = 40-man players not on a long-term IL; FA signings = unsigned free agents; extensions = players with 1-2 years of control left; manager hires = open vacancies. Daily hazard h(d) = events on d / eligible stock at d. Fit a Poisson log-linear model h(d) = exp(a_type + sum_k b_k * anchor_k(d) + season trend) with anchors (trade deadline +-7 days, winter meetings week, non-tender day, spring training start, opening day); shrink each b_k toward its pooled across-type value with k = 3 seasons. Lockout days (2021-12-02 to 2022-03-10) are excluded from the fit and set to structural zero for 40-man transactions. Output h(d) for the window dates and survival to the window end. As-of: current eligible stock.
raw_data: calendar anchors (deadline, winter meetings, non-tender day, spring training start)
mlb.calendar_hazard_by_event_type.why: Gives time-conditioned base rates instead of one reference-class rate.

mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.label: Competitive-balance-tax and payroll headroom for the acquiring team
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.mechanism: Finance constrains who can absorb salary.
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.rationale: Teams near luxury-tax thresholds or with stated payroll limits are much less likely to add salary; headroom also determines trade behaviour.
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.measurement: Headroom_t = CBT base threshold for the season (published CBA figure) - projected CBT payroll_t, where CBT payroll = sum of average annual values of contracts of players on the 40-man roster or IL on the determination date (last day of the regular season) + player benefits (published league figure for the season). Also output tier indicators: over tier 1 (base), tier 2 (+$20M), tier 3 (+$40M), tier 4 (+$60M), with tier values verified against the CBA text. Owner-stated budget is not used. Units: dollars and flags. As-of: latest transaction in the contract tracker before the snapshot.
raw_data: team payroll table: AAV by contract, 40-man roster, benefits
CBT thresholds and tiers from the CBA
mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom.why: Explains who can sign or trade for salary and so conditions signing and trade probabilities.

mlb.manager_firing_hazard.label: Manager seat heat: tenure, underperformance vs expectation, contract expiry and owner statements
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.mechanism: Managers are removed when results fall short of expectations and the owner or front office is willing to act.
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.rationale: Next-manager markets resolve on a hiring event preceded by a vacancy; the vacancy hazard depends on wins below projection, contract status, front-office change and public statements.
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.measurement: Hazard = logistic on (wins - preseason projected wins) per 162, tenure years, contract years remaining (<=1 flag), prior-year playoff flag, recent front-office change, and winning percentage trailing 30 games; calibrate on 20 years of mid-season and off-season manager changes (shrink k = 3 seasons). Units: probability of vacancy before date. As-of: current day.
raw_data: manager-season table: team results, contract status, change events
mlb.manager_firing_hazard.why: The vacancy hazard is the first stage of next-manager contracts.

mlb.destination_selection_signal.label: Destination or candidate selection signal: positional need, competing bidders, market size, player preference and qualifying-offer status (players); interview pool and executive connections (managers)
mlb.destination_selection_signal.mechanism: KXMLBNEXTTEAM and KXMLBCOACH resolve one market per team or candidate, so the outcome is a categorical choice, not just whether a transaction occurs.
mlb.destination_selection_signal.rationale: Eligibility and timing hazards say when a move happens but not where: the signing team depends on roster need at the player's position, who can afford him, market size and ownership spending, the player's stated preferences or hometown ties, whether his old team made a qualifying offer, and for managers the interview pool and ties to the decision maker. The existing payroll-headroom input does not carry competing bids.
mlb.destination_selection_signal.measurement: Scope: free-agent player destination (managers use mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal). For free agent f and team t at the snapshot: need_t = max(0, 1 - projected WAR of the incumbent at f's position / league mean WAR at that position) from FanGraphs depth charts; afford_t = clip((tax threshold - projected CBT payroll)/projected_AAV_f, 0, 1) with projected AAV from a public pre-signing projection, never the signed contract; reported_t = distinct outlets in own timestamped capture naming t as interested, shrunk with k = 2 reports; large_market_t = top-10 market indicator; prior_team and qualifying-offer flags. Fit a conditional logit over 30 teams on FA classes 2012-2025 with team effects shrunk (k = 3 signings). Output P(destination = t | signs before date). Only reports before the snapshot.
raw_data: team payroll and depth charts at signing time
mlb.destination_selection_signal.why: Adds the selection stage the record lacked: the markets are one-per-team and one-per-candidate.

mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.label: Labour-stoppage regime: CBA expiry (Dec 1 2026), lockout flag and expected end, and transaction freeze rules
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.mechanism: A lockout freezes 40-man roster transactions and free-agent signings, turning a window into a pre-expiry rush, a frozen interval of unknown length and a post-deal rush.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.rationale: The 2022 CBA expires at 11:59 pm ET on Dec 1 2026 and a lockout is widely reported as likely; in 2021-22 the lockout froze 40-man transactions from Dec 2 until Mar 10 2022. A next-team market closing Mar 25 2027 and any call-up or opening-day contract in 2027 are therefore mixtures over stoppage length, and 15 years of calendar hazard history include only one such stoppage.
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.measurement: State variables: days to CBA expiry, lockout flag, days since lockout start, reported negotiation status (own capture of timestamped reports coded into ordinal stage 0-4). Model the stoppage length L with a survival model whose prior is built from the 1994-95, 2021-22 and 1990 stoppages (3 events, heavy shrinkage) and updated by negotiation stage; apply the freeze: hazard of any 40-man transaction = 0 during lockout, with a post-agreement rush multiple estimated from March 2022 (units: multiple of baseline hazard). Output P(freeze covers date d) and the adjusted calendar hazard. As-of: daily.
raw_data: CBA expiry date and labour news timeline
mlb.labor_stoppage_regime.why: Adds the missing labour-stoppage regime for transactions whose windows span Dec 1 2026.

mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.label: Draft prospect selection signal: consensus board rank, signability and reported team links for a given pick slot
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.mechanism: Which player a club takes at a slot follows the consensus ranking adjusted for club preference, bonus-pool strategy (underslot deals) and signability, with late reports of pre-draft agreements.
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.rationale: A draft-pick market resolves on an identity or slot, so the input must turn public rankings and reported links into a selection probability; the bonus-pool system makes underslot picks common at the top, so rank alone mis-prices.
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.measurement: For each prospect and slot j: average rank across public boards (MLB Pipeline, Baseball America, FanGraphs) at the as-of date; signability flag (college senior, high-school commitment strength); reported links per club from timestamped mock drafts and reports (count of independent outlets). Fit a conditional-logit choice model per slot on 2012-2025 drafts with club-level shrinkage (k = 5 drafts); P(player at slot) chained over earlier slots by sequential sampling. Units: probability. As-of: timestamp of the latest board and report; lottery outcome as a conditioning input for slot ownership.
free_sources: MLB Pipeline and FanGraphs draft boards (free_scrape)
mlb.draft_prospect_selection_signal.why: Defined here while KXMLBDRAFTPICK was filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation that series is in the amateur-draft archetype, which has no review yet; kept so the definition is not lost, not staged here.

mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.label: Manager-hire candidate selection signal: interview reports, candidate pool, internal/external status and executive connections
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.mechanism: Given a vacancy, the hire is a selection among candidates driven by reported interviews, prior relationships with the deciding executive and organizational preference for internal or experienced candidates.
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.rationale: A next-manager market pays per candidate, so identity-level signals matter more than timing or base rates: a reported finalist who worked with the president of baseball operations is far likelier than a name on a speculative list, and reports lead the official announcement.
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.measurement: For each vacancy and candidate record (a) reported interview flag and number of independent outlets reporting it, (b) internal-vs-external flag, (c) years of shared employment with the deciding executive, (d) prior managerial years, (e) days since the vacancy. Fit a conditional-logit selection model over the candidate set on all MLB vacancies 2010-2025 with candidate-level shrinkage (k = 3 vacancies); output selection share per candidate times P(hire announced before the market close). As-of: timestamp of each report; only reports published before the quote time are used.
free_sources: Beat-reporter and national-outlet reports (own timestamped capture)
raw_data: vacancy log with dates and outcomes
mlb.manager_candidate_selection_signal.why: KXMLBCOACH (next manager, filed here) is a selection among reported candidates for a vacancy; interview reports, internal status and executive ties drive the choice in stage s7.

mlb.roster_moves.reason: Transaction log is the ground truth feed; as a raw feed it is not a driver without hazard modelling.

mlb.seller_buyer_status.reason: Buyer/seller incentives drive trades and destinations; the 'playoff odds' in its definition must come from the project's own season simulation (mlb.season_sim) or a projection system, never from futures or sportsbook prices, which are benchmarks.

mlb.service_time_rules.reason: Option, 40-man and Rule 5 constraints define feasibility windows; partially covered by contract status.

mlb.news.reason: Reports precede official moves; value depends on source credibility.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: Injuries trigger IL moves and call-ups and shape trade behaviour.

mlb.season_sim.reason: Playoff probability from season simulation is what drives buyer/seller status, so it duplicates seller_buyer_status already in use here and is a source, not a separate input.

mlb.offfield_base_rate.reason: One reference class for heterogeneous events is inadequate; a time-conditioned hazard per event type is needed. No longer used in coverage or data feeds.

m.rules_text.reason: Status-quo resolution, re-signing and extension clauses (NEXTTEAM) and the any-club, any-game debut definition determine the event; COACH and DRAFTPICK wording is unseen.

m.quote_history.reason: Price reaction to reports is a market response, only useful to evaluate report credibility. Removed from stage s5 inputs and data feeds.

interactions.mechanism: A seller with an expiring contract in the final weeks before the deadline has a trade hazard that is the product of team status (seller), player contract (expiring, tradable) and calendar proximity, so none of these alone predicts a trade; each multiplies the daily hazard.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit Cox hazard with interaction of seller status, expiring contract and days to deadline.

interactions.mechanism: The completion probability given a report depends on wording and source, and on whether the rules count only the official announcement; a credible 'pending physical' report implies high probability of completion within days but not certainty. The official-versus-report distinction is an assumption about settlement until the full rules are read.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate completion probability by source-wording class and time since report.

interactions.mechanism: Payroll headroom acts as a threshold: teams near the tax line are very unlikely to add salary beyond it, so a free-agent signing probability for that team is near zero until headroom exceeds the contract's annual value; contract structure shifts the effective threshold.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate signing probability by headroom to AAV ratio and test discontinuity near zero headroom.

interactions.mechanism: Managers are fired in-season mainly when the team is out of contention, and in the offseason after the season ends; the hazard regime switches at the end of the season, and the next-manager market depends on a vacancy created in the first regime or second.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hazard in regular season versus offseason and test dependence on playoff odds.

interactions.mechanism: Injury-driven call-ups and IL moves are constrained by roster and option rules, so the number of available call-up slots and the date relative to roster expansions changes the hazard in steps.
interactions.how_to_test: Segment history by roster-rule regime and compare call-up rates.

interactions.mechanism: During a lockout the signing hazard is zero and the destination choice cannot resolve; after an agreement the pent-up signings arrive in a rush on compressed calendar anchors, so the probability a named destination wins before March 25 2027 equals P(lockout ends in time) times the post-deal destination share.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare March 2022 signing rate and destination shares with the pre-lockout December 2021 rush and with ordinary years.

interactions.mechanism: On deadline day many agreements are reported in the final hour, and the trade market counts only those officially processed before the date; a credible report of an agreed deal minutes before the deadline converts to Yes only if processing lands in time, and players with no-trade or 10-and-5 rights add a consent step that can push completion past the cutoff.
interactions.how_to_test: For deadline-day trades since 2015, compare report timestamps with official processing times and estimate the share of late-reported deals that miss the cutoff, split by no-trade status.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise-constant spikes at calendar anchors
nonlinearities.why: Events cluster around fixed dates, so cumulative probability over a window is a step-like function of window placement.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in playoff odds (illustrative author guess near 10-20%, to be estimated) where teams flip from buyers to sellers
nonlinearities.why: Teams behave discontinuously around the contention boundary, so a linear function of playoff odds misprices behaviour.

nonlinearities.shape: Beta-posterior shrinkage with source report count
nonlinearities.why: Reliability is estimated from few reports per source, so posterior probability depends nonlinearly on counts.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at zero headroom
nonlinearities.why: Teams avoid crossing tax lines, so signing probability collapses near and below zero headroom.
