contract.settlement_definition: Fifty-five live series of season-long team outcomes after the reconciliation; all but KXMLBWS (title-only) have sampled rules. Team win-total ladders (KXMLBWINS-<TEAM>, all thirty teams) pay Yes if the team has at least N wins in the 2026 regular season ('Ties do not count as wins'); division winners pay on the 2026 division title; pennant (KXMLBAL, KXMLBNL), World Series and champion-division/league futures pay on the title, with division or league affiliation fixed 'when that championship begins'; qualifier markets (NLCSQUAL, ALCSQUAL, PLAYOFFS) pay if the team reaches that stage; KXMLBSEEDWIN pays if a team holding the named seed at the start of the postseason wins the championship; KXMLBMATCHUP resolves 'immediately upon qualification' of the named pairing; KXMLBWSOUTCOME pays on the exact winner and runner-up. Season extremes: best and worst record by winning percentage ($1/N rounded down to the cent on ties, no tiebreakers), longest winning and losing streaks ($1/N on shared streaks), and 100+ losses (no tie branch). KXMLBWORLD pays on the World Baseball Classic winner (2026 tournament). KXMLB includes a 2027 championship future that depends on a 2027 season being played after the CBA expires on Dec 1 2026. No text names a source or addresses a cancelled or shortened season.

rules_evidence.quote: If Chicago C has 95+ wins in the 2026 pro baseball team regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Win-total markets are N+ ladders on regular-season wins only (playoffs excluded).

rules_evidence.quote: Ties do not count as wins.
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties are excluded from wins; in MLB all regular-season games end with a winner, so this matters for suspended or cancelled games only.

rules_evidence.quote: The seed designation is fixed at the start of the postseason and does not change as teams advance.
rules_evidence.establishes: Seed futures key off the initial seeding, tying probability to the bracket structure and tiebreaker-determined seeds.

rules_evidence.quote: a team designated as a 6 seed in either the American League or National League at the start of the postseason wins the Pro Baseball Championship
rules_evidence.establishes: A seed contract pays if either league's team with that seed wins the title, so it is a union of two teams' championship events.

rules_evidence.quote: If two or more teams share the longest winning streak (i.e., they have win streaks of the same length, and no other team has a longer one), then the markets for each of those tied teams will resolve to $1/(the number of tied teams), rounded down.
rules_evidence.establishes: The streak market is an extreme-value event with a tie-split payout, so the expected payout needs the probability of sharing as well as of leading outright.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution occurs immediately upon qualification, not when the game is actually played.
rules_evidence.establishes: Matchup markets settle on bracket qualification, so they are a function of division-series outcomes and bracket structure only.

rules_evidence.quote: If Texas is the 2026 Pro Baseball AL West Division Winner, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Division-winner futures, moved here from the moneyline archetype, settle on the final division title.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington wins the 2027 Pro Baseball Championship, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: At least one live championship future refers to the 2027 season, so labour-stoppage risk enters directly.

rules_evidence.quote: If either team is eliminated from contention for its specified role, the market resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Exact-outcome markets need both teams' bracket paths jointly, not each team's title probability.

rules_evidence.quote: Any postseason qualification, seeding, or home-field advantage tiebreakers will not be used.
rules_evidence.establishes: Best and worst record markets settle on raw winning percentage with ties split $1/N, an order statistic over thirty teams rather than a standings outcome.

rules_evidence.quote: If two or more teams share the longest losing streak
rules_evidence.establishes: The losing-streak extreme uses the same shared-maximum $1/N split as the winning-streak market.

rules_evidence.quote: records at least 100 losses in the 2026 Pro Baseball regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The 100-loss market is a lower-tail threshold on one team's regular-season record with no tie branch.

rules_evidence.quote: A team's division affiliation is its official Pro Baseball affiliation when that championship begins.
rules_evidence.establishes: Division and league championship futures are unions over the member teams' title events with affiliation frozen at the start of the postseason.

rules_evidence.quote: If Chinese Taipei wins the World Baseball Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A national-team tournament winner market is filed here; it needs national rosters and a short-tournament model, not club inputs.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington is one of the 2026 Pro Baseball Playoff Qualifiers, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Playoff qualification settles on the final qualifier list (division winners and wild cards), so seeding tiebreakers matter at the boundary.

variants_and_edge_cases: Same archetype mixes regular-season win ladders (binomial-like with talent uncertainty), division titles and playoff qualification (standings and tiebreakers), title futures (bracket dynamic program), seed and division/league unions, bracket pairings, season extremes (best/worst record, longest winning and losing streaks, 100 losses) and a national-team tournament; each needs a different generator.

Seed futures fix seed at the start of the postseason; tiebreakers (head-to-head, divisional record) decide seeds without a game-163 under the current format, so tiebreaker data are required for close races, while record-extreme markets explicitly ignore tiebreakers and split ties $1/N.
Postseason qualifiers resolve at the moment the series is reached; some markets (NLCSQUAL) are determined by winning the division series, so the probability is conditional on the bracket path.

KXMLBWS is the only series without sampled rules; no sampled text addresses a cancelled postseason or a shortened season, which matters for the 2027 championship future (KXMLB) given the CBA expiry on Dec 1 2026 (in 1994 the World Series was cancelled), and for any record, streak or 100-loss market whose season is shortened.

KXMLBWORLD (World Baseball Classic) is a separate competition with national rosters, pool play followed by single elimination, pitch-count limits and mercy rules (to my knowledge); its one-line text is silent on cancellation, tied pool standings and rain-shortened games.

KXMLBDIVWINNER (2025 sample) and KXMLBCHAMPDIVISION (2026) are the same object, the division of the champion; the 2025 text has no affiliation clause, the 2026 text fixes affiliation when the championship begins.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB standings and postseason results; World Baseball Classic official results for KXMLBWORLD; not named in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: Futures integrate three layers. First, a team's true talent is uncertain: a preseason projection prior is updated by run differential (not record) with a posterior standard deviation that shrinks through the season and jumps with roster changes and injuries. Second, the remaining schedule converts talent into a distribution of wins, with binomial game noise of about six wins over a full season on top of talent uncertainty, which gives the wide win-total distributions the ladders price. Third, standings are turned into postseason fates by rules: division winners, wild cards, byes for the top division winners, tiebreakers decided by head-to-head and divisional records, and a bracket in which each series is a dynamic program over announced starters, rest, bullpen leverage and home-field pattern. Short series compress the talent gap, so championship probabilities for even good teams are low and depend on rotation depth and bullpen top-end in October, not on regular-season records. Season extremes (best and worst record, 100 losses, longest winning and losing streaks) are order statistics or run lengths over thirty teams' game sequences, with $1/N tie splits and no tiebreakers; matchup, seed and division-of-champion markets are bracket-path events or unions of team title events. The World Baseball Classic market is a national-team short tournament with its own rosters, pitch limits and single-elimination rounds. Award and leader series sit in season_leaders_and_awards.

stages.name: Talent posterior and uncertainty
stages.description: A team's strength is a distribution, not a number: a preseason projection built from player aging curves and depth charts is the prior, run differential adjusted for schedule and luck updates it, and roster changes (trades, injuries, call-ups) shift it. The posterior standard deviation determines how wide the win-total and title distributions are and decreases with games played.
stages.distribution: Normal-like posterior on true win percentage with sd falling from about 0.04 in April to about 0.028-0.03 by September (the data add precision slowly because a season of games identifies talent only to about 0.03); jumps at injuries and deadline trades.

stages.name: Remaining schedule to wins distribution
stages.description: Given talent, wins to date plus the sum of remaining game outcomes with per-game probability depending on opponent strength, park, rest and the unbalanced division schedule; binomial noise dominates close thresholds and is correlated with talent uncertainty, so the distribution is a mixture of binomials. For any 2027 future the number of games and whether a postseason is held are themselves uncertain under a labour-stoppage scenario, which shrinks win totals and, in the extreme, cancels the championship.
stages.distribution: Mixture of binomials; sd of final wins about 6.5 for 162 games from game noise plus 3-5 from talent uncertainty early.

stages.name: Standings, tiebreakers and seeding
stages.description: Division winners, three wild cards and byes are decided on final records; ties are broken by head-to-head record, divisional record and other criteria with no tiebreaker game, so the same win total can map to different outcomes. The seed assigned at the start of the postseason sets the bracket path and home-field, which matters for the seed and qualifier contracts.
stages.distribution: Discrete fate with probability concentrated at near-boundary records; tiebreaker outcomes are deterministic functions of records.

stages.name: Postseason series dynamic program
stages.description: Each series is a sequence of games with a rotation order, rest and travel days, shortened starter leashes and use of top relievers; teams' per-game win probabilities differ by announced starter and by the playoff-adjusted lineup and bullpen strength; game outcomes are correlated through unobserved strength. Championship probability is the product over rounds of series win probabilities with path dependence.
stages.distribution: Series win probability compresses talent gap (a 60% single-game team wins a best-of-7 about 71%); path-dependent mixture.

stages.name: Season extremes and bracket pairings
stages.description: Several series are not functions of one team's win total. Best and worst record and 100+ losses are tails of the joint distribution of thirty teams' records, correlated through shared schedules, with $1/N splits on tied winning percentage and no tiebreakers. The longest winning and losing streak markets are maximum run lengths over 162-game sequences for all teams, depending on per-game win probabilities, current streaks and the league maximum to date. Matchup markets resolve on which two teams qualify for a series through a fixed bracket, and division- or league-of-champion markets are unions over member teams' title paths.
stages.distribution: Record extremes: order statistics with mass concentrated on two to four teams and frequent ties at the extreme; streaks: extreme-value with a heavy upper tail (league maximum typically 9-12 games); matchup and union markets: categorical over bracket paths, moving in steps as series end.

stages.name: World Baseball Classic national-team tournament
stages.description: The World Baseball Classic winner depends on which major-league players each federation actually rosters (participation decisions, club and insurance restrictions on pitchers), how that talent maps into a few games under pitch-count limits that cap starters at short outings, pool play with run-based tiebreakers and then single-elimination knockout rounds where one game decides advancement. Depth of relief pitching matters more than in MLB because starters are limited, and the tournament is played in March before players are at full workload.
stages.distribution: Strongly favourite-compressed: single-elimination games at roughly 55-70% for the better side give even the strongest roster a title probability well below one half; pool-stage tiebreakers add discrete jumps.

talent_strength.note: Club prior, update and uncertainty; national-team roster strength for the World Baseball Classic.

environment.note: League run baseline and park-balanced schedule.

distribution_variance.note: Mixture of binomials with shared strength uncertainty, order statistics of thirty teams' records, and extreme-value distributions of the longest winning and losing streaks.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Remaining schedule, tiebreakers and labour-stoppage season length for 2027 futures.

pace_volume.note: Games remaining set the exposure for win ladders and streaks.

efficiency_conversion.note: There is no per-opportunity conversion rate at the futures level; team run-prevention and run-scoring efficiency enter through talent estimates (projections and pythag) rather than a separate conversion variable.

officiating_rules.note: Officials play no role in club season outcomes; the World Baseball Classic round pitch-count limits change how talent converts to wins and are encoded in the national-team strength measurement; the mercy rule is not modelled (sf_wbc_rules).

mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team talent posterior (mean and standard deviation) combining projection prior and run differential
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: True team strength is uncertain; its spread determines the width of win-total and title distributions.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A single rating hides that April uncertainty is large and that roster shocks widen it; futures prices at tails (95+ wins, a long-shot pennant) depend on the variance more than the mean.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Prior mean mu0 = preseason projected win% (average of ZiPS/Steamer/PECOTA) with prior sd s0 = 0.04. Data: pythagenpat win% from RS/RA with n games and per-game outcome variance s_game^2 = 0.25 (binomial; use 0.22 for run-based). Conjugate normal update: weight on data w = n/(n + k) with k = s_game^2 / s0^2 = 0.25/0.0016 = about 156 games, so posterior mean = (1-w) mu0 + w pyth_wp and posterior variance = 1/(1/s0^2 + n/s_game^2); at n = 140 this gives sd of about 0.029 and at n = 162 about 0.028. Add roster shock: change in rest-of-season projected WAR per 162 games divided by 162 added to the mean, with variance 0.002 per shock. Units: win probability per game. As-of: daily after games.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.why: Provides the tail-width parameter the season simulation needs.

mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.label: Tiebreaker state (head-to-head and divisional records) and seed-to-bracket path matrix
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.mechanism: Ties in win totals are broken by specified records, and seed determines opponents and home field in a known bracket.
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.rationale: Close races resolve through head-to-head records, not just wins; markets on seeds and qualifiers depend on tiebreakers, which are fully determined by games already played and remaining head-to-head games.
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.measurement: Encode MLB's published tiebreaker hierarchy for the season (versioned text, separate lists for division-title ties and wild-card ties; head-to-head first, then division/intraleague records and later criteria exactly as published, with a final random draw). For each contender pair compute current head-to-head W-L, remaining head-to-head games, division and intraleague records and the next criterion; in each simulated season resolve ties by applying the criteria to simulated results. Seed path: seeds 1-6 per league mapped to round-1 pairing (3 v 6, 4 v 5), byes for seeds 1-2 and home field per round. Output P(seed s) and P(path). Units: probability. As-of: daily.
free_sources: MLB standings and tiebreaker rules documentation
raw_data: game results with opponent and division flags
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.why: Seed and qualifier markets settle on seed and bracket, so ignoring tiebreakers misprices close races.

mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.label: Playoff-adjusted team rating (top-3 starters, top relievers, regular lineup) for short series
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.mechanism: In October rotations shorten and top relievers pitch more, so the relevant team strength differs from the regular-season average.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.rationale: A team's regular-season run differential includes innings from fourth and fifth starters and mid bullpen arms that disappear in the playoffs; the weights shift toward the top of the rotation, top bullpen arms and starting lineup.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.measurement: Team run rate per game in series = (a) lineup: sum over the expected nine of projected runs created per PA (wRC+-based, vs starter hand) x expected PA share; (b) pitching: starters' share of innings in postseason series 2015-2025 (about 0.55-0.6 for top-3 starters, from observed data) x projected RA9 of the top-3 starters weighted by their expected starts, plus relief share x projected RA9 of the top-4 relievers weighted by leverage-share observed in the same sample. Difference vs opponent gives expected run difference per game; convert to win probability with logit slope fitted on 2012-2025 postseason and late-season games (ridge shrink). No bench term unless fitted. Units: runs per game and probability. As-of: playoff roster and announced rotation.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.why: Matches the information relevant to series and title futures instead of full-season ratings.

mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.label: Deadline roster strength shift (net rest-of-season WAR added/lost via trades and call-ups)
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.mechanism: Teams change materially at the trade deadline; sellers lose talent, buyers add it.
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.rationale: Win-total futures after the deadline need a changed mean; a team that sells a star shifts its remaining win rate down by a measurable amount, which the season-to-date record does not reflect.
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.measurement: For each team transaction at time t (trade, claim, release, IL activation, call-up) compute dWAR_t = ROS WAR of players added minus ROS WAR of players lost minus ROS WAR of the displaced next-best depth player, where ROS WAR = ROS projection rate (WAR per 600 PA or 200 IP, ZiPS/Steamer average captured at t) times expected remaining PA or IP from games remaining and health status (zero if out for the season). Win probability shift per game = sum over transactions of dWAR_t / games_remaining(t), accumulated since the baseline date. Units: win probability per game. As-of: transaction timestamp; only projection vintages captured at or before t are admissible.
raw_data: ROS projection vintages at each transaction date
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.why: A direct input to the remaining-schedule simulation that is not captured by season-to-date records.

mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.label: Season state: wins, losses, games remaining, run differential to date and ties/suspended games
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.mechanism: A win-total threshold is wins already banked plus the number of wins in the remaining games, so the state variables set how much uncertainty is left.
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.rationale: The primary state of a win-total ladder is not a rating but how many wins are banked and how many games remain; the required additional wins W_needed = N - wins and the remaining games determine the binomial tail, and the posterior from run differential only prices the per-game probability. Suspended or cancelled games change games remaining.
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.measurement: Daily from standings: W, L, G_rem = 162 - W - L (adjusted for suspended or cancelled games per the official schedule), W_needed = N - W, run differential RD and pythagenpat win% to date. P(wins >= N) = sum over k >= W_needed of P(Bin-mixture(G_rem, p_i)) where p_i is the per-game probability from the talent posterior. Units: wins and games. As-of: after each day's final games.
free_sources: MLB Stats API standings and schedule
raw_data: daily standings with W-L and run differential
mlb.wins_to_date_and_games_remaining.why: Supplies the primary state of the win-total ladders that pythag_luck alone did not define.

mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.label: Postseason bracket-path enumeration: pairing, series length and home-field pattern probabilities
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.mechanism: Matchup, games-hosted and qualifier contracts are functions of which teams reach which round and how long each series lasts.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.rationale: KXMLBMATCHUP and KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST resolve on bracket pairing and on how many games each team hosts, which requires enumerating the fixed bracket (no reseeding within the 12-team format, to be verified) with series-length distributions and home-field patterns, not a title-probability number.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.measurement: Enumerate all bracket paths from the current seeds or seed probabilities: P(path) = product of series-win probabilities from the team-strength posterior; series length distribution from per-game probabilities with home-field pattern (2-3-2 or 2-2-1-1-1) and shared team-strength draws; games hosted = sum over series of the home games in the realised length. Output P(matchup A vs B in round r) and the distribution of games hosted by a team. As-of: daily.
raw_data: bracket structure and home-field pattern table
series results history for length calibration
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.why: Specifies the missing inputs for the matchup and games-hosted series.

mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.label: Series and World Series MVP: P(team wins series) times a player credit-share model
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.mechanism: Series MVP is chosen from the winning team, so probability = P(team wins) times the player's share of the winning team's credit, which depends on his series performance and star status.
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.rationale: KXMLBWSMVP and the championship-series MVP markets pay on the official named winner (co-winners $1/N). The winner comes from the winning team, with voters rewarding series-leading production and narrative; a team's win probability alone overstates its weaker contributors.
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.measurement: P(player MVP) = P(his team wins series) x share_i where share_i = softmax over his team's players of (a x series WPA/RE24 to date + b x pre-series star score (3-season WAR, shrunk k = 3 series)), fitted on MVP voting 2000-2025 series with a pooled coefficient; co-winner probability from history. As-of: after each game for in-series updating. Units: probability.
raw_data: series player-level WPA/RE24 and box scores
mlb.series_mvp_credit_share.why: Defined here while award and playoff-leader series were filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation they are in season_leaders_and_awards, which stages this input. Not staged here: the MVP and playoff-leader series are in season_leaders_and_awards, which stages it.

mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.label: Playoff games played and plate-appearance distribution for a named player (for playoff-leader markets)
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.mechanism: A playoff statistical leader needs games played, which depends on the team's bracket survival, and PA per game, which depends on lineup slot.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.rationale: KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF counts only playoff statistics and resolves No for non-participants, so the leader distribution is a maximum over players of a count over a random number of games; the games-played distribution comes from bracket survival and the PA share from lineup slot and rest.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.measurement: For each candidate i: G_i distribution from mlb.bracket_path_enumeration (games played by his team). Per game, start probability s_i from last 30 team games lineup share (shrunk to 0.9 for everyday, 0.5 platoon with k = 20 games); PA per start by slot from 2015-2025 postseason PA/game (slots 1-9 observed means); stat (HR, RBI, hits, as stated in the contract) per PA from projection rate shrunk to 3-season rate with k = 300 PA, adjusted by opposing starter. Simulate 20k joint draws of counts over G_i games with game-level shared environment; leader = maximum count among players of teams that played; ties split per contract. Output P(leader) and distribution of counts. Units: probability. As-of: daily during the postseason.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason schedule and box scores
raw_data: lineup slot history and start rates
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.why: Defined here while award and playoff-leader series were filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation they are in season_leaders_and_awards, which stages this input. Not staged here: the MVP and playoff-leader series are in season_leaders_and_awards, which stages it.

mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.label: World Baseball Classic national-team strength from confirmed rosters (projected WAR by role, pitch-limit-adjusted pitching depth)
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.mechanism: National-team win probability depends on rostered player talent, with pitching value reweighted for tournament pitch limits that shorten starts and shift innings to relievers.
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.rationale: KXMLBWORLD resolves on a short tournament between federations whose strength changes with each MLB player's decision to participate and with club or insurance limits on pitchers; club-based ratings do not apply, and pitch limits make relief depth worth more than in MLB.
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.measurement: Team run rate per game = sum over the expected lineup of projected runs created per PA (projection rate converted via league-equivalence factors, NPB 0.9, KBO 0.85, minor leagues by level, each shrunk to replacement with k = 200 PA) x expected PA, minus expected runs allowed = sum over rostered pitchers of projected RA9 x expected tournament innings share, where innings share follows the round pitch limits (verify the published limits for the edition; 2023 was 65/80/95 pitches) and relievers' appearances available. Convert run difference to game win probability with a log5/logistic fitted on 2006-2026 tournament games; simulate pools and bracket with the official tiebreaker. Units: probability. As-of: final roster announcement.
free_sources: World Baseball Classic official rosters and results (free_scrape)
raw_data: confirmed national-team rosters with announcement dates
pool and bracket format with tiebreaker rules
mlb.wbc_national_team_strength.why: Gives KXMLBWORLD a national-team strength input; no club-level input in this archetype measures it.

mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.label: League order-statistic engine for best/worst record, 100+ losses, longest losing streak and team strikeouts (simulation method; its inputs are mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_vintage)
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.mechanism: The extreme among thirty teams is determined by each team's talent distribution and the shared schedule.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.rationale: Existing inputs address single games; extremes require a league-wide simulation where each team's outcome is drawn jointly, ties are tracked for $1/N payouts, and streak and strikeout statistics are computed from game-level sequences.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.measurement: Simulate remaining games for 30 teams using team talent posterior (mean, sd) and schedule; record final wins, the longest loss streak per team (run-length of simulated sequence) and team strikeouts (batters faced x team K rate with pitching staff K% projection, sd from game-level variance). Outputs: P(team is unique best), P(tied for best with N teams), expected payout with $1/N rounding; P(wins <= 62 for 100 losses). 20k simulations; calibrate sd to historical. As-of: daily. Units: probabilities.
free_sources: MLB Stats API results and schedule
raw_data: team game logs; remaining schedule; team projections; team K%
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.why: Best/worst record, 100-loss and losing-streak series (KXMLBBESTRECORD, KXMLB100LOSS, KXMLBLSTREAK, filed here) are thirty-team order statistics simulated by this engine.

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.label: Longest winning streak: extreme-value distribution given team win probabilities and remaining games
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.mechanism: The longest win streak across teams is the maximum over runs of consecutive wins; the season-level maximum is an extreme value.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.rationale: Season streak markets are filed in this archetype but are not inning markets; the winning team is the one with the longest run, with ties paying $1/N, so the exact distribution of the maximum run for each team (given per-game win probability, mostly 0.4-0.65) determines the odds.
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.measurement: For team i with games remaining n_i, current streak c_i and per-game win prob p_ij: P(longest streak >= L) computed by a run-length Markov chain; account for heterogeneity of p_ij by opponent and home/away, and current maximum across league to date. P(team has strict maximum) = Prod over rivals (1 - ...) with Monte Carlo and tie share 1/N (payout rounded down). Streak serial correlation assumed zero unless tested. As-of: daily. Units: probability. Postponed, suspended and cancelled games are excluded from the sequence; the streak model assumes independent games conditional on p_ij, so serial correlation and doubleheader order are assumptions.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule and results
raw_data: team game log: date, win/loss, opponent, home flag
mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.why: KXMLBWSTREAK (longest winning streak, filed here) is a run-length extreme over every team's remaining schedule.

mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.label: All-30-team talent posteriors with projection vintage, remaining schedule and head-to-head structure
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.mechanism: League-wide order statistics need every team's win-probability distribution, correlated through the shared schedule.
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.rationale: Best record, worst record, 100+ losses and the longest-streak markets are maxima over 30 teams; the engine inputs are the 30 posterior means and sds, the remaining schedule and projection vintages, not the engine itself.
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.measurement: For each team i: posterior mean p_i and sd s_i from preseason projection (average of ZiPS/Steamer, prior sd 0.04) updated by pythagenpat win% with conjugate normal weights (k = s_game^2/s0^2 about 156 games), as-of daily; remaining schedule with opponent posteriors and home flags; projection vintage stored at each date so backtests use only information available then. Output: 30 x (p_i, s_i), the 30-team opponent matrix and remaining games. As-of: after each day's games.
free_sources: FanGraphs ZiPS/Steamer (current only; vintages need own capture)
MLB Stats API standings and schedule
mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.why: All-30-team talent posteriors with projection vintage are the inputs of the order-statistic engine used for the league-wide record and streak series filed here.

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.label: Lockout and shortened-season scenario: P(lockout), start/end dates and games lost under each scenario
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.mechanism: A CBA lockout after Dec 1 2026 could delay opening day and cancel games, so season-games and opening-day outcomes are mixtures over scenarios.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.rationale: A 600-game strike equals roughly a quarter of the 2,430-game schedule and a May 31 opening cutoff is a long delay; both are plausible stoppage thresholds. In 2021-22 the lockout postponed opening day by about one week with no games lost (to my knowledge), but 1994-95 lost the end of one season and the start of the next; the distribution of games lost is heavy-tailed with a large mass at zero.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.measurement: Scenario mixture: P(no lockout) from negotiation state (own timestamped coding of reports, ordinal 0-4); conditional on a lockout, the stoppage end date drawn from a survival model with prior from 1990, 1994-95 and 2021-22 (3 events, strongly shrunk) updated by negotiation stage; games lost = schedule games before the agreed start date after a compressed ramp-up (about 3 weeks of spring training), with doubleheaders making up part. Output: P(first regular-season game before May 31 2027) and P(games played > 600) = P(games lost < 1,830). As-of: daily.
mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.why: 2027 season futures resolve on a season whose length depends on a lockout after the Dec 1 2026 CBA expiry; the scenario mixture sets games played.

mlb.season_sim.reason: A method for generating probabilities, not an input; its inputs (talent posterior, wins to date and games remaining, schedule, tiebreakers) are specified separately and it is kept only as the aggregation engine.

mlb.preseason_projections.reason: Talent prior from projection systems; vintage and calibration of the prior sd matter.

mlb.pythag_luck.reason: Run-based record regression is the right update signal; weights must depend on games played.

mlb.remaining_sos.reason: Opponent strength and home/away mix of remaining games; modest effect for most teams but meaningful for division races.

mlb.depth_injury_war.reason: Injuries to key players and depth shift rest-of-season strength; needs ROS WAR with replacement.

mlb.sp_quality.reason: Rotation matters for series but is already inside team rating for season totals.

mlb.bullpen_talent.reason: Bullpen quality for close games; high noise year to year; only top relievers matter in October.

mlb.postseason_seeding_rules.reason: Seeding, byes and tiebreakers determine which path and contract settles; must be in simulation.

mlb.series_context.reason: Rest and rotation order for series; only relevant when the series is underway.

mlb.postseason_leverage_usage.reason: Shorter leash and high-leverage reliever usage; informs the playoff rating.

mlb.rule_regime.reason: League run baselines affect league-wide scale not relative strength; matters for specials rather than win totals.

mlb.news.reason: Injury and trade news is captured via depth and roster-shift inputs; raw news is an input only for timing.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures are the benchmark for fair probability, not an information source.

mlb.season_sim_distribution.reason: The simulated distribution is the output of the season simulation, not a separate input.

interactions.mechanism: The weight on run-based evidence versus the preseason prior is games/(games + k), so early in the season the prior dominates and late the record dominates; the posterior variance falls accordingly. The interaction between games played and each source determines tail width, so the two sources cannot be added with fixed weights.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the weighting k by backtesting predicted rest-of-season win% at different dates; compare to fixed-weight blend.

interactions.mechanism: A seller's loss of rest-of-season WAR matters most for teams still in the race, and its effect on win total is proportional to games remaining; opponent strength of those remaining games conditions the impact on wins, so the shift must enter the simulation, not the record.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate remaining games with and without shifts and measure change in P(win threshold).

interactions.mechanism: Championship probability is convex in seed through the bye and bracket: a top-two division winner skips a round (one fewer series to win) and faces weaker opponents; the value of one extra win near the seeding boundary is large, so final-week wins have convex impact on title odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute title probability by seed with a bracket simulation and compare marginal value of a win near boundaries.

interactions.mechanism: In the postseason the rotation shortens, so the weight on top starters rises and day-by-day starter identity matters; the pitching regime changes at the start of the playoffs, so regular-season starter weights misprice series.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate series win probability with playoff weights versus season weights on historical series.

interactions.mechanism: Uncertainty about team strength is shared across games and rounds, so series outcomes are positively correlated across a team's path: a team that is stronger than believed wins several series, which fattens the tails of championship probability relative to independent rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probability from simulations with shared strength draws versus independent per-series draws.

interactions.mechanism: The chance of a long streak rises much faster than linearly in per-game win probability (P of an L-game run scales like p^L), so the strongest teams dominate the streak market more than their win-total edge suggests, and a team with an active streak near the league maximum late in the season is priced mostly off its next few games; games remaining cap the opportunity.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated and realised league-maximum streaks by team quality decile over past seasons and check calibration of P(longest) for teams with active streaks.

interactions.mechanism: For 2027 futures the model is a mixture over labour regimes: no stoppage (a normal 162-game season), a shortened season (fewer games, so more variance in standings and more upsets of strong teams) and a cancelled postseason (settlement unknown). Strong favourites lose value under shortened seasons because season-long talent edges matter less, so the regime weights interact with team strength rather than scaling all teams equally.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare championship probabilities of top-, middle- and bottom-tier teams under 60-, 120- and 162-game simulated seasons, using 2020 as a reference for a shortened season.

interactions.mechanism: Best-record, worst-record and 100-loss outcomes are linked: teams share opponents, so one team's extra wins are another's losses, and the worst-record race is usually decided among two or three teams whose posteriors overlap. Ties at the extreme pay $1/N, so the joint probability of equal winning percentages near the end of the season changes expected payouts even when the leader is clear.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the full league season jointly versus independently per team and compare predicted extreme and tie probabilities against settled seasons since 2000.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance falls hyperbolically with games played, with jumps at roster shocks
nonlinearities.why: Posterior precision adds linearly with games, so sd falls like 1/sqrt(n) and not linearly; shocks reset part of the uncertainty.

nonlinearities.shape: Logistic in log run ratio, which is close to linear in run differential over normal team ranges (exponent about 1.83); the relevant nonlinearity is the games-played shrinkage weight n/(n+k) on run-based evidence
nonlinearities.why: The claim of concavity at large run ratios is irrelevant for full-season totals; what matters is how fast pythagenpat evidence outweighs the preseason prior, which is the weight n/(n+156) specified in the talent-posterior input.

nonlinearities.shape: Compressing S-shape: series win probability is a steep logistic of per-game edge, with best-of-7 amplification
nonlinearities.why: Longer series amplify edges, but the amplification is limited, so title futures compress toward 50% pairs.

nonlinearities.shape: Cliff at the seeding boundary
nonlinearities.why: One extra win can change a bye, opponent and home field, giving a step in title probability at the boundary.

nonlinearities.shape: order-statistic concentration
nonlinearities.why: The probability of holding the best or worst record rises steeply with a team's mean relative to its nearest rival, so small posterior shifts late in the season move the extreme markets far more than win-total ladders.
