contract.settlement_definition: Thirty-one live series of voted awards, selections and statistical races after the reconciliation, all with sampled rules. Award winners (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie, Reliever, Manager and Executive of the Year, Hank Aaron, Comeback, ALCS/NLCS/World Series MVP) pay on the official winner; the series-MVP texts pay $1/N to each official co-winner, and AL Comeback Player lists a separate 'Tie/Co-Winners' outcome, while the other award texts have no co-winner clause. KXMLBAWARDFIN pays if the player is named a finalist 'as reported by one of the Source Agencies', resolving all No if finalists are not announced before the winner. Monthly and weekly awards (Player and Pitcher of the Month, Player of the Week) pay $1/N rounded down when several candidates share the award. KXMLBALLSTAR pays Yes if the player is selected to his league's All-Star team, even if he does not participate. KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF counts playoff statistics only, resolves No for a non-playing participant, pays tied leaders proportionally and considers statistical corrections only if made before expiration. KXMLBSEASONHR (50+ HR) and KXMLBSTATCOUNT (50 HR and 40 SB) count regular-season games only; KXMLBTRIPLECROWN requires leading the league in batting average, home runs and RBIs over the regular season; KXMLBTEAMSTAT (sampled: most strikeouts thrown by a team's staff) pays $1/N on ties. Silver Slugger (sampled: NL team award) and Gold Glove (sampled: NL pitcher) name specific awards. No text names a source of truth other than the finalist 'Source Agencies'. All-Star Game, Derby and draft series are in other archetypes.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on who is selected as a finalist for National League MVP as reported by one of the Source Agencies.
rules_evidence.establishes: Finalist market settles on the announced finalist list from named source agencies, not on the eventual winner.

rules_evidence.quote: In the event that finalists are not announced and reported by one of the Source Agencies prior to the award winner being announced, then all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement has an announcement-timing condition: no finalists before the winner means No, so the timing of announcements is an input.

rules_evidence.quote: If T.J. Rumfield wins the Pro Baseball National League Rookie of the Year in the 2026 season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Rookie of the Year settles on the official winner; eligibility (rookie status) is implicit in the award definition.

rules_evidence.quote: each co-winner’s Yes contracts will pay $1/N and No contracts will pay $1 minus the Yes payout
rules_evidence.establishes: Series-MVP markets split the payout among official co-winners.

rules_evidence.quote: Participants who do not play any games due to injury, suspension, retirement, or other reasons resolve to No. In case of exact ties where the league does not declare a single winner, tied participants receive a proportional payout.
rules_evidence.establishes: The playoff-leader market has no void for non-participants and splits ties, so games-played exposure and tie probability both enter.

rules_evidence.quote: (excluding preseason, exhibitions, the All-Star Game, and postseason)
rules_evidence.establishes: The 50 HR / 40 SB market counts regular-season games only.

rules_evidence.quote: A Triple Crown occurs when a player leads their league in batting average, home runs, and RBIs for the Pro Baseball regular season.
rules_evidence.establishes: The Triple Crown is league-specific and regular-season only; the text does not say whether a tie for a category lead counts as leading.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington wins the NL Silver Slugger for Team in the 2026 Pro Baseball season
rules_evidence.establishes: The Silver Slugger series includes the team award, a different object from the positional player awards.

rules_evidence.quote: If Dillon Dingler is selected but does not participate, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: All-Star markets settle on selection, so injury replacements and declined invitations do not reverse a Yes; the object is the selection process, not the game.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple candidates are given Player of the Month on the Pro Baseball American League Player of the Month for July, then their Contracts will resolve to $1/(the number of candidates awarded), rounded down.
rules_evidence.establishes: Monthly awards split the payout among co-recipients, so the probability of a shared award enters expected payout.

rules_evidence.quote: If Tie/Co-Winners wins the Pro Baseball American League Comeback Player of the Year in the 2026 season
rules_evidence.establishes: The comeback award lists a co-winner outcome as its own market, so a shared award is a priced state rather than a payout split.

rules_evidence.quote: If Washington records the most strikeouts thrown in the 2026 Pro Baseball regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The team-stat market is an order statistic of pitching-staff strikeouts over the regular season, with $1/N on ties.

variants_and_edge_cases: Finalist versus winner: the finalist market has a fixed field (three finalists per league per award) selected from ballot ranks, so probability is rank-based (top three) rather than winner-based; the announcement condition adds a No branch.

Voter populations differ (verified 2026-11-08): BBWAA ballots decide MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year and Manager of the Year; the Rivera/Hoffman Reliever of the Year awards are voted by a panel of retired relievers (Rivera, Hoffman, Eckersley, Fingers, Franco, Wagner in 2023); Comeback Player by the 30 MLB.com beat reporters; the Hank Aaron Award by a Hall of Fame panel plus an MLB.com fan vote; Executive of the Year by the 30 clubs before the postseason; Gold Gloves by managers and up to six coaches plus the SABR Defensive Index (about 25 percent); fans, players and the league choose All-Stars. The electorate of the team Silver Slugger sampled in KXMLBSS remains unverified. Each needs its own model (award_electorate_procedure).
Statistical races (Triple Crown) are joint order statistics of three correlated categories with rate-stat qualification rules and tie handling; counting windows (regular season only) matter.

Eligibility rules (rookie status limits on at-bats, innings and days on the active roster) can make candidate sets differ from the obvious field; most award texts are silent on co-winners, which only the series-MVP texts, the monthly and weekly awards and the AL Comeback 'Tie/Co-Winners' outcome address.

Postseason awards and leaders: series MVPs are named from the winning team in nearly all cases and pay $1/N on co-winners; the playoff runs leader depends on how many games a player's team plays, so it is a joint bracket-and-production event; a non-playing participant resolves No rather than voiding.

Manager and Executive of the Year (moved here): Manager of the Year is a BBWAA award voted before the postseason (3 places, 5-3-1); Executive of the Year is voted by executives of the 30 clubs before the postseason with no public ballots (verified from MLB's announcements), so it uses executive_award_team_improvement, not the BBWAA rank model or the manager score.

Silver Slugger and Gold Glove series name specific awards: the sampled KXMLBSS market is the NL Silver Slugger for Team (a team-offence award) and KXMLBGG is the NL Gold Glove for Pitcher, so each series needs the award's own electorate and candidate pool (team offence for SS Team; pitcher fielding, where the SABR Defensive Index is thin, for GG); a tie for a Triple Crown category lead is not addressed.

Selection versus participation: KXMLBALLSTAR resolves Yes on selection even without participation, so injury replacements named later count as separate selections; monthly and weekly awards split the payout among co-recipients.

Team counting race (KXMLBTEAMSTAT, sampled: most strikeouts thrown) is a thirty-team order statistic of staff strikeouts over the regular season with $1/N on ties; other stat variants of the series are unseen.

Reliever of the Year ambiguity: KXMLBALRELOTY/KXMLBNLRELOTY name the 'Pro Baseball ... Reliever of the Year'; from 2026 two awards exist, MLB's panel award (Rivera/Hoffman, retired relievers) and the new BBWAA Relief Pitcher of the Year (finalists announced Nov 2 2026, winners due Nov 11 2026). The text does not say which settles; the panel and the writers can disagree.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official awards announcements and ballots (BBWAA/MLB), official league statistics for leader markets; the finalist market names 'Source Agencies' without listing them in the sample.

mechanism.summary: Awards and leaders are of two types. Statistical outcomes (season leaders, Triple Crown, season thresholds) equal current totals plus rest-of-season rate times opportunities times availability, so the probability that a player finishes first is the probability his final total exceeds every rival's, with correlations through teams and parks and with rate-stat qualification rules deciding who is eligible. Voted outcomes (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, finalists, Gold Glove, Silver Slugger, All-Star) are produced by a ballot of a specific electorate that ranks candidates on a mixture of production (WAR variants, counting stats), team success and narrative, with ballots cast at a fixed date and finalists announced before winners. The finalist market is a rank-three event, which is easier to predict than the winner, with a timing condition. A first-principles model uses a production model for statistical races and a rank-ordered voter model (Plackett-Luce) for awards, with candidate sets restricted by eligibility. Early-season leaders are mostly luck so regression of rates is critical; late-season markets are dominated by remaining games and injuries. After the reconciliation the archetype also holds postseason MVP and playoff-leader markets (team advancement times player credit), Manager of the Year (team surprise versus projection, BBWAA) and Executive of the Year (club executives' vote before the postseason on team improvement and resource efficiency), and single-hitter season counting thresholds (50 HR, 50 HR plus 40 SB). The team-strikeout leader market (KXMLBTEAMSTAT) is a thirty-team order statistic of batters faced times staff strikeout rate.

stages.name: Candidate set and eligibility
stages.description: Each market has a candidate set determined by rules: rookie status for ROY, qualifying PA/IP for rate leaders, league membership, position for Gold Glove and Silver Slugger, and active roster for All-Star. The set is smaller than the full player pool, and eligibility changes (call-ups, injuries) change the field.
stages.distribution: Small candidate set (3-10 realistic contenders) with long tail of near-zero probabilities.

stages.name: Production to date and rest-of-season projection
stages.description: For statistical races final total = current total + rest-of-season rate x games remaining x probability of playing; rate is the true-talent estimate regressed from observed performance (HR/FB, BABIP), and opportunity depends on lineup slot, platoon and team schedule. Correlation across contenders arises from shared opponents and parks.
stages.distribution: Sum of a fixed current total and a compound future; right-skewed for HR, near-normal for rate stats with qualifiers.

stages.name: Voter model for awards
stages.description: Ballots rank candidates; each voter's ranking combines production metrics (WAR variants, counting stats), team success (playoff berth, division title) and narrative (milestones, comeback), with systematic biases (pitchers vs hitters in MVP, closers in Cy Young). Point systems aggregate ranks to a winner and finalists. The outcome is a rank distribution, not a single winner. The electorate differs by award and is now sourced (award_electorate_procedure): BBWAA writers with public ballots for MVP, Cy Young, Rookie and Manager of the Year; rank-model coefficients are pooled only within one electorate class, and the ballot simulation uses each award's own voter count and points scale (MVP 14-9-8-...-1 over 10 places, Cy Young 7-4-3-2-1, Rookie and Manager 5-3-1).
stages.distribution: Rank distribution over few candidates; multinomial-logit or Plackett-Luce with correlated voter noise.

stages.name: Announcement timing and information events
stages.description: Finalists are announced about a week or two before winners, and ballots are cast before the postseason; markets that settle on announcements depend on whether and when these events occur. Finalist announcements are strong information events for winner markets.
stages.distribution: Discrete timing events with known calendar; announcement conditions create No branches.

stages.name: Period and joint-leader variants
stages.description: Monthly and weekly awards select players over short windows from committee judgement of production in that window, while Triple Crown requires leading three correlated categories (batting average, HR, RBI) simultaneously, with rate-stat qualification; these are distinct joint models.
stages.distribution: Short-window noisy production (monthly) and joint order statistic (Triple Crown); rare event.

stages.name: All-Star selection, postseason MVP and award combinations
stages.description: All-Star selection combines fan-vote phases, a player vote and commissioner or roster-fill rules. Series MVPs are chosen almost always from the winning team, so a player's chance is his team's series-win probability times his share of the credit (a few big games, a starter's two wins). The playoff runs leader is a race whose exposure is the number of playoff games each team plays, and award combinations need the joint distribution of correlated award outcomes.
stages.distribution: Selection: Bernoulli over vote tallies with a discrete roster-fill step; series MVP: product of a series-win probability and a concentrated credit share; playoff leader: order statistic over very unequal exposure; combinations: positively correlated joint outcomes.

stages.name: Manager awards and season counting thresholds
stages.description: Manager of the Year votes reward wins over preseason expectation, a division title or a turnaround, with ballots cast before the postseason, so the input is the team's surprise relative to projection rather than its record. The 50 home run and 50 HR plus 40 SB markets are threshold events of one hitter's regular-season counts, driven by current totals, remaining plate appearances and the correlation of power and speed through playing time.
stages.distribution: Manager award: concentrated rank distribution over two or three surprise teams; counting thresholds: rare joint tail that collapses once the pace falls behind.

stages.name: Team pitching-staff strikeout leader
stages.description: The team leading in strikeouts thrown is the maximum over thirty staffs of strikeouts to date plus remaining batters faced times the staff's strikeout rate, where the rate is a weighted mix of rotation and bullpen pitchers' projected K% and changes with injuries and deadline trades; extra-inning games and doubleheaders add batters faced. Ties at the top pay $1/N, which matters only when two staffs are within a few strikeouts in the final week.
stages.distribution: Order statistic of near-normal staff totals (season sd roughly 40-60 strikeouts from rate uncertainty and volume); probability concentrated on two or three high-strikeout staffs, with tie mass negligible except at the very end.

stages.name: Non-BBWAA electorates: relievers' panel, beat reporters, fans and club executives
stages.description: Four award families are not BBWAA votes and need their own branch. Reliever of the Year: the MLB award named for Rivera and Hoffman is chosen by a panel of about six retired relievers picking three per league on regular-season work, while the BBWAA introduced a separate Relief Pitcher of the Year in 2026; the Kalshi text names only 'Reliever of the Year', so which award settles is itself uncertain. Comeback Player: 30 MLB.com beat reporters reward a return from injury or collapse, so the prior-season absence or decline is the key covariate. Hank Aaron Award: a Hall of Fame panel plus an online fan vote over club nominees, so popularity adds to offensive production. Executive of the Year: the 30 clubs vote before the postseason on regular-season improvement and resource efficiency, with no public ballots.
stages.distribution: Small finalist or nominee sets with concentrated winner probabilities; no public ballots for most classes, so coefficients rest on a handful of winners per award and need strong shrinkage.

talent_strength.note: True-talent rates, production metrics and team surprise for manager awards.

game_context_script.note: Team success enters votes through award_narrative; series-MVP credit is conditional on the team winning the series.

pace_volume.note: Regular-season PA/IP opportunity and playoff games-played exposure.

efficiency_conversion.note: The only conversion input, HR/FB regression, was audited WEAK and subsumed by rate projection; leader and award markets use the projected rate directly, so no separate conversion input is claimed.

distribution_variance.note: Order statistics, rank distributions and joint threshold tails.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Narrative flags, ballot timing and electorate per award, executive and fan-vote branches, games remaining.

settlement_contract.note: Source agencies, announcement conditions, tie handling.

opponent_matchup.note: Season leaders and awards are accumulated over hundreds of games against the whole league, so single-game matchup effects average out; the only matchup-like factor is remaining schedule strength, which is a minor term in the rest-of-season rate.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager decisions affect leaders through lineup slot and playing time (included in expected PA) and for Gold Glove/Silver Slugger the voters are managers, covered in the voter model; no separate scheme factor drives the outcome.

environment.note: Park and weather enter the rest-of-season rate through projections and are not separate drivers at this horizon; home-park effects on counting stats are in the player's projected rate.

officiating_rules.note: Official scoring changes can alter totals slightly and tie handling matters for leaders, but these are covered in settlement; umpire effects are negligible at season scale.

mlb.award_vote_rank_model.label: Rank-ordered voter model (Plackett-Luce) for award points and finalists
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.mechanism: Awards are decided by ballots ranking candidates; the distribution over rankings, not a single score, gives winner and finalist probabilities.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.rationale: A winner market and a finalist market need different parts of the same ranking distribution; point totals depend on ballot structure (first-place votes, 10-deep ballots) and on how the voters weigh WAR, counting stats and team success.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.measurement: Plackett-Luce likelihood on 1996-2025 BBWAA ballots per award and league (rank-ordered top 10 for MVP with points 14-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1, top 5 for Cy Young since 2010 with 7-4-3-2-1, top 3 for Rookie and Manager of the Year with 5-3-1): worth_i = exp(b1*WAR_z + b2*team_win_pct_z + b3*counting_z + b4*playoff_flag + b5*milestone_flag + position/pitcher effects), z-scores computed within each league-season over the top 15 candidates by WAR, WAR = mean of fWAR and bWAR at the end of the regular season (ballot deadline). Estimate by maximum likelihood with ridge shrinkage of each award's coefficients toward the pooled coefficients of the same electorate class from mlb.award_electorate_procedure (penalty equal to 3 seasons of data); BBWAA coefficients are never pooled with panel, beat-reporter, fan or executive awards. Simulate 30 voter ballots from the fitted model (temperature tau fitted on first-place-vote dispersion) with the real points scale; output P(winner) and P(top 3 by points). milestone_flag and the other narrative terms are the pre-registered flags of mlb.award_narrative. As-of: final regular-season stats, before ballot release.
raw_data: season-candidate table: fWAR/bWAR, counting stats, team win%, playoff flag
ballot results with points and ranks, ballot sizes
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.why: Provides the estimand the voter hypotheses refer to and distinguishes finalist from winner markets.

mlb.roy_eligibility_status.label: Rookie-of-the-Year eligibility status and candidate set (rookie limits on at-bats, innings and active-roster days)
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.mechanism: ROY eligibility depends on prior at-bats, innings pitched and days on the active roster; some prominent players are ineligible.
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.rationale: A market on a prominent debutant must be restricted to eligible candidates; mistaking an ineligible player for a contender mis-sets the field, and call-up timing affects total production.
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.measurement: At the start of the season Y, from career MLB stats and roster transactions through Y-1: rookie_eligible = (career AB <= 130) AND (career IP <= 50) AND (career days on the active roster, excluding injured-list days, <= 45), thresholds to be checked against MLB's published rookie rule for season Y and versioned. Candidate set = eligible players with a projection above replacement or MLB Pipeline top-100 rank. For prospects, P(call-up by date) = hazard from option status, 40-man membership and service-time date. Output eligibility flag and call-up probability. Units: flag and probability. As-of: day; recompute daily in season because days and AB accumulate.
free_sources: MLB Stats API player career stats
raw_data: career MLB at-bats, innings pitched, active-roster days (from transactions)
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.why: Defines the candidate set for the ROY market, a first-order determinant of probabilities.

mlb.award_timing_information_state.label: Award calendar information state (ballot deadline, finalist announcement date, announcement-before-winner condition)
mlb.award_timing_information_state.mechanism: Awards have a fixed calendar: ballots close before the postseason, finalists are announced, then winners.
mlb.award_timing_information_state.rationale: The finalist contract resolves No if finalists are not announced before the winner, and finalist announcements are information events that collapse winner uncertainty; knowing which dates are fixed and which are not is part of settlement.
mlb.award_timing_information_state.measurement: Table by award and season: ballot deadline, finalist announcement date, winner date, announcing agency; compute historical lag between finalist and winner announcements (days) and the fraction of awards with a finalist announcement at all (by award type). P(finalists announced before winner) from that history (Beta prior, k = 5 seasons). Units: dates and probability. As-of: current season calendar.
raw_data: award calendar by year: ballot date, finalist date, winner date, source
mlb.award_timing_information_state.why: The finalist rule gives a No branch tied to the announcement calendar, so its probability must be estimated.

mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.label: Monthly/weekly window production rank (OPS, HR, ERA, K) within the award window
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.mechanism: Player of the Month/Week is chosen from production over a short window by a selection committee.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.rationale: Short windows are noisy and the top performer in OPS or ERA is largely determined by luck, but the selection rule (batters from each league, pitchers separately) and narrative create structure.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.measurement: For each league and window (calendar month, or Mon-Sun week): hitters qualify with >=3.1 PA per team game in the window, pitchers with >=1 IP per team game (starters; relievers separately by min 10 IP). Score_hit = z(wOBA) + z(HR) , Score_pit = z(ERA-) + z(K) with z computed across qualifiers in that league-window; rank within league. P(selection) = conditional logit over the qualifiers, features rank, score gap to rank 1, team own-model playoff probability (market-free simulation), prior-winner flag, fitted on 2015-2025 windows with ridge penalty. Units: probability. As-of: last game of the window; no data after the announcement is used.
raw_data: daily player batting/pitching lines for the window
Player of the Month/Week award history 2015-2025
team standings and own playoff-odds simulation
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.why: Gives a specific input for the monthly and weekly awards filed in this archetype, otherwise unaddressed.

mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.label: Triple Crown joint leader probability (batting average, home runs, RBI) with correlations
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.mechanism: Triple Crown requires leading all three categories; they are positively correlated but the batting-average race has qualification and different drivers.
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.rationale: Product of marginal leader probabilities overstates the event if categories were independent and understates it if highly correlated; the joint distribution matters.
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.measurement: Within one league: contenders = top 10 in each of AVG (qualified, 3.1 PA per team game with the hitless-AB adjustment), HR and RBI. Simulate rest-of-season counts from projections (HR, RBI, H, AB, PA) with a multivariate model whose correlation matrix is estimated from 2000-2025 player-season residuals of rest-of-season stats against projection (shrunk to the pooled matrix with k = 30 seasons). 20k simulations; P(Triple Crown) = P(one player leads all three after applying qualification and tie rules per contract). Units: probability. As-of: daily.
raw_data: player-season stats with PA, AB, H, HR, RBI
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.why: Triple Crown is rare, so the joint distribution is crucial.

mlb.all_star_selection_model.label: All-Star selection model: fan-vote phases, player vote, commissioner/roster-fill rules and positional slots
mlb.all_star_selection_model.mechanism: A player is selected through fan voting that fixes starters, a player vote and then commissioner or roster-fill picks, so selection probability depends on vote share, position slot and team-representation rules.
mlb.all_star_selection_model.rationale: KXMLBALLSTAR cannot be modelled from season production alone: starters are fan-determined, reserves player-chosen and pitchers and replacements follow rules, with injured selectees replaced and each team is assured a representative.
mlb.all_star_selection_model.measurement: P(selected) = P(starter via fan vote) + P(reserve via player vote | not starter) + P(added by commissioner or as replacement | neither). Fan-vote share modelled from last-year vote share, WAR rank at the ballot-close date and market size with a multinomial logit by position (shrinkage k = 2 seasons); player-vote probability from WAR rank within position; team-representation fill from the rule that each club has at least one selectee. Calibrate on 2015-2025 selections. As-of: ballot phase timestamps.
raw_data: fan vote phase tallies with timestamps
All-Star rosters by year with selection route
player WAR rank at ballot close
mlb.all_star_selection_model.why: Defines the selection process for the All-Star series that previously had no stage or input.

mlb.all_star_game_event_model.label: All-Star Game result and MVP model: league talent, exhibition usage and MVP credit given the winning team
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.mechanism: The exhibition has equal-stakes, short-stint pitcher usage and substitution rules, so the result is close to a coin flip and the MVP comes from the winning team's players with the most plate appearances and highlights.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.rationale: KXMLBASGAME and KXMLBASGMVP resolve on a one-off game: league strength differences are tiny relative to variance, and MVP depends on the winning side, plate appearances and extra-base or home-run events.
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.measurement: P(league wins) = logistic(b * (S_A - S_B)) where S_L = sum over the nine lineup slots of PA_share(slot) * projected wOBA runs (wOBA minus league mean, divided by 1.2) plus sum over about eight pitchers of 1 inning * (league ERA minus projected FIP-based ERA), all from ZiPS/Steamer ROS at roster announcement; b = 0.5 times the regular-season slope from a logistic of game outcome on team run-differential strength (2010-2025) and shrunk toward 0 with k = 10 ASG games. P(MVP = i) = sum over leagues of P(league wins) * softmax within the winning league of log(E[PA_i] * h_i), E[PA_i] from mlb.asg_roster_participation_plan, h_i = P(HR) + 0.5 * P(2+ hits) per PA (pitchers: batters faced x K rate), with MVP credit weights (RBI, go-ahead event) fitted on 2000-2025 ASG box scores. As-of: lineups and pitching plan at announcement.
raw_data: ZiPS/Steamer ROS projections for rostered players
mlb.all_star_game_event_model.why: Defined here while the All-Star Game series were filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation they are in all_star_week_events and this input is not staged here.

mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.label: Draft lottery odds by prior-season record and eligibility rules
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.mechanism: Draft position is set by a lottery among non-playoff clubs whose odds are fixed by prior-season record, with restrictions on consecutive top-pick wins.
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.rationale: KXMLBDRAFTPICK is not an award or race: the probability of a given pick is a lottery function of record rank, the number of lottery slots and the consecutive-win restrictions.
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.measurement: Odds table P(pick = j | record rank r) from the official lottery rules (non-playoff clubs, odds by reverse record rank, lottery covering the first picks, restrictions on repeated winners and revenue-sharing recipients), with record ranks from the final standings and tiebreaker; simulate the lottery. Units: probability by pick slot. As-of: final standings. The numeric odds table for the draft in question is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED here.
free_sources: MLB draft lottery rules and odds table
raw_data: published lottery odds table and restrictions
mlb.draft_lottery_odds_by_record.why: Defined here while KXMLBDRAFTPICK was filed in this archetype; after the reconciliation the draft market is in the amateur-draft archetype; not staged here or in transactions.

mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.label: Joint distribution of award outcomes for combination markets
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.mechanism: A combination market pays only if several awards go to specified outcomes, whose probabilities are correlated through shared player performance and team narrative.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.rationale: KXMLBAWARDCOMBO needs P(A and B), not the product: an MVP and Cy Young from the same team are positively dependent via team success, while two MVPs in different leagues are nearly independent; the electorates also differ.
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.measurement: For awards A and B, take marginals P(A), P(B) from mlb.award_vote_rank_model (never from prices). Define relation group g in {same team, same league different team, different league} for the two candidate outcomes. From 1996-2025 winners compute lift_g = [n_AB,g / n_g] / [P_hist(A) * P_hist(B)] where n_AB,g counts seasons both events in group g happened and n_g counts seasons the pair was possible; shrink lift_shrunk = 1 + (lift_g - 1) * n_g / (n_g + 10). Then P(A and B) = min(P(A), P(B), P(A) * P(B) * lift_shrunk). Output P(A and B) and the ratio to the product. As-of: after finalists are announced, using only winners before the snapshot.
raw_data: award winners and finalists by season and league
team of each winner and playoff status
mlb.award_combo_joint_distribution.why: Defines the joint structure for combination markets.

mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.label: Manager of the Year score: wins over preseason expectation, division outcome and turnaround
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.mechanism: BBWAA voters choose Manager of the Year before the postseason on team surprise and success relative to preseason expectation rather than on absolute record; the executive award has a different electorate and its own input.
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.rationale: Votes correlate more with wins minus preseason projection (and a division title or big turnaround) than with wins alone; the voting ballot closes before the postseason, so late-season trajectory and awards-ballot deadline matter.
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.measurement: score = (actual wins - preseason projected wins, mean of ZiPS and PECOTA team projections published before opening day) + b1*I(division title) + b2*I(playoff berth) + b3*(wins - prior-season wins), evaluated at the ballot deadline (end of regular season) and updated daily in-season. P(manager i wins) = softmax over the finalist set of c*score_i, with b1, b2, b3 and c fitted by multinomial logit on 2005-2025 finalist sets and c shrunk toward 0 with k = 3 seasons. The executive-award extension is dropped until its inputs are defined. Units: wins-equivalent score and probability.
raw_data: season-level: team wins, preseason projected wins, prior-year wins, division rank, award votes
mlb.manager_wins_over_expectation.why: Manager of the Year (KXMLBALMOTY, KXMLBNLMOTY, filed here) is a BBWAA vote cast before the postseason that rewards wins over preseason expectation; this is the manager-specific score used in stage s7.

mlb.award_electorate_procedure.label: Award electorate and ballot procedure by award (who votes, ballot depth and points, vote timing, fan-vote component, public ballots)
mlb.award_electorate_procedure.mechanism: Each award is produced by a different electorate with its own ballot, so the vote model, its coefficients and its training data depend on which body votes and how ballots are aggregated.
mlb.award_electorate_procedure.rationale: Verified electorates differ: BBWAA writers vote MVP (10 places, 14-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2-1), Cy Young (5 places, 7-4-3-2-1), Rookie and Manager of the Year (3 places, 5-3-1) before the postseason with public ballots; the Rivera/Hoffman Reliever awards are voted by a panel of about six retired relievers (3 picks, 5-3-1); the BBWAA added its own Relief Pitcher of the Year from 2026 (finalists named Nov 2 2026); Comeback Player is voted by the 30 MLB.com club beat reporters; the Hank Aaron Award combines a Hall of Fame panel with an MLB.com fan vote; Executive of the Year is voted by the 30 clubs before the postseason; Gold Gloves are managers and up to six coaches per club plus the SABR Defensive Index at about 25 percent. Pooling coefficients across these bodies is wrong.
mlb.award_electorate_procedure.measurement: Table keyed by award x league x season with fields: electorate_class in {BBWAA, RETIRED_RELIEVER_PANEL, MLBCOM_BEAT_REPORTERS, HOF_PANEL_PLUS_FANS, CLUB_EXECUTIVES, MANAGERS_COACHES_PLUS_SDI, OTHER}, n_voters, ballot_places, points_vector, vote_deadline relative to the end of the regular season, postseason_included flag, fan_vote flag and published weight (null if unpublished), public_ballots flag, finalist_announcement flag. Source each row from the awarding body's announcement for that season. Use: award_vote_rank_model coefficients are pooled only within one electorate_class; classes without public ballots are fitted on winner and finalist outcomes only (multinomial logit over the finalist set, ridge-shrunk toward the BBWAA coefficients with penalty equal to 3 seasons); the ballot simulation uses that row's n_voters and points_vector. As-of: the row for the season being priced, frozen at the vote deadline.
free_sources: BBWAA voting FAQ and award results (bbwaa.com)
MLB.com press releases for Reliever of the Year, Comeback Player, Hank Aaron Award and Executive of the Year
SABR Defensive Index and Rawlings Gold Glove selection process (sabr.org)
raw_data: award procedure table: award, league, season, electorate_class, n_voters, ballot_places, points_vector, vote_deadline, fan_vote_flag, public_ballots_flag, source_url
mlb.award_electorate_procedure.why: The archetype mixes BBWAA awards with panel, beat-reporter, fan and executive votes; the electorate decides which voter model and which training data apply to each series.

mlb.award_fan_vote_popularity.label: Fan-vote popularity of a candidate for awards with a fan ballot (Hank Aaron Award)
mlb.award_fan_vote_popularity.mechanism: Where fans vote, a candidate's popularity and market size add support beyond the offensive production a panel weighs, so the winner can differ from the statistical leader.
mlb.award_fan_vote_popularity.rationale: The Hank Aaron Award combines a Hall of Fame panel with an online MLB.com fan vote, so a large-market or widely followed slugger gains share that a production model does not see; the relative weight of the two components is not published, so popularity must be estimated from outcomes. The All-Star fan ballot published by MLB is the only public, dated measure of the same fan population's preferences.
mlb.award_fan_vote_popularity.measurement: pop_i = log(All-Star Phase 1 fan votes of player i in the same season, from MLB's published leader updates; 0 for players not listed, with a not-listed flag) + log(team metro population) as a second term. Winner model over the club-nominee finalist set: P(i) = softmax(a1*OPS+_z + a2*HR_z + a3*pop_i + a4*team_playoff_flag), z-scores within league among finalists at the end of the regular season; fit a1-a4 by conditional logit on 2014-2025 winners per league with ridge shrinkage toward a1 = production-only fit (penalty 3 seasons). Units: probability; as-of end of the regular season (voting runs through the postseason, so later fan activity is unobserved).
free_sources: MLB.com All-Star ballot leader announcements (Phase 1 vote updates)
MLB.com Hank Aaron Award finalist and winner releases
FanGraphs or Baseball-Reference season batting (OPS+, HR)
raw_data: All-Star phase-1 vote totals by player and season
Hank Aaron finalists and winners by league and season
mlb.award_fan_vote_popularity.why: KXMLBALHAARON and KXMLBNLHAARON settle on an award partly decided by fans; the panel-only production model misprices popular candidates.

mlb.executive_award_team_improvement.label: Executive of the Year signal: team improvement versus prior season and projection, payroll efficiency and value of the executive's acquisitions, judged by club executives before the postseason
mlb.executive_award_team_improvement.mechanism: Club executives vote before the postseason for the front office that most improved its club relative to expectations and resources, so the signal is the team's regular-season surprise, cost efficiency and the visible results of recent trades and signings.
mlb.executive_award_team_improvement.rationale: MLB's Executive of the Year is voted by the 30 clubs before the postseason (winners since 2018 include Beane, Antonetti, Elias and Arnold twice), with no public ballots, so BBWAA-style ballot models and fan inputs do not apply and the manager score is the wrong object; small-revenue clubs that outperform projections dominate the history.
mlb.executive_award_team_improvement.measurement: For each club's top baseball-operations executive at season end: x1 = regular-season wins - prior-season wins; x2 = wins - preseason projected wins (mean of ZiPS and PECOTA team projections published before opening day); x3 = playoff-berth flag; x4 = z-score of wins per $10M of opening-day payroll; x5 = fWAR produced this season by players acquired by trade or free agency in the prior 12 months minus fWAR of players traded away in that period. P(i) = softmax(b * x) over the 30 executives, b fitted by conditional logit on 2018-2025 winners with ridge shrinkage (penalty 3 seasons) because only 8 winners exist. Units: probability; as-of the last day of the regular season (votes are cast before the postseason, so postseason results are excluded).
free_sources: MLB.com Executive of the Year announcements (mlb.com/awards/executive-of-the-year)
FanGraphs projections and WAR; Baseball-Reference transactions and payroll
raw_data: preseason team projections by system and publish date
transaction log with player fWAR before and after
mlb.executive_award_team_improvement.why: KXMLBEOTY (moved here) settles on the executives' award, which none of the BBWAA, fan or manager inputs measures.

mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.label: League order-statistic engine for best/worst record, 100+ losses, longest losing streak and team strikeouts (simulation method; its inputs are mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_vintage)
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.mechanism: The extreme among thirty teams is determined by each team's talent distribution and the shared schedule.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.rationale: Existing inputs address single games; extremes require a league-wide simulation where each team's outcome is drawn jointly, ties are tracked for $1/N payouts, and streak and strikeout statistics are computed from game-level sequences.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.measurement: Simulate remaining games for 30 teams using team talent posterior (mean, sd) and schedule; record final wins, the longest loss streak per team (run-length of simulated sequence) and team strikeouts (batters faced x team K rate with pitching staff K% projection, sd from game-level variance). Outputs: P(team is unique best), P(tied for best with N teams), expected payout with $1/N rounding; P(wins <= 62 for 100 losses). 20k simulations; calibrate sd to historical. As-of: daily. Units: probabilities.
free_sources: MLB Stats API results and schedule
raw_data: team game logs; remaining schedule; team projections; team K%
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.why: KXMLBTEAMSTAT (team strikeouts leader, stage s8) is a thirty-staff order statistic computed by this engine.

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR_0, SB_0, team games remaining G, per-game play probability from availability and PA per game by lineup slot, set rates r_HR and r_SB per PA = (ROS projection * 250 + season pace * n)/(250 + n) with n = season PA. Simulate 20,000 seasons: PA_rest from game draws with a health hazard; HR_rest ~ NegBin(mean r_HR*PA_rest, dispersion fitted across hitters 2015-2025) and SB_rest ~ NegBin(mean r_SB*PA_rest); couple the two with a Gaussian copula whose rho is the cross-hitter correlation of season HR and SB rate residuals given PA (2015-2025). Output P(HR_0 + HR_rest >= H* and SB_0 + SB_rest >= S*) for contract thresholds. As-of: daily.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.why: Single-hitter season thresholds filed here (50 HR, 50 HR plus 40 SB) are tails of the joint power-speed season distribution (stage s7).

interactions.mechanism: Final total equals current plus rate times games remaining times the probability of playing, so injury hazard and role changes scale the projected increment; for a leader with a small lead and a high injury risk, availability dominates talent differences.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute leader probability with and without injury hazard multipliers; check calibration in late-season leader races.

interactions.mechanism: Rate-stat leaders need the plate-appearance qualification (3.1 PA per scheduled team game for batters), so a borderline hitter's probability of leading a rate category depends on whether he accrues enough PAs; just below the threshold the official shortfall provision still lets him lead if hitless at-bats added up to the minimum leave his rate on top, so the threshold is soft for batters. No equivalent provision is known for the ERA title (1 inning per team game), which stays a hard cut (unverified; contract wording unseen).
interactions.how_to_test: Model qualification as a stopping rule on PA accrual and compare leader probabilities with and without it.

interactions.mechanism: Voters trade off WAR and narrative and team success nonlinearly: beyond a certain WAR gap the narrative matters little, and below it a division title can flip the ranking; the interaction between production gap and team success is not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Plackett-Luce with interaction of WAR gap and team playoff flag and test improvement.

interactions.mechanism: Finalist markets settle on a top-three rank only if finalists are announced before the winner. The rank event and the announcement-timing event are different processes; the interaction of interest is whether announcement timing depends on how tight the field is or on the award's calendar, not their product.
interactions.how_to_test: Test whether the announcement-before-winner indicator varies with field concentration or award type across 2015-2025, rather than assuming independence.

interactions.mechanism: Triple Crown needs one player to lead three correlated stats; the joint probability depends on the covariance of HR and RBI (strongly positive) and AVG (weakly related), so the probability is much larger than an independent product for a power hitter with a big lead but small when AVG is contested. The stated covariances and the 1.5-sd collapse are illustrative and must be estimated.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate stat covariance from historical seasons; compare joint simulation to product of marginals in past races.

interactions.mechanism: A series-MVP or playoff-leader probability is the product of team advancement (games played) and the player's share of production or credit given those games; the same hitter is a long shot if his team is likely to be swept and a favourite if a seven-game series is likely, so team and player components cannot be added.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit series-MVP outcomes 2000-2025 with P(team wins series) x credit share versus additive and share-only baselines and compare log loss.

interactions.mechanism: A staff's strikeout lead depends on who pitches the remaining innings: a deadline acquisition of a high-strikeout starter or the loss of an ace to injury shifts the staff K% for the rest of the season, and the effect on the leader market is large only when the race is close, since a staff ahead by a hundred strikeouts in August is rarely caught.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rest-of-season staff K% before and after deadline moves and test whether leader probabilities updated on roster changes beat a static staff projection.

interactions.mechanism: How strongly WAR drives the outcome depends on who votes: BBWAA writers track WAR closely in MVP and Cy Young voting, the retired-reliever panel weighs saves and leverage innings, and club executives weigh improvement relative to payroll; one pooled coefficient on WAR overstates favourites in the non-writer awards and understates them in the writer awards.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the winner model with WAR coefficients by electorate class versus pooled; compare out-of-sample log loss on 2014-2025 winners for each award family.

interactions.mechanism: Fan popularity matters only where a fan vote exists (Hank Aaron, All-Star) and scales the panel's production-based preference: a popular slugger with similar OPS+ gains a large share, while for writer-only awards the popularity term is zero.
interactions.how_to_test: Add the All-Star fan-vote term to winner models for Hank Aaron versus BBWAA MVP; the coefficient should be positive for Hank Aaron and indistinguishable from zero for MVP.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in lead size: probability of finishing first rises steeply when the lead exceeds one standard deviation of remaining production
nonlinearities.why: Leader probability is a tail event of the difference of two noisy totals; it saturates near one when the lead exceeds the plausible remaining production.

nonlinearities.shape: Qualification threshold at 3.1 PA per scheduled team game with a shortfall exception: a batter just below it can still win a rate title if his rate stays highest after hitless at-bats are added to reach the minimum (official scoring rule, wording for this contract unverified)
nonlinearities.why: The probability is not zero below the threshold: a borderline player with a large rate lead remains a contender, so the PA-shortfall must be modelled rather than a hard cut; the record's hard-zero treatment mis-specifies such candidates.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: marginal vote probability per WAR falls as WAR gap grows
nonlinearities.why: Voters recognise a clear best player; further WAR advantage adds little, but near parity small differences matter.

nonlinearities.shape: Strong shrinkage of early-season totals toward projection, flattening later
nonlinearities.why: Early-season award leaders should be shrunk heavily toward projection because counting production stabilises slowly, and the weight on observed totals rises nonlinearly with games played.
