contract.settlement_definition: Five live series after the reconciliation, all with sampled rules. Postseason league counts: KXMLBWALKOFFS (at least N walk-offs in the 2026 playoffs; 'A walk-off occurs when a game ends with the home team scoring the winning run in the bottom half of the 9th inning or any extra inning', however the run scores) and KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS (at least N home runs by all players in the 2026 playoffs, inside-the-park counted if officially recorded). Player home runs: KXMLBSERIESHR (named player's officially recorded home runs across one playoff series, extra innings and inside-the-park included, other rounds excluded; no start gate) and KXMLBNEXTHR (Yes if the named player 'hits a home run in an MLB game' after one date and before another, No otherwise). Pitcher streak: KXMLBSISTREAK (Yes if the named pitcher reaches N consecutive scoreless innings from the stated streak start until the streak ends or the regular season concludes; partial innings count 1/3 per scoreless out; a broken streak resolves unreached rungs No). No text names a source, and none defines what breaks a streak (earned versus unearned runs, inherited runners) or how a player who misses games settles. Season team extremes, velocity and series exact-score markets moved to season_futures, season_leaders_and_awards, the velocity archetype and the playoff-series archetype.

rules_evidence.quote: A walk-off occurs when a game ends with the home team scoring the winning run in the bottom half of the 9th inning or any extra inning. The run that gives the home team the lead ends the game immediately. The way the run scores does not matter.
rules_evidence.establishes: Any game-ending home-team go-ahead run counts (not only home runs), across the whole postseason.

rules_evidence.quote: an inside-the-park home run counts as a home run, as long as it is officially recorded as such by the Governing League.
rules_evidence.establishes: The playoff HR count follows the official scoring of home runs across all playoff games.

rules_evidence.quote: This market counts the named player's total officially recorded home runs across the entire series, including extra innings and inside-the-park home runs.
rules_evidence.establishes: Series HR total counts every HR in one playoff series with no start or plate-appearance gate, unlike the single-game ladder.

rules_evidence.quote: Home runs from other postseason rounds or the regular season do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: Exposure is the games of one series, a random number between the minimum and maximum series length.

rules_evidence.quote: If Fernando Tatis Jr. hits a home run in an MLB game after May 26, 2026 and before Aug 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: A window market: any MLB game in the window counts, with no team restriction, so a trade does not end exposure but an injury absorbs it.

rules_evidence.quote: each scoreless out counts as 1/3 of an inning toward the total streak
rules_evidence.establishes: Streak length is measured in outs (thirds of an inning), so the rung is a count of consecutive outs without a run.

rules_evidence.quote: If Cristopher Sanchez's consecutive scoreless innings streak is broken, then all markets that have not been achieved yet will resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Rungs are nested: reaching N settles Yes immediately and a run before N settles every higher rung No.

variants_and_edge_cases: Exposure differs by series: walk-offs and playoff home runs count all playoff games; KXMLBSERIESHR counts one series; KXMLBNEXTHR counts every MLB game in a date window (the sampled text does not restrict it to the regular season or one team); KXMLBSISTREAK runs until the streak breaks or the regular season ends.
KXMLBWALKOFFS is titled 'Walk-Off Home Runs' but its rule counts any walk-off ('The way the run scores does not matter'); the rule text governs (see unr_walkoff_title).

KXMLBSISTREAK counts partial innings at 1/3 per scoreless out but does not say whether an unearned run or an inherited runner who scores after the pitcher leaves breaks the streak (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS; postseason innings are excluded, since the text runs the streak only until the regular season concludes, unr_streak_break_definition).

KXMLBSERIESHR has no start gate and no clause for a player who misses series games through injury or benching; KXMLBNEXTHR has no clause for injury, so a player on the injured list simply accrues no exposure and the market resolves No at the window end (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS, unr_serieshr_missed_games).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box scores and game logs (Stats API) for walk-offs, home runs and pitcher outs and runs; the sampled rules name only 'the Governing League'.

mechanism.summary: After the reconciliation this unregistered bucket holds three mechanisms. Postseason league counts (walk-offs, total home runs) are sums over a random number of playoff games: the number of games comes from the bracket and series lengths, each game contributes a walk-off with a probability set by close-late game states and the home team's last at-bat, and home runs per game come from the two lineups, parks and October weather. Player home-run exposure markets (series total, home run inside a date window) are the hitter's per-plate-appearance home-run rate times his plate appearances, where plate appearances depend on how many games the series lasts or how many games fall in the window and whether he plays them; injury acts as an absorbing state and the count is convex in exposure for 2+ rungs. The pitcher scoreless-innings streak is a survival process over outs: each out recorded without a run charged extends the streak by a third of an inning, and the streak ends at the first run charged, so the probability of reaching N innings is a product of per-out survival over the outs still needed, limited by the starts remaining before the season ends. The bucket is handled as three explicit branches, each with its own complete input list attached to the archetype: postseason counts (playoff_walkoff_event_rate, postseason_league_hr_count, bracket_path_enumeration, game_shared_hr_dispersion, run_dist, bullpen), player home-run exposure (series_hr_exposure, series_length_distribution, playoff_games_pa_distribution, hitter_hr_profile, pitcher_hr_vulnerability, hr_environment, window_exposure_schedule, injuries_pit, rehab_progression_stage, expected_pa, playing_time_role) and the scoreless streak (scoreless_streak_survival, pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest, sp_workload, inherited_runner_charge_risk, baserunner_to_run_conversion); inputs of series that left the bucket are audited IRRELEVANT.

stages.name: Contract family classification and gate
stages.description: Five series span postseason league counts, player home-run exposure markets and a pitcher scoreless streak. Routing from the rules text comes first because the exposure window (all playoff games, one series, a date window, or until the streak breaks or the season ends), the counted event (any walk-off despite a home-run title; scoreless outs at one third of an inning) and the nested-rung settlement differ by series and change what is priced.
stages.distribution: Categorical routing; window and event definitions change the payout function, not the underlying process.

stages.name: Postseason event counts over a random number of games
stages.description: Playoff walk-offs and playoff home runs are sums over every playoff game, so their exposure is the number of games, which depends on series lengths and how many rounds are left. Each game produces a walk-off only when the home team is tied or trailing narrowly entering its last at-bat and then takes the lead, which depends on close-game frequency and the visiting closer; home runs per game depend on the two lineups, parks and October weather. Counts so far are known, so late in the playoffs the market is a short remaining-games problem.
stages.distribution: Walk-offs: Poisson-binomial over remaining games (per-game probability a few percent) mixed over the games-remaining distribution; home runs: negative-binomial per game with game-shared dispersion, summed over a random number of games.

stages.name: Player home runs across one playoff series
stages.description: A named hitter's series home-run total is the sum over the series' games of his home runs, so it depends on how many games the series lasts (four to seven in a best-of-seven), whether he starts each one, his plate appearances per game and his per-PA home-run rate against the specific rotation he will face, adjusted for the two parks and October weather. There is no start gate, so a benched or injured hitter accrues fewer chances rather than voiding.
stages.distribution: Compound sum over a random number of games of per-game Poisson-binomial counts; P(2+) is convex in total plate appearances and sensitive to series length.

stages.name: Player home run inside a date window
stages.description: KXMLBNEXTHR pays if the hitter homers in any MLB game inside the window, so the probability is one minus the product over scheduled games of the per-game no-home-run probability, where each game's chance depends on whether he plays, his plate appearances and his per-PA rate. Injury is an absorbing state that ends exposure until his return, so the injured-list status and rehab timeline at the as-of date dominate for a hurt player; a trade keeps exposure because any MLB game counts.
stages.distribution: Survival in games with per-game hazard around 0.10-0.25 for regular power hitters; mixture over an injury state with long absences; right-censored at the window end.

stages.name: Scoreless-innings streak survival
stages.description: From the current streak length, reaching N innings requires 3*(N - current) further consecutive outs with no run charged to the pitcher. Per-out survival comes from his run-prevention profile (strikeouts, walks, home runs and sequencing), the opponents and parks of his next starts, and the chance that runners he leaves on base score after he exits. The number of starts left before the regular season ends caps the outs available, and an injured-list stint pauses exposure.
stages.distribution: Approximately geometric in innings (per-inning scoreless probability around 0.70-0.85 for elite starters), so P(reach N) decays exponentially in outs needed; truncated by remaining starts.

talent_strength.note: Hitter power profile for series and window home runs; pitcher run prevention for the streak.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing rotation HR vulnerability in a series, the visiting closer in walk-off states, lineup-versus-pitcher HR rates per playoff game.

role_personnel.note: Whether the hitter starts the games in his window or series; the pitcher's rotation slot and remaining starts.

availability_news.note: Injury absorbs exposure in the window and series markets and pauses a streak.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager tactics matter only through bullpen deployment in close late games, the hook decision for a streaking starter and lineup choices, all carried by bullpen, inherited-runner and playing-time inputs.

environment.note: Parks and weather of the series games scale per-PA home-run rates.

game_context_script.note: Close-and-late game states that create walk-offs.

pace_volume.note: Playoff games remaining, series length, games in the window and outs per start.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-out probability of avoiding a charged run and conversion of baserunners to runs.

distribution_variance.note: Compound playoff counts, convex series totals and geometric streak survival.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Off days and doubleheaders in the window; starts remaining before season end for the streak.

officiating_rules.note: Umpires do not move these counts at first order; official scoring of inside-the-park home runs and of earned runs is a settlement-definition issue handled under settlement_contract.

settlement_contract.note: Exposure windows, walk-off definition, one-third-inning streak credit and nested rungs.

mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.label: League-wide playoff home-run count: games remaining by bracket path times per-game home-run expectation with game-level dispersion
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.mechanism: Total playoff home runs equal home runs so far plus a sum over the remaining playoff games, each contributing a negative-binomial count driven by the two lineups, the park and weather; the number of remaining games is itself random.
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.rationale: KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS is a threshold on a sum over a random number of games, so most of its variance late in October comes from how many games remain (sweeps versus seven-game series) rather than from per-game HR rates; per-game rates differ by park and cold weather, and games share weather and pitcher-day factors.
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.measurement: H0 = official playoff HR so far. For each remaining game g on each bracket path (probabilities from mlb.bracket_path_enumeration): lambda_g = sum over both teams of projected HR per PA (rest-of-season hitter projections vs the probable starter and bullpen, shrunk to team rate with k = 300 PA) x expected PA (about 38 per team) x park-and-weather factor (mlb.park_specific_xhr deciles). Game count ~ NB(lambda_g, phi) with phi from mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion. P(H0 + sum >= N) by Monte Carlo over paths and series lengths (20k draws). Calibrate total-HR-per-postseason predictions on 2015-2025 postseasons. Units: count and probability. As-of: after each playoff game.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason box scores
raw_data: probable starters and lineups per game
mlb.postseason_league_hr_count.why: Gives KXMLBPLAYOFFHRS a defined input; without it the series had no mechanism after moving into this archetype.

mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.label: Scoreless-streak survival: per-out probability a pitcher records an out with no run charged, and P(reach N innings) from the current streak
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.mechanism: A scoreless streak extends by one third of an inning per out recorded without a run charged to the pitcher and ends at the first charged run, so reaching N is a survival product over the outs still needed.
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.rationale: KXMLBSISTREAK settles on consecutive scoreless innings counted in thirds; elite starters post per-inning scoreless rates near 0.80, so a ten-inning gap has probability around 0.1 and is extremely sensitive to the per-inning rate, opponents, parks and whether runners he leaves on base later score. The contract does not say whether unearned runs break the streak, so both definitions must be computed.
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.measurement: Define the streak in outs. For each future outing j compute, by dynamic programming over the 24 base-out states within each half-inning, the probability S_j(k) of recording k consecutive outs with no run charged to the pitcher (counting all runs, and separately earned runs only). Transition probabilities from the pitcher's projected K%, BB%, HR/PA and BABIP vs the opponent lineup and park, each shrunk to league with k = 300 batters faced. Outs per outing from mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve. P(reach N) = P(streak of N innings completed) summed over the outings remaining before season end by recursion on the carried streak. Add P(inherited runner scores) from bullpen strand rate. Units: probability. As-of: after each outing.
free_sources: Baseball Savant and MLB Stats API play-by-play (free)
raw_data: play-by-play with base-out state and runs charged
pitcher game logs with outs recorded
mlb.scoreless_streak_survival.why: Gives KXMLBSISTREAK its outcome-generating process: per-out survival over the outs still needed within the starts left.

mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.label: Playoff walk-off count: remaining-games exposure and per-game walk-off probability
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.mechanism: A walk-off is a home-team win in the bottom of the 9th or an extra inning; the playoff count is the sum over remaining playoff games of a Bernoulli event whose probability depends on late-inning state, closer quality and who is home.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.rationale: KXMLBWALKOFFS pays on at least N walk-offs across the playoffs (the run that gives the home team the lead ends the game), so it is a count over a random number of games, with the count so far fixed. The per-game probability is not constant: it needs the home team to be tied or trailing by a small margin entering its last at-bat and to score the go-ahead run, and it varies with bullpen quality, extras probability and home-team identity.
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.measurement: Count so far W0 from official game results. Remaining games G are random: enumerate bracket paths and series lengths (best-of-5 or 7) from own per-game win probabilities. For each future game compute p_walkoff = P(home team trails by <=3 or is tied entering the bottom of the 9th and takes the lead before three outs, or wins in an extra inning) from the game run model plus half-inning chain with the visiting closer and due-up slots (walk-off stopping rule), shrunk to the league postseason rate over 2015-2025 with k = 100 games. P(count >= N) = P(W0 + sum Bernoulli(p_g) >= N) integrated over the distribution of G (Poisson-binomial mixture). Units: count and probability. As-of: daily during the playoffs.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason schedule and linescores
raw_data: postseason game log with inning-by-inning score and walk-off flag
mlb.playoff_walkoff_event_rate.why: Postseason-count family: per-game walk-off probability over remaining playoff games for KXMLBWALKOFFS.

mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.label: Postseason bracket-path enumeration: pairing, series length and home-field pattern probabilities
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.mechanism: Matchup, games-hosted and qualifier contracts are functions of which teams reach which round and how long each series lasts.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.rationale: KXMLBMATCHUP and KXMLBPLAYOFFHOST resolve on bracket pairing and on how many games each team hosts, which requires enumerating the fixed bracket (no reseeding within the 12-team format, to be verified) with series-length distributions and home-field patterns, not a title-probability number.
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.measurement: Enumerate all bracket paths from the current seeds or seed probabilities: P(path) = product of series-win probabilities from the team-strength posterior; series length distribution from per-game probabilities with home-field pattern (2-3-2 or 2-2-1-1-1) and shared team-strength draws; games hosted = sum over series of the home games in the realised length. Output P(matchup A vs B in round r) and the distribution of games hosted by a team. As-of: daily.
raw_data: bracket structure and home-field pattern table
series results history for length calibration
mlb.bracket_path_enumeration.why: Postseason-count and series families: number of playoff games remaining by bracket path and series length, the exposure of the walk-off and playoff HR counts.

mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.label: Within-game shared HR environment dispersion (wind/ball/pitcher day latent)
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.mechanism: Home runs by different hitters in the same game share environment and pitcher states, so counts are overdispersed relative to independent Bernoullis.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.rationale: Single-hitter markets need only his marginal, but any multi-hitter or team inference (and the 2+ HR rung) depends on positive dependence; wind blowing out raises everyone's probability together and HR events cluster when a pitcher is lacking command.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.measurement: From 4 seasons of games compute the variance ratio of team-plus-opponent HR counts to the Poisson-binomial expectation given the matchup model, by park roof type and wind-out strength decile; estimate dispersion phi (negative binomial) shrunk to league with k = 100 games. Units: variance inflation. As-of: through prior games. FALLBACK (pre-registered, no matchup model needed): estimate phi first from league-average HR per PA by park, roof type and wind-out decile using plate-appearance counts, then replace expectation with the project's matchup model once it exists; the two-step version avoids circularity.
mlb.game_shared_hr_dispersion.why: Postseason-count family: game-level overdispersion of home runs that widens the playoff HR total distribution.

mlb.series_hr_exposure.label: Series home-run exposure: games played distribution x start probability x per-game HR rate
mlb.series_hr_exposure.mechanism: A series HR total is an aggregation over a random number of games in which the hitter may or may not start.
mlb.series_hr_exposure.rationale: The 2+ HR series rung is dominated by how many games the series goes (4-7) and whether the hitter plays each; the per-game HR probability then compounds. Team playoffs and rest days change both exposure and opposing starters (aces vs fifth starter).
mlb.series_hr_exposure.measurement: N_games ~ distribution from series win-prob model (probability each game, length distribution 4-7 for best-of-7); P(start) per game from role (everyday = 0.95, platoon = 0.55 conditional on opposing starter hand); per-game p_HR from the single-game model with each game's probable starter. Series count distribution = compound sum. Units: expected HR in series. As-of: before each game with updated series state.
raw_data: series state, probable starters, games remaining
mlb.series_hr_exposure.why: Player-exposure family: games, starts and per-game HR rate across one series for KXMLBSERIESHR.

mlb.series_length_distribution.label: Series length distribution (probability of 4/5/6/7 games) from game-level win probabilities with team-strength dependence
mlb.series_length_distribution.mechanism: A series total contract settles on how many games are played, a function of game win probabilities, home-field pattern and the dependence of games on a shared team-strength latent.
mlb.series_length_distribution.rationale: Using independent Bernoulli games understates the probability of sweeps and long series; team strength uncertainty and starter rotation make the sequence dependent, and short series compress the talent gap.
mlb.series_length_distribution.measurement: Simulate best-of-seven: game i win prob p_i from the single-game model with announced starters and rest (default 2-3-2 home pattern), draw team-strength offset ~ N(0, sd = 0.04 in win prob) shared across games, compute P(N=4,5,6,7). P(7 games)=1 - P(<=6). Calibrate sd to historical series length frequency (best-of-7 series since 2012). As-of: after each game with updated series state.
free_sources: Game-level win probability from team model
raw_data: per-game pregame win probability from the project's model
mlb.series_length_distribution.why: Player-exposure family: series length (four to seven games) sets the number of games in KXMLBSERIESHR.

mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.label: Playoff games played and plate-appearance distribution for a named player (for playoff-leader markets)
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.mechanism: A playoff statistical leader needs games played, which depends on the team's bracket survival, and PA per game, which depends on lineup slot.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.rationale: KXMLBLEADERPLAYOFF counts only playoff statistics and resolves No for non-participants, so the leader distribution is a maximum over players of a count over a random number of games; the games-played distribution comes from bracket survival and the PA share from lineup slot and rest.
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.measurement: For each candidate i: G_i distribution from mlb.bracket_path_enumeration (games played by his team). Per game, start probability s_i from last 30 team games lineup share (shrunk to 0.9 for everyday, 0.5 platoon with k = 20 games); PA per start by slot from 2015-2025 postseason PA/game (slots 1-9 observed means); stat (HR, RBI, hits, as stated in the contract) per PA from projection rate shrunk to 3-season rate with k = 300 PA, adjusted by opposing starter. Simulate 20k joint draws of counts over G_i games with game-level shared environment; leader = maximum count among players of teams that played; ties split per contract. Output P(leader) and distribution of counts. Units: probability. As-of: daily during the postseason.
free_sources: MLB Stats API postseason schedule and box scores
raw_data: lineup slot history and start rates
mlb.playoff_games_pa_distribution.why: Player-exposure family: plate appearances per playoff game for the named hitter.

mlb.hitter_hr_profile.label: Hitter HR profile: barrels, fly-ball and pull-air rate, max EV
mlb.hitter_hr_profile.mechanism: HR probability per PA depends on how often a hitter hits fly balls hard and to the pull side.
mlb.hitter_hr_profile.rationale: HR markets are low-probability events per game, so differences in per-PA HR probability and PA count matter greatly. Subtle: pull-air% and barrel% predict HR beyond past HR; park HR factor for the hitter's pull side interacts.
mlb.hitter_hr_profile.measurement: HR/PA from regression on barrel%, pull-air%, FB%, max EV, with shrink to career HR rate; times PA expectation; apply park/hand/weather factors.
free_sources: Baseball Savant / pybaseball statcast (baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search CSV export, leaderboards)
FanGraphs (fangraphs.com leaderboards, splits, projections: Steamer/ZiPS/ATC, park factors, RosterResource) batted-ball leaderboards
mlb.hitter_hr_profile.why: Player-exposure family: the named hitter's per-PA home-run rate for KXMLBSERIESHR and KXMLBNEXTHR.

mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.label: Pitcher HR vulnerability: HR/FB, barrels allowed, fly-ball rate by batter hand
mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.mechanism: Pitchers who allow fly balls and hard contact give up more home runs, and the hitter-pitcher combination determines the single-game probability.
mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.rationale: Pitcher HR rates are noisy; barrel% and fly-ball rate against are more stable. Subtle: pitch type matters (center-cut fastballs, hanging breaking balls) and HR/FB regresses strongly toward league average.
mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.measurement: Pitcher barrel%/FB% allowed by batter hand, HR/FB regressed (prior weight ~200 FB); combine with hitter HR profile via log5 for per-PA HR probability. When used for opposing-hitter markets before first pitch (single-game HR, hits, TB), evaluate it as a mixture over starters: per-PA HR probability = (1 - P(change)) * p(announced starter) + P(change) * sum over replacements r of P(r | change) * p(r), with P(change) and the replacement distribution (next rotation arm, opener plus bulk, bullpen game) from mlb.f5_starter_change_risk at the same as-of time; for the pitcher's own ladders use the announced pitcher only. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Baseball Savant / pybaseball statcast (baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search CSV export, leaderboards)
FanGraphs (fangraphs.com leaderboards, splits, projections: Steamer/ZiPS/ATC, park factors, RosterResource)
mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.why: Player-exposure family: HR vulnerability of the rotation the hitter will face in the series.

mlb.hr_environment.label: Home-run environment: park HR factor by handedness, wind, temperature, ball carry
mlb.hr_environment.mechanism: HR probability on a fly ball depends on park dimensions, wind and air density, so identical batted balls leave the park at different rates.
mlb.hr_environment.rationale: HR markets are rare-event Bernoulli outcomes whose probability scales multiplicatively with environment; a 10% HR-factor shift is a large change in a 10-15% market. Subtle: handedness-specific park HR factors, wind component along the pull-side field and temperature/air density interact with the hitter's pull-air profile.
mlb.hr_environment.measurement: HR factor by batter hand (multi-year regularised) x wind-out component (mph along spray direction) x temperature/humidity coefficient (from fitted HR/FB model); validate against historical HR/FB by park-weather bins; combine with hitter-specific HR probability per PA.
free_sources: FanGraphs (fangraphs.com leaderboards, splits, projections: Steamer/ZiPS/ATC, park factors, RosterResource) park factors by handedness
Baseball Savant / pybaseball statcast (baseballsavant.mlb.com/statcast_search CSV export, leaderboards) (park HR factor by hand, distance/launch)
mlb.hr_environment.why: Player-exposure and postseason-count families: park HR factors of the playoff venues.

mlb.window_exposure_schedule.label: Window exposure: games, off days, doubleheaders and role-probability per game within the window
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.mechanism: A multi-game window aggregates per-game participation probabilities with schedule structure.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.rationale: P(at least one) in a window depends on the number of team games remaining (off days, doubleheaders, postponement) and on the team's usage pattern; a two-way player's pitching is limited by rotation turns.
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.measurement: N = number of team games in the window from the official schedule (adjust for postponement probability from mlb.forecast_precip_timing). Per-game participation p_g: hitters from mlb.playing_time_role start probability, pitchers from mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest P(start on date) plus relief-appearance rate for relievers. P(healthy through g) = (1 - h)^g with per-game injury hazard h from mlb.injuries_pit shrunk to league by age/role (k = 100 player-seasons). P(at least one) = 1 - prod_g (1 - p_g x P(healthy through g)); multiply by (1 - clinched rest factor) from mlb.clinched_rest_policy after the clinch date. Units: probability. As-of: daily.
raw_data: schedule with dates, rotation order, off days
mlb.window_exposure_schedule.why: Player-exposure family: games and role probability per game inside the KXMLBNEXTHR date window.

mlb.injuries_pit.label: Injury/IL and late scratches with point-in-time vintages
mlb.injuries_pit.mechanism: Absences change lineup/rotation composition and late scratches can void or reprice player markets.
mlb.injuries_pit.rationale: Players in the lineup can be scratched after the card posts (warmups injury), and pitchers can be scratched pregame, which resets props. Subtle: vintage timestamps are necessary to avoid look-ahead; IL moves are retroactive and transactions timestamp can differ from news time.
mlb.injuries_pit.measurement: Archive transaction feed (IL placements, call-ups) with timestamps; late-scratch flags from lineup changes between confirmation and first pitch; team-level absence value via projections.
free_sources: FanGraphs (fangraphs.com leaderboards, splits, projections: Steamer/ZiPS/ATC, park factors, RosterResource) RosterResource injuries
mlb.injuries_pit.why: Player-exposure family: injured-list status that absorbs exposure in the window and series markets.

mlb.rehab_progression_stage.label: Rehab progression stage and return-to-pitch/play timeline for injured players
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.mechanism: A returning player must progress through defined rehab steps before appearing, so timing depends on the stage reached.
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.rationale: Window markets such as 'will he pitch before a date' are hazard problems; the information is the rehab stage (throwing program, bullpen sessions, simulated games, minor-league rehab assignment) and the team's stated timetable.
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.measurement: Weibull survival on time from IL placement to activation by injury class (shoulder, elbow, hamstring, other) from MLB transactions 2015-2025, with covariates age, prior IL stays, and a flag for rehab assignment started (time-varying). Stages 0-3 are recorded forward by own capture and enter as covariates only after >=30 observations per class; before that, only rehab-assignment status is used. Class parameters shrunk to the overall Weibull with k = 10 players. P(appear in window) = P(activation before window end | survived to as-of) x P(used within window | active), the latter from the team's last 30 days of relief or start usage for the same role. Units: probability. As-of: latest dated report.
raw_data: IL transactions with dates and injury type
mlb.rehab_progression_stage.why: Player-exposure family: return timeline of an injured hitter inside the KXMLBNEXTHR window.

mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.label: Starting-pitcher rotation slot, days of rest, off-day skipping and announced-probable status
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.mechanism: A pitcher starts when his rotation turn arrives after the club's off days, injuries and bullpen days, and when the announced probable is not replaced.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.rationale: KXMLBSTARTER-type markets depend on the rotation: position in the five-man (or six-man) order, days since the last start, whether the club will skip him around an off day, opener or bullpen-game usage, staff injuries and the probable-pitcher announcement vintage. Hitter lineup-card inputs (platoon, catcher rest, DH rotation) do not describe it.
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.measurement: For each pitcher compute (a) days_rest = game date - last start date, (b) expected next-start date = last start + 5 days adjusted for scheduled off days using the team's last 3 seasons of skip rate on off days (shrunk k = 20 team-off-days), (c) probable-pitcher announcement flag with timestamp and the historical change rate by days-to-game (own capture), (d) opener/bullpen-game rate of the team over the last 30 days. Output P(start on date d) = P(slot lands on d) x P(no change | announced). As-of: announcement time; before announcement the slot-based prior.
free_sources: MLB Stats API schedule hydrate probablePitcher and game logs
raw_data: start log with dates and rest
mlb.pitcher_rotation_slot_and_rest.why: Streak family: remaining starts before the regular season ends cap the outs available to KXMLBSISTREAK.

mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.label: Inherited-runner charge risk after starter exit (expected extra earned runs)
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.mechanism: A starter is charged for runners left on base when relieved, so the bullpen strand rate determines part of his earned runs.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.rationale: The starter's earned-run count is not finished when he leaves: if he leaves with traffic and the reliever allows them to score, those runs are his. Exit-with-traffic probability is high in blow-up outings, the same outings that populate the right tail of the ER ladder.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.measurement: P(exit with k runners) from the shared exit hazard mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve evaluated inside the PA simulation x P(each inherited runner scores | reliever profile) with reliever strand rate shrunk to league (k = 60 BF with inherited runners). Expected extra ER = sum_k P(k) x k x p_score x (1-unearned share). Use the likely first reliever from bullpen availability (setup man or long man). Units: expected earned runs added. As-of: lineup post + bullpen usage from prior 2 days.
raw_data: relief-appearance level: inherited runners, inherited scored, reliever, team, game state
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.why: Streak family: runners left on base who score after the streaking pitcher exits are charged to him and break the streak.

mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.label: Run-expectancy conversion of baserunners (RE24-allowed by base-out state, pitcher profile)
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.mechanism: Earned runs equal the sum of run-value increments across base-out states; HR and extra-base hits convert traffic to runs.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.rationale: LOB% regression treats strand rate as luck, but strand rate partly reflects pitcher skill (K and GB with runners on) and HR timing. A direct PA-level run-expectancy accounting separates how many baserunners a pitcher allows from how many each is worth.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.measurement: For each pitcher, estimate PA outcome probabilities (K, BB/HBP, GB-DP, HR, other) separately in 8 groups (bases empty, then runners on with 0, 1, 2 outs for runner on 1B only vs scoring position) over the last 2 seasons with 400-BF half-life weights, shrunk to the league group rate with k = 250 BF in that group. Expected earned runs for the target game = Markov-chain simulation (10,000 games) over the confirmed batting order using these state-dependent pitcher outcomes combined by log5 with batter rates and the park, minus the unearned share from mlb.er_ur_scoring_split; also report RE24 allowed per PA by group (RE24 after minus before plus runs on play, season league matrices). Units: expected runs charged to the starter over his expected batters faced. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Statcast events with runners on base and outs
raw_data: event-level: base-out state before, event, runs on play, batter, pitcher, park
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.why: Streak family: base-out run conversion against the pitcher sets per-out scoreless survival.

mlb.expected_pa.reason: Plate appearances per game set a hitter's per-game home-run chance in the date-window and series markets (KXMLBNEXTHR, KXMLBSERIESHR), which multiply it over games. The catalog definition conditions PA on an implied team total; for window and series exposure use projected team runs per game, not market totals (BENCHMARK_ONLY).

mlb.plate_discipline.reason: Walk propensity of opposing lineups enters the streak's per-inning scoreless probability only through the pitcher's projected BB%, which the streak input already carries; no remaining series counts walks.

mlb.sb_context.reason: Pitcher hold time and catcher pop time served KXMLBSB, now in hitter_rbis_runs_sb; no remaining series here involves stolen bases.

mlb.baserunning.reason: Runner attempt and success served the steal ladder (moved) and the 50/40 threshold (moved to season_leaders_and_awards); irrelevant to the remaining series.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Outs per start determine how fast a scoreless streak can accumulate outs before the season ends; it is the exposure term in the streak survival product.

mlb.leash.reason: Hook tendency affects how long a streaking starter stays in and whether he leaves runners for the bullpen, but sp_workload and inherited_runner_charge_risk carry those effects with defined estimands.

mlb.run_dist.reason: Supplies the frequency of tied or one-run games entering the bottom of the ninth for the walk-off count and per-game run environment; not the right object for the player or streak markets.

mlb.bullpen.reason: The visiting closer's availability and quality decide walk-off conversion, and the relievers who inherit a streaking starter's runners decide whether those runs are charged to him.

mlb.lineup_pit.reason: Daily lineup cards confirm whether a window or series hitter plays a given game; useful as an as-of update, but exposure over many games is driven by role and injury.

mlb.playing_time_role.reason: Whether the named hitter starts each game in his window or series sets exposure for KXMLBNEXTHR and KXMLBSERIESHR, neither of which has a start gate.

mlb.umpire.reason: Zone effects shift walk and strikeout rates and so a streaking pitcher's per-inning scoreless probability slightly, but the per-start opponent and park effects dominate and no remaining series has first-order umpire dependence.

mlb.pa_sim.reason: A simulation method, not an input; usable as the per-game engine behind walk-off and HR counts but not staged.

mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.reason: Served best/worst record, 100-loss, losing-streak and team-strikeout series, now filed in season_futures and season_leaders_and_awards (attached there); no remaining series here uses it.

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.reason: Served the single-hitter 50/40 and 50/50 thresholds, now in season_leaders_and_awards and the KXMLBSTAT branch of pitch_velocity_extremes (attached there).

mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.reason: Served the velocity markets, now in the pitch_velocity_extremes archetype, which audits it as its primary engine; no remaining series here involves pitch speed.

mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.reason: Served series exact-score markets, now in playoff_series_markets, which already carries it; no remaining series here is a series score.

mlb.longest_streak_extreme_value.reason: Served the longest winning streak series (KXMLBWSTREAK), now filed in season_futures (attached there); no remaining series here is a team streak.

mlb.lockout_games_lost_scenario.reason: Served the games-played-in-a-season series, now in labour_stoppage_and_season_schedule (attached there) and season_futures; no remaining series here depends on a stoppage.

mlb.league_team_talent_posteriors_with_v.reason: Feeds the team-season order-statistic engine for season_futures series (attached there); no remaining series here is a thirty-team race.

interactions.mechanism: Walk-offs need games, and only games that reach the home team's last at-bat tied or narrowly behind; the count is therefore games remaining (set by bracket path and series length) times a per-game rate that rises with evenly matched, low-scoring pairings. A long series between two strong pitching staffs raises both factors at once, so the two cannot be estimated separately.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress postseason walk-offs per game on pre-game total and win-probability gap, and compare count calibration with and without path-dependent games remaining.

interactions.mechanism: The playoff HR total is a compound sum: its variance is the variance of the number of games times the squared per-game mean plus the per-game dispersion times the expected games. Early in October the games-remaining term dominates and the threshold probability moves in steps with each series result; late, per-game park and weather matter more.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose the variance of simulated playoff HR totals into games-count and per-game parts by date and compare with realised totals 2015-2025.

interactions.mechanism: A 2+ series home-run rung needs two events, so its probability rises faster than linearly in total plate appearances: a series that goes seven games instead of four nearly doubles a hitter's chances for 1+ but more than triples them for 2+, and the effect is larger for high per-PA power rates.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised series home-run rungs against a linear-in-games model, split by series length and hitter power tier.

interactions.mechanism: In the date-window market a healthy power hitter's probability saturates quickly (he usually homers within a few weeks), so almost all uncertainty is the injury state: a hitter on the injured list with an uncertain return has a probability governed by return timing, not power.
interactions.how_to_test: Split historical windows by injured-list status at the as-of date and compare realised hit rates with the power-only model.

interactions.mechanism: A streak can only reach N if enough starts remain to record the needed outs: late in the season the rung becomes impossible once remaining starts times outs per start falls below the gap, regardless of how dominant the pitcher is.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the maximum attainable streak from remaining starts and check that market rungs beyond it settle No.

interactions.mechanism: Runners a streaking pitcher leaves on base and who later score are charged to him and, if the streak counts all charged runs, break it; managers protecting a streak pull him with bases empty, so the bullpen and exit-state policy change survival late in starts.
interactions.how_to_test: In historical long streaks, compare the share of streak-ending runs scored by inherited runners with the share expected from typical exit states.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function in time as series end; convex in games remaining for a 5+ threshold
nonlinearities.why: A threshold of several walk-offs needs many close games; each finished series removes potential games in a step, and the probability of reaching N rises faster than linearly with remaining games because several rare events must coincide.

nonlinearities.shape: exponential decay in outs needed
nonlinearities.why: Each inning survives with probability q, so P(reach N) is about q to the power of the innings needed; a change in q from 0.78 to 0.82 nearly doubles the chance of a ten-inning gap.

nonlinearities.shape: convex in plate appearances for 2+ rungs
nonlinearities.why: Two home runs are needed, so the rung grows roughly with the square of exposure at low rates; series length and benching change it more than proportionally.
